GENERAL SPECIFICATIONS In conventional electrical systems, functions are activated with the aid of dedicated point-to-point lines The increase in the number of electrical/electronic devices on board new cars has given rise to heavier and more complex connections. This is partly due to the complexity of the functions implemented in the burgeoning number of electronic units - which also need to exchange data continually: all this makes new electrical systems more difficult to install and increases the complexity of fault diagnosis. Many problems have been overcome and new electrical systems have been optimised compared to conventional systems by using a network form of connection. This provides a more effective means of managing communication on the board the car and of transferring data between the various subsystems. Information is distributed via serial pathways (buses) that may take the form of: individual wires, twisted wire pairs or even optical fibres. Conventional solution The three control units (electronic nodes) require a number (N) of wires for each input/output data item in order to perform their function. This multiplied the amount of cable required to the point that systems are made more complex (design and manufacture) and more voluminous (weight, bulk, cost). Some 40 kg of wiring looms are required that stretch for more than 2 km - and this figure could double every 10 years because even now a car could be equipped with 20 to 40 electronic control units (ECUs). Tx - information to be transmitted from nodes A (A1,A2) B (B1, B2) C (C1, C2) Rx - information to be received from nodes A (B1, B2, C1) B (A1, A2, C2) C (A2, B1, B2) The first step towards reducing the volume and complexity of wiring looms was to group several electronic functions in a single unit: fewer control units = fewer wires. Examples of integation The engine management control unit (NCM) manages: injection, ignition, pollution system, engine cooling control etc. 1 - Engine management control unit 2 - Engine cooling fan, 1st speed 3 - Engine cooling fan, 2nd speed 4 - Injectors (injection) 5 - Coils (ignition) 6 - Lambda sensor Integration of electrical/electronic functions in a single electronic control unit (ECU) has allowed us to improve: current uptake management (lower battery wear); the operation of appliances, because they are managed by a single control unit; troubleshootng due to self-diagnostic functions in the control units. This first stage allowed us to reduce the number of electronic units but not to reduce the volume of wiring to a sufficient extent. MULTIPLEXING solution This involves exchanging various data signals between various ECUs on a single transmission channel (a principle already used for phone, radio and TV networks): 1 BUS (2 wires) for all data. The second stage allowed us to make a decise leap in terms of: Reducing and simplifying the wiring Reducing the number of sensors (information sharing) Allowing ECUs to communicate among themselves. As more and more systems require interconnection, the MULTIPLEXING solution becomes more and more attractive. In general terms, in order to transmit data via a multiplexing system we need to define the following with precision: transmission channel (wires, optical fibres, radio waves etc.); type of signal sent via the channel (voltage, current, light etc.); the communication protocol (all the rules that allow management of analogue or digital transmission type, code type, address, transmission order, error detection etc.). transmission channel (wires, optical fibres, radio waves etc.); type of signal sent via the channel (voltage, current, light etc.); the communication protocol (all the rules that allow management of analogue or digital transmission type, code type, address, transmission order, error detection etc.). transmission channel (wires, optical fibres, radio waves etc.); type of signal sent via the channel (voltage, current, light etc.); the communication protocol (all the rules that allow management of analogue or digital transmission type, code type, address, transmission order, error detection etc.). The transmission support or channel on the car is a pair of wires known as a BUS. The system therefore transmits batches (packages of information sent one after another. This is not done in any particular set order but in accordance with the needs of the control unit). The following protocols are used for the voltage signals produced; CAN protocol (Controller Area Network): used for the high speed transfer of data (engine management, ABS, automatic transmission) initiated and developed by Robert Bosch as early as 1983, VAN protocol: used for managing standard bodywork functions. Binary The language of the electronic units is binary - compatible with the electronic circuits (high low) (open closed etc.): to transmit information, data must therefore be handled in accordance with specific codes. Various codes have therefore been developed to meet all requirements. One of the most common codes is ASCII (American Standard Code for Information Interchange). This alphanumerical code uses coded groups of bits. It is able to represent the 26 letters of the English alphabet plus the ten decimal numbers in addition to punctuation marks and instruction commands. ASCII is an eight bit binary code. Seven bits are used to code information and the eighth is used to check errors. By using seven bits per character, it is posible to code no fewer than 128 pieces of information including decimal numbers, upper and lower case letters of the alphabet, punctuation marks etc. Once the number of bits making up a word (i.e. the word length) has been fixed by a data code, this number must not be altered. A group of eight bits is called a byte and represents 256 values: this number is obtained by testing all possible combinations of (0) and (1) in the eight positions availalbe per byte, for example 00000001, 00001111, 11111111 etc. The number 256 (2 exp. 8) can be used to represent the set of alphabetical characters, punctuation marks, accented or special characters etc. In effect, therefore, a single byte may represent a number, a letter of the alphabet, a punctuation mark or a special character. The byte is used as a unit of measurement in saved data quantities and memory device storage capacity. As with any unit of measurement, bytes are also defined as multiple amounts: 1 kilobyte (kb) = 1024 bytes = 2 exp. 10 (210) 1 megabyte (Mb) = 1024 kb (about one million bytes) = 2 exp. 20 (220) 1 gigabyte (Mb) = 1024 kb (about one billion bytes) = 2 exp. 30 (230) 1 terabyte (Mb) = 1024 Gb (about one trillion bytes) = 2 exp. 40 (240) 1 kilobyte (kb) = 1024 bytes = 2 exp. 10 (210) 1 megabyte (Mb) = 1024 kb (about one million bytes) = 2 exp. 20 (220) 1 gigabyte (Mb) = 1024 kb (about one billion bytes) = 2 exp. 30 (230) 1 terabyte (Mb) = 1024 Gb (about one trillion bytes) = 2 exp. 40 (240) 1 kilobyte (kb) = 1024 bytes = 2 exp. 10 (210) 1 megabyte (Mb) = 1024 kb (about one million bytes) = 2 exp. 20 (220) 1 gigabyte (Mb) = 1024 kb (about one billion bytes) = 2 exp. 30 (230) 1 terabyte (Mb) = 1024 Gb (about one trillion bytes) = 2 exp. 40 (240) Analogue "Linear" electronics is the term applied to analogue effects, i.e. effects that are proportional and continuous. A water tap is an example of an analogue switch. This is because it can used to shut off the water flow completely, turn the flow to maximum and also obtain all the other intermediate positions that occur between the closed state and the fully open state. The Tester mobile coil instrument is also analogue: the pointer may indicate the measurement position from zero to full scale deflection, by moving continuously along the entire graduated scale and passing through all the points on its way. Digital Digital electronic, on the other hand, denotes progress by discrete quantities in quantifiable steps. A light switch is an example of digital operation because the only possible statuses are well-defined and distinct. In this case there are two: on and off, with no intermediate positions. In practice, a digital gauge (whether it operates using warning lights or numbers) increases in steps. It is not possible to determine, for example, the exact level of a fluid between a stage when one warning light on the level gauge is lit and the next is still turned off. The sensitivity is therefore one step, i.e. the interval between one warning light and the next. The reading is, however, precise and non-subjective. It is possible to interpose a series of steps between one warning light and the next containing an equal number of warning lights and so on until the discrete measurement steps can practically be equated with the continuous line of an analogue instrument. The similarity is, however, more apparent than real because each step on the digital gauge, however small, determines a well-defined position and represents an unequivocable value. Above all, it is not subject to parallalax or interpolation reading errors. To sum up, the sensitivity of a digital instrument is equivalent to that of an analogue instrument but the reading accuracy is always higher. OPERATION OF MULTIPLEXING NETWORK The designer of the multiplex system allocated control functions to the Body Computer. The additional Body Computer functions allow it to provide information on: network activities status, operational failure status of individual electronic units (nodes), a possible network fault. The Body Computer Node is given the task of "waking up" the network when the ignition key is turned on. In the case of a fault in the NBC, the Instrument Panel Node (NQS) is given the task of waking up the network. The NQS cuts in only if it is not woken up by the Body Computer after a certain length of time with the ignition key. This prevents network conflicts. All the "Node" electronic units process the various signals from associated sensors for individual management purposes and also to manage other control units. On latest-generation electrical systems, the number of electronic unit that are interconnected, and thus the number of data packages that need to be handled, is very high. For this reason, one or more CAN networks are used in these systems. Compared to conventional wiring, these allow more effective information exchange between the various electronic units. The physical means used for the CAN is a twin plaited copper wire cable; where one of the wires is for high voltage and the other low voltage. The BUS signals are differential, i.e. the value allocated to the bits is represented by the difference between voltage levels. To sum up, the combined use of two wires and differential signals allow data packages to be exchanged between different control units on the network. This is even possible in the presence of electromagnetic interference. The message issued to a network by an electronic unit or node is known as a "raster" (data package). It takes the form of a series of pulses, as mentioned previously (known as bits) that take the value (1) or (0). This denotes the presence of absence of a transmitted signal. Communication protocol Circulation or transmission of a message known as a frame or data package on a multiplexing network is possible only if a transmission protocol is adopted. This the set of rules that allows the exchange of data and controls between two or more electronic units (control units or, better still, nodes). 1 - Frame 2 - Blocks A - Identifies the beginning of transmission or start of a new frame (START OF FRAME. SOF) consists of 1 dominant bit and indicates to all other interfaced nodes that they must synchronise with this SOF bit (awake the BUS that may be in stand by). B - Identifier (12 bits): marks and identifies the contents of the message. Also contains information on message recipients. Arbitrage of transmitted frames is carried out in this field. This means that the indentifier code allows frame content and priority allocated by the network architect to be uniquely identified. C - Control range (4 bits); indicates the nature of the frame or message and makes it possible to indicate whether the frame is a question, a response or data diffusion. At the same time it indicates whether it is necessary for the frame recipient to communicate that the frame has been correctly received. D - Data to be trasmitted (may be orders or information to be transmitted): for the VAN it can be between 0 and 28 bytes (1 byte = 8 bits), whilst for the CAN it can be between 0 and 8 bytes. E - Control field; allows a check to be run that the data transmitted are unaltered (message validity). The node or nodes that detect the presence of an error first issue a series of dominant warning bits. The transmitting node eliminates the message and emits a new frame after a certain time lapse. F- Reception confirmation. This allows all the destination nodes to indicate that the frame has been correctly transmitted. For messages transmitted via the VAN, confirmation of receipt is optional, whilst for frames transmitted via the CAN it is compulsory. G - End of frame: determines the end of the message with no ambiguity. Bus communication rules The two types of nodes There are two different types of nodes: Master Node: issues frames to send or receive information, receives frames sent directly to its address or diffused over the network without a particular destination; Slave Node: receives frames and only issues them if interrogated directly In the following type of network: Master / Slave, the management of the information is entrusted solely to the Master Node, In the following type of network: Multi Master, the management of the information is not concentrated at a single Node, but they are all authorized to circulate messages. In a mixed type of network: different Master Nodes with Slave Nodes, the information is managed by the Master nodes. Priority management (Superimposition or collision of non-destructive frame) The system protocol allows superimposition problems to be handled when several nodes need to emit a frame simultaneously. Each node possesses an identification code that also expresses its priority. In practice, when a node expresses its intention to transmit a frame on the network by means of its initial bit and another node simultaneously carries out the same operation, because both read (as well as transmit) the signals emitted by the network, the node that detects a difference between the emitted signal and the received signal detects that another node is emitting a higher priority frame. The node that transmits the lower priority message immediately interrupts its transmission and makes way for the node that is transmitting a higher priority message. In practice, the high priority message is sent to the network without any interruption or delay. Naturally, the nodes that intended to transmit messages with lower priority must suspend transmission to become receivers and then re-attempt to send the frame when transmission is complete. This non-destructive superimposition is regulated by bit arbitrage. One bit is called the dominant bit and allocated a value of zero (0) while the other bit is known as a recessive bit and its value is equal to one (1). The higher priority frame gains the right to be transmitted on the BUS. A dominant level (0) always takes precedence over a recessive level (1). Types of information interchange Communication between the various nodes can be: point to point: sending the data involves a precise destination, diffused: the data transmitted does not have a precise destination question / response: the answer may be provided directly within the question frame or in a different frame dedicated to the response. with the confirmation of receipt: the node that receives the frame completes the actual frame on receipt. Structure of the network The physical medium used for automotive networks is double copper electrical cable type, where one wire is associated with a higher voltage level than the other. In order to transfer and receive information, all electrical/electronic units are connected to the network by means of switching interfaces built into the electronic units that are known as transceivers. The electronic units in the networks are programmed and operate by means of data and information storage, processing and transmission using a binary convention, i.e. two symbols that denote two basic electrical logic statuses. absence of voltage, circuit open or level zero (0) presence of voltage; circult closed; or level one (1). Levels (0) and (1) constitute the basic information unit known as a BIT (binary digit). STRUCTURE The system interacts with all electrical system functions to directly control body functions (visibility, access, on-board information, comfort, communications etc.) and supports information exchange between traction control systems (engine, braking, gearbox etc.). Power is distributed via the junction units and/or fuse boxes. These are connected to control elements (relays and static actuators) to ensure maximum electrical protection and minimum complexity. Systems of this type offer innumerable benenfits, for example: sensors included in the various subsystems are available to the network; information may be shared; sensor duplication is eliminated; system flexibility is increased; new functions may be added simply by changing the software (developments throughout the car's lifetime), wiring design is simplified and the number of connectors reduced, the operational safety of electronic devices is increased to improve the reliability of information transmitted, because a diagnostic function is built-in, service operations on electric/electronic components are easier. Network architecture The structure consists of three communication networks which connect nodes belonging to the different areas (vehicle dynamic control and bodywork functions) and a certain number of complementary serial lines used for diagnosis and other specific functions: a multi-master type CAN for the dynamic control of the vehicle (high speed), a multi-master type CAN known as a COMFORT network which connects the NBC to the information or comfort equipment. a master/slave type CAN also known as the BODYWORK network: CAR. INTRODUCTION Il Nodo Body Computer (NBC) è un componente elettronico costituito da una base hardware e da un'interfaccia software - hardware (ILM). Il NBC garantisce le seguenti funzioni: le funzioni di Carrozzeria (illuminazione, visibilità, memorizzazione, protezione dell'abitacolo, ...) una parte delle funzioni di erogazione e di protezione delle alimentazioni elettriche dei componenti dell'abitacolo. la funzione di interscambio delle informazioni tra le reti CAN e VAN. la funzione di interfaccia con la linea di diagnosi per le funzioni d'allarme, climatizzazione, airbag, le pulsantiere di comando sulle porte, lo schermo, l'autoradio, il CDC, il navigatore, il radiotelefono, il NQS ed il FAP (i nodi su rete VAN non sono collegati alla presa di Diagnosi). La funzione di erogazione e di protezione delle alimentazioni può essere di 3 tipi: uscite a relè e protette (semplici o mezzo ponte) uscite protette uscite a transistor (smartpower) Relay protected components Simple outlet: Outlets FUNCTIONS 1 rear fog lamp 2 left front, left rear, trailer light 3 right front, right rear, no. plate light, buttons 4 heated rear windscreen 5 rear windscreen wiper 6 +van-car1 +van-car2 7 +van-CONFORT Outlet by means of bridge: OUTLETS FUNCTIONS 1 locking 2 unlocking 3 superlocking Components protected by fuses OUTLETS FUNCTIONS 1 ignition key at "ACC" 2 ignition key at "MAR" 3 diesel additive 4 diagnostic socket 5 child locks 6 alarm, radio, telephone, display, climate control, navigator, steering wheel node 7 sun roof 8 front electric windows 9 rear electric windows 10 Brake light Components controlled by transistor (smartpower) OUTLETS FUNCTIONS 1 bonnet release 2 left direction indicators 3 right direction indicators 4 bonnet light 5 underdashboard light 6 running board light 7 courtesy lights 8 evaporator compressor The NBC interfaces with the other vehicle nodes by means of four networks: a multi-master type CAN known as an intersystems network (I.S.) which connects the NBC to the nodes which supervise the mechanics in general (engine management, ABS, information for the driver, etc.), a multi-master type VAN known as a COMFORT network which connects the NBC to the information or comfort equipment, a master/slave type VAN divided into two sub sectors also known as BODYWORK networks: the VAN CAR1 groups together the steering column switch unit/AIR BAG module functions; the VAN CAR2 is dedicated to the management of Safety functions (Alarm), the opening devices (Sun Roof Node, Sliding Door Node), the FAP (NAD), the Steering Position Node and the Driver's Door Node (NPG) and Passenger Door Node (NPP). The NBC is also connected to some sensors and actuators and to the diagnostic socket. NBC ROLE AND FUNCTIONS The NBC carries out the following processing: it manages the system operating state, it carries out the application programme, it saves data, it loads codes and manages the diagnostic line, it guarantees time management (timer and delays), it converses via the VAN and CAN it acquires direct inputs, it operates the direct outlets (except the networks), it operates the system status LED, it allows the diagnosis of some direct outlets, it provides power supplies, it detects a fault in the direction indicator, it measures the engine oil level. NBC VERSIONS The are 3 possible different NBC configurations. In the low range configuration the NBC implements the following functions: front electric windows, heated seats, automatic climate control with air temperature and solar sensor, central locking for the doors, rear windscreen wiper. In the mid-range configuration the NBC implements the following functions: automatic climate control with air temperature and solar sensor, front running board light (under the door), front electric windows, rear electric windows, electric child locks, heated seats, central locking for the doors, rear windscreen wiper In the top of the range configuration the NBC implements the following functions: rain sensor information management, automatic switching on of the lights, automatic climate control with air temperature and solar sensor, front running board light (under the door), front electric windows, rear electric windows, electric child locks, heated seats, super locking, rear windscreen wiper OPERATING MODES There are four operating modes for the NBC: "system inactive" mode - supply below 5 volt with all the outlets in stand-by state, "system stand-by" mode: if the ignition key is not in the ON position or it is at "ACC" after the delay for the stand-by for the VAN and deactivation of the NBC. "system activated" mode in which all the functions are activated. "system being activated" mode which corresponds to the initialization of the software which takes place during the activation of the NBC. ACTIVATION There are three different causes of activation: activation via bus: by means of direct inputs (door opening remote control, hazard warning lights button, headlamp flasher, manual sliding side door), activatation by means of key at "ACC" or key at "MAR", activation by means of direct inputs: door unlocking, door opening (when the vehicle is unlocked) action of bonnet release button, courtesy lights on button, locking button, tailgate contact closure, no fuel tank cap. FORCED SWITCHING OFF/ON OF LOADS The NBC is equipped with a control function for the electrical loads to prevent overloading (deactivation of electrical consumers) or to force the engagement of the alternator (activation of electrical consumers). Forced deactivation of electric loads The load deactivation function is designed to prevent the battery from being run down or even ruined through the application of temporary current interruptions. The NBC intervention levels are as follows: level 0: no deactivation level 1: interruption of heater plugs power supply (if supplied for the function of the artificial regeneration of the particle filter), level 2: interruption of engie cooling fan power supply, at medium speed (if supplied for the function of the artificial regeneration of the particle filter), level 3: interruption of engie cooling fan power supply, at low speed (if supplied for the function of the artificial regeneration of the particle filter), level 4: interruption of the heated rear windscreen power supply (if supplied for the function of the artificial regeneration of the particle filter), level 5: interruption of the heated rear windscreen power supply (if the activation time is > 6 mins) if authorized by the Climate Control Node, level 6: reduction in the climate control fan speed (with automatic type climate control), level 7: interruption of the compressor power supply (with automatic type climate control). With a manually operated climate control system, the compressor is not switched off because the NBC does not recognize the climate control fan rotation speed. Forced activation of electric loads The forced activation of certain electrical loads required by the Engine Management Node for the regeneration of the particle filter does not take priority. The forced activation levels are as follows: level 0: no forced activation, level 1: heated rear windscreen power supply, level 2: engine cooling fan, low speed, power supply, level 3: engine cooling fan, medium speed, power supply, level 4: heater plugs power supply. NBC diagnostics The fault diagnosis of the NBC makes it possible to be aware of the input and output states. It also allows certain outputs to be operated (actuator test). The fault memory This is a memory that makes it possible to display the appearance and disappearance of every fault memorized. Each fault detected is stored in the memory and classified according to the order in which it appears at the corresponding mileage. The mileage recorded goes up to 65535 km. Beyond this, the recording is made in modules of 65535, e.g.: 11659 ( 2 x 65535 + 11659) will be displayed for 142749 km. When the allocated memory is full, the recording works on a rotation principle: the new faults will be superimposed on the old ones.

INTRODUCTION The engine compartment node is located on the right side of the actual engine compartment (near the windscreen washer fluid reservoir). NDVM FUNCTION The NDVM has the task of distributing the power supplies via: Relays. Fuses. Mini fuses. Maxi fuses. housed in it. The NDVM comprises 2 modules (1 and 2) and guarantees the following functions: Distribution and protection of the main power supply lines and different functions Protection of the engine function power supply lines Communcation via the VAN CAR 1 network Interconnection Switching and protection of different functions: Main relay (powerlatch) and engine management power, fuel pump interruption, climate control vent, horn, main/dipped beam headlamps, fog lights, front/rear screen washers, headlamp washer, front windscreen wiper Rereading outputs Sensor signal recording. The battery lead is fastened at module 1 of the NDVM (power module) which has the task of distributing the +BATT power supplies to the various components in the engine compartment (NDVM module 2, NFR, alternator) and in the passenger compartment (anti-theft devide, NBC). Starting from the positive battery lead, module 1 guarantees: distribution and protection via the maxi fuse for the +BATT electrical power supplies to the components connected via the main wiring, the electrical power supply (+BAT Power) for module 2, the electrical interconnection between the battery lead and the alternator/starter motor/spark plugs connection. Starting from the +BATT supplied by module 1 and the anti-theft enablement, module 2 guarantees the distribution, protection and interupption of the power supply (via relays) for the components connected by means of the main and engine wiring. A - module 1 B - module 2 Distribution of the power supplies by fuse, with ignition at MAR for module 2: The NDVM is supplied with the ignition ON. The following components are supplied with the ignition ON, by fuse, by the NDVM: NCA, reversing switch/reversing light, (NCM, NFR), water in diesel sensor (for diesel engines), Preheating node (for diesel engines), air flow meter (for diesel engines), speed sensor (for petrol engines), gas discharge headlamps, Engine cooling fan assembly relay, engine coolant level (for diesel engines) Distribution of power supplies by fuse for module 2: Additive Control Node (for diesel engines), Additive injector (for diesel engines), Distribution of power supplies by relay and fuse for module 2: NCM, Left/right dipped headlamps, Left/right main beam headlamps, Fog lights, Front windscreen wiper, Front/rear windscreen washer pump, Headlamp washer pump, Signal, Additional vents, NCM actuators/sensors, NCM, Fuel pump, Air pump (for petrol engines), Ignition coil (for petrol engines), Injectors (for petrol engines), EGR solenoid valve (for petrol engines), Lambda sensor (for petrol engines), EGR solenoid valve, Turbo pressure regulator solenoid valve (waste gate) (for diesel engines) Diesel heater (for diesel engines), Powerlatch and power electrical supply for engine management system: In the case of an impact, the NBC requests the NDVM to cut off the fuel pump supply via the VAN CAR network. The NDVM cuts off the "power activator" electrical supply for the fuel pump. Operating procedure There are 4 operating modes for the NDVM electronics: "system inactive or standy" mode: with +15 or +VAN power supplies below 5.5 V. powerlatch mode: +15 and +VAN power supplies below 5.5V and the main relay controlled by the engine management control unit. "system reactivated" mode: all the functions are active. Effective communication on the VAN multiplex network. emergency mode if there is no VAN communication. Vehicle mileage management The instrument panel saves the data relating to the mileage travelled: at least once every 5 kilometres, when "stand-by within 5 seconds" information is received, or when the ignition is turned off, or if the trip meter zeroing button is pressed (transmitted from the NSO). The following strategies are implemented to guarantee the milometer figures if the NBC or the NQS is replaced: if the value memorized in the NQS is below or equal to the value memorized in the NBC, the NQS adapts to the basic value memorized in the NBC, if the value memorized in the NQS is higher than the value memorized in the NBC, the NQS maintains the value memorized. The milometer can be completely zeroed (reset) if the mileage is below 250 km (or 250 miles). This zeroing can only be done once. In the case of a fault: if there is a network error or an invalid figure is received, the instrument panel does not make the comparison. NQS lighting LIGHTING DIMMER CONTROL The lighting for the panels and the displays is the dimmer type. The lighting level for the instrument panel is defined by a table with 16 values memorized in an EEPROM regulated in such a way that the lighting is in line between the two extreme brightness values. If there is a fault: if there is a network error, the instrument panel lighting takes place at the standard value. Self-diagnosis The instrument panel carries out an autodiagnosis on its operation and the components connected to it for which it guarantees operation. All the problems which occur during operation are memorized and made available to be read and deleted using the diagnostic equipment. INTRODUCTION The NVO module is an interface that retransmits the actions carried out by the user by means of the steering column switch unit controls. The NVO communicates with the NBC via the VAN CAR 1, but the processing remains the responsibility of the NBC which is the true heart of the system. The steering column switch unit module, in the main, manages the function of collecting the RF messages for the remote controls and sender units for the insufficient tyre inflation pressure, transmits information concerning the steering wheel angle and operates the transponder aerial. The NVO guarantees the connection with the NBC for the following functions: management of the switches (lighting, direction indicators, windscreen wipers, horn, radio controls, speed regulator). emission of warning signals (buzzer built into the steering column switch unit module). dialogue with the transponder coil (aerial). acquisition of remote control RF signal. acquisition of insufficient inflation pressure function RF signal. Air Bag connection. steering wheel angle sensor information. VAN interface. system diagnosis. The steering column switch unit is supplied by the + VAN and the RF receiver function receives a permanent + 12V supply. The system activates the NBC each time the following actions take place at the steering column switch unit: activation of the horn headlamp switching on and flashing receipt of a message from the remote control concerning the opening of the doors. The steering column switch unit module moves to stand-by when there is an interruption in the +VAN. INTRODUCTION A loss in tyre inflation pressure can result in serious problems: Burst tyre A considerable deterioration in the vehicle's road holding and braking stability. Irregular, rapid wear of the tyres. Increased fuel consumption. Currently there is no device that informs the driver of a fall in the tyre inflation pressure; the insufficient pressure warning system is designed to meet this need by constantly checking the four wheels. In particular, the device has the task of constantly monitoring the three pressure states (normal, deflated, punctured) and whether a wheel(s) is(are) missing. The information is displayed both via the NSO (milomter warning lights node) by the STOP warning light coming on and via the NSC (multifunction screen node) in the form of a message in the display. Composition The system consists of: 4 pressure sensors inside the wheels transmitting at radiofrequency which allow a pressure, compensated for by the temperature of the wheels, to be measured (a variation in temperature of between -30°C and +70°C translates into a variation of 0.3 bar). 1 R.F. signals reception and management control unit located inside the steering column switch unit. The reception control unit also analyzes the correct operation of each sensor following no response from the sensor (malfunction or batteries run down) or if new sensors are being programmed. The sensors are designed to prevent possible false alarms caused by differences in pressure due to climatic and environmental conditions during the normal use of the vehicle. the wheel control system does not check the spare wheel, does not deal with over inflation and does not allow which wheel(s) has(have) the problem to be precisely identified. The product cannot be used in Japan, the USA, Israel, Australia and New Zealand and all countries which allow the use of RF devices with different frequency and emission ranges from Europe. Operation The structure of the system is illustrated below 1,2,3,4 - Tyre pressure sensors L1 - VAN CAR 1 network L2 - Van Confort network NVO - Steering wheel node NBC - Body Computer Node NSO - Milometer Warning Lights Node NSC - Multifunction screen node The sensor operating logic is mainly managed by the NBC which has the task of co-ordinating the various nodes and managing the associated functions. The NVO acquires the pressure information required from the 4 sensors by means of reception control unit and sends the "rough" signal to the NBC. The Body Computer Node processes the information from the NVO in detail using the following functions: it processes a possible puncture or insufficient inflation pressure, it determines the number of sensors missing it determines a rapid fall in pressure, a fairly rapid fall in pressure, a punctured wheel, a deflated wheel or incorrect pressure it memorizes wheel worn sender unit module battery" and "wheel sender unit module not read" faults. Depending on the alarm in progress, the NBC activates the various warning lights in accordance with the diagram below. Puncture alarm: The NBC detects a puncture alarm via the steering column switch unit module NVO The NSO (milometer warning lights node) lights up the STOP warning light when commanded by the NBC. The puncture alarm causes a message to be displayed on the screen and the steering column switch unit module produces an acoustic warning. Insufficient inflation The NBC detects a puncture alarm via the steering column switch unit module NVO The insufficient inflation alarm causes a message to be displayed on the screen and the steering column switch unit module produces an acoustic warning. Detection of tyre inflation pressure fault: The tyre inflation pressure alarm causes a message to be displayed on the screen and the steering column switch unit module produces an acoustic warning. The fall in pressure compared with the recommended pressure of 3.5 bar (set in the factory), until the tyre is considered to be deflated, is 0.3 - 0.5 bar, beyond this value the wheel is considered to have a puncture. Pressure sensor The pressure sensor is illustrated in the diagram below It is a device that monitors the pressure inside the tyre through a dedicated sensor which is linked to an electronic circuit for acquiring and processing the signals; it is has a section specially designed for transmitting radiofrequency signals at 433.92 MHz and a centrifugal switch for checking the rotation of the wheel. The signals transmitted are then received by a reception control unit dedicated to transferring danger information. The sensor is supplied by a lithium battery that lasts 10 years in normal vehicle usage conditions. A system that checks the state of the battery guarantees that there is an alarm at least 3 months before it is completely run down. Each sensor is also equipped with an identification code that is transmitted to the tyre pressure control unit which memorizes it. technical data: Maximum pressure range measured between 0.25 and 3.5 bar with a Maximum pressure resolution 0.014 bar Frequency 433.92 MHz, 90 Kh Operating procedure The presence of a switch (incorporated in the sensor) that is sensitive to the centrifugal force exerted by the rotation of the wheel, makes it possible to determine whether the vehicle is moving or stationary. This involves two data transmission and processing modes: vehicle moving mode; vehicle stationary mode. Vehicle moving mode The centrifual switch closes following the rotation of the wheel before a speed of 35 Km/h is reached or a maximum of 15 seconds after this level is passed. After it closes, the sensor measures the pressure and transmits the data immediately. During this stage, the standard pressure monitoring takes place every 15 seconds and the information is systematically transmitted within 15 - 21 minutes as long as the pressure values remain within the normal range. When an excessive fall in pressure is detected, the transmission takes place every 5 seconds. Vehicle stationary mode The shift to this conformation takes place 30 seconds after the vehicle has stopped with the centrifugal switch open. The sensor systematically checks the pressure every 15 minutes and transmits the signal within 65 minutes. If pressure irregularities are detected, the transmission takes place in the same way as for the "vehicle moving mode" and the first time the ignition is turned ON the customer is advised of the problem through the NSO and the multifunction screen. there is an opening in the sensor to allow the pressure to be measured and it should not be obstructed (avoid using spray canisters for inflation and fast repairs to the rubber) Fitting the sensor The tyre pressure sensor is fitted at the rear of the tyre inflation pressure valve. Fitting and dismantling should be carried out by specialized personnel using the correct equipment so that the sensor is not permanently damaged. Receiver control unit This control unit is incorporated in the NVO with a 433.92 MHz radiofrequency receiver with the identification codes for the 4 sensors memorized so that it is capable of carrying out each pressure check for each individual tyre. It is a specific module for the insufficient inflation function and the aerial is incorporated in the steering column switch unit module. Diagnostic function It is possible through the fault diagnosis to know the number of wheels that have a problem but not their precise location on the vehicle. A pressure of 2.31 bar is programmed in the NBC as the standard value but it can be reprogrammed and a different value set using the Examiner.

INTRODUCTION The vehicle is equipped with an electronic alarm that can only be activated using the remote control, with perimeter (exterior) and volumetric (interior) protection. The alarm is the ultrasound type and has the task of managing: the volumetric detection, the supply and management of the ultrasound sensors, the perimeter detection, the siren. OPERATING PRINCIPLES The various connections are illustrated in the diagram below. 1 - remote control 2 - NVO receiver 3 - NBC 4 - Direction indicators 5 - Switches in door locks and rear tailgate 6 - Volumetric surveillance off button 7 - Volumetric sensors 8 - Bonnet lock contact 9 - NAL 10 - Serial line 11 - Siren 12 - Alarm state LED Volumetric surveillance Volumetric surveillance is guaranteed by two ultrasound sensors, located in the front courtesy light, which allow movement or a variation in volume to be detected. Perimeter control The perimeter control is managed: by the NBC as far as the signals coming from the contacts in the 4 doors and the tailgate are concerned. by the NAL as far as the signal coming from the switch on the bonnet release mechanism is concerned. Its engagement is signalled by the flashing of the direction indicators and then the flashing of the LED located in the instrument panel. Locking the doors by turning the key does not switch the anti-theft device on. The alarm can be deactivated: using the remote control, the direction indicators flash rapidly for a few seconds, through recognition of the key by the Code system. With the alarm switched on, when one of the doors is opened using the key (an operation which does not switch off the alarm), there are 10 seconds to allow the Code to recognize the key. Perimeter control function The perimeter surveillance function is activated 5 seconds after the alarm is switched on. The function is managed by the NBC and the siren is activated in the following circumstances: following a variation in the condition of one of the switches in the door locks, following the disappearance of the +Bat, following the key being turned to the ON or starting position using a key not recognized by the Code system. The change in state of one of the switches located in the locks produces the reactivation of the NBC (door or boot opening) which, in turn, reactivates the +VAN network. The NBC transmits the siren activation order to the NAL and it remains operational for 30 seconds. Volumetric detection and lid opening function The volumetric surveillance function is activated 45 seconds after the alarm is switched on. The volumetric and bonnet measurements are managed by the NAL and the siren is activated under the following circumstances: when the volumetric sensors detect a significant movement of air inside the passenger compartment, following a variation in the condition of the switch located on the bonnet release mechanism. In the case of a break in, the NAL recalls current ot the DATA/ with a consequent reactivation of the NBC which, in turn, reactivates the network with +VAN. after 10 volumetric measurements made by the NAL during a continuous volumetric surveillance period, this function is automatically switched off and only the perimeter surveillance remains. Volumetric surveillance disengagement function The volumetric surveillance can be excluded by keeping the button pressed for more than 1 second before switching on the alarm. In this case the signal LED remains on. If the alarm is not switched on within 5 minutes of pressure the exclusion button, the system activates both surveillance functions. When the alarm is next switched on both the surveillance functions are activated except if the volumetric function is excluded. Particular functions Following a request to switch on the alarm via the remote control, if a part that opens (including the bonnet) is not properly shut, an auditory signal is produced. If the condition of this part that opens does not change after 45 secs, the alarm is activated. If the part that opens is closed before the alarm is activated, the NBC produces an alarm activatation request and operates the LED. SPECIFICATIONS The vehicles are equipped with an electronic system known as the CODE to produce the engine immobilizer function. The CODE system only allows the engine to be started after a secret code, memorized previously in the NCM, is received. System details The second generation Code system is incorporated in the Body Computer Node (NBC). COMPOSITION The CODE system comprises 4 basic components (in addition to the Body Computer which acts as a control unit): CAN line for dialogue between the NBC and the NCM between two and five electronic keys containing a transponder with a secret code; an aerial that reads the code contained in the key transponders; the NCM. 1 - Key 2 - Aerial 3 - Steering Wheel Node (NVO) 4 - Body Computer Node (NBC) 5 - Engine Management node (NCM) 6 - Signal LED OPERATION The CODE allows the start of the engine management by the NCM by means of a coded dialogue between the NBC and NCM during the stage that precedes starting. After the key is turned to the ON position, the NCM sends a code request to the NBC which only responds after having recognized (via the aerial) a known electronic key in the ignition switch. If the secret code in the answer is valid, the NCM continues with the regular engine management activities, allowing the engine to be started up. The NCM can only memorize the secret code through a special procedure. The operation of the CODE is guaranteed if any of the other NBC functions are not working properly. After recognizing an enabled transponder, the CODE switches off any alarm system. Interaction of Code with the key Every key contains a transponder with the IDENTIFICATION CODE and the SECRET CODE. As soon as the key is turned, the transponder sends the identification code to the CODE which, having recognized it as one of the enabled ones, continues with the transponder recognition strategy. If the identification code is not recognized, the procedure is aborted and the engine cannot be started. The transponder is recognized by means of an algorithm with an encrypted code exchange. The code recognition time is less than 160 ms per attempt. The CODE attempts the transponder acquisition for up to 1 second. Dialogue between engine management node and NBC The dialogue between the CODE (NBC) and the NCM takes place via the CAN. Starting from when the key is turned to the ON position, the flow of code exchanger operations between the NBC and the NCM depends on the NCM status (pristine or programmed).l If the NCM is pristine, the procedure involves sending the fix-code request to the NBC: in this way the NCM lears the secret code and stores it in its memory. This procedure is known as CODE RECORDING. If the NCM has already been programmed, the procedure involves checking that the fix-code stored in the engine management control unit memory and the one memorized in the NBC correspond: the NCM asks the NBC for the secret code and compares it with its own. This procedure is known as CODE VERIFY. CODE RECORDING The CODE RECORDING procedure is the memorizing of the fix code in the NCM. Only after the NBC has memorized the identification codes, the secret code and the fix code, is the NBC ready to satisfy the request to transmit a code to a pristine NCM. After the ignition key has been turned, the NCM initializes its software and, if it is pristine, requests the fix code. If the NBC is not pristine, it responds by sending the fix code, but only after having recognized an authorized key. If the key is not authorized (unrecognized) or there is no key, the CODE does not respond. When the NBC is pristine and there is no transponder in the aerial, it does not respond to the NCM's request for a fix code. CODE VERIFY This is the standard procedure that is repeated during the life of the vehicle each time the user insesrts the key in the ignition and turns it ON. this procedure enables the starting of the engine if the key inserted is enabled. The code verify procedure continues even when the user turns the key to the starting position. After the key is in the ON position, the NBC recognizes whether the transponder in the key is one of those that is enabled. At the same time, the NCM initializes its software until it verifies whether a fix code has been memorized. If the answer is yes, it sends a fix code request to the NBC. In response to this request, the NBC only sends the encrypted fix code to the NCM if the transponder is recognized as enabled. If the transponder is not recognized (incorrect transponder, no transponder in the aerial, etc.), the NBC will send the code (incorrect transponder or missing transponder) to the NCM. If the NBC is pristine and the NCM sends a fix code request, after having recognized the transponder, the NBC responds by sending a pristine NBC transponder recognized encrypted code message. DESCRIPTION OF THE COMPONENTS NBC CODE function The CODE is a function of the NBC. The main CODE functions are: recognizing the introduction and rotation of a key in the ignition; placing the alarm in a deactivated state after recognizing an enabled key; producing an electromagnetic field to read the key transponder; sending the random code to the transponder; receiving the encrypted code transmitted by the key; memorizing up to 5 identification codes; memorizing the secret code; managing a list of up to a maximum of 5 enabled identification codes; managing the CAN line to the NCM; managing the lighting up of the warning light; carrying out the autodiagnosis. Aerial Specifications Toroid type aerial located around the ignition switch, sends a 125 kHz signal to the transponder. Operation The aerial is supplied by the NBC to energize the key transponder. Since the aerial needs to be as close as possible to the transponder (on account of electro-magnetic immunity, the limited range of the transponder and small dimensions) it is fastened axially to the ignition switch. Ignition key Specifications The mechanical key contains a cipher transponder in the grip. Operation The moment the key is inserted in the ignition and turned to the ON position, the transponder is energized by the aerial and responds by emitting the rolling, encrypted secret code. The emission into the atmosphere is sufficiently powerful to produce a high immunity to electromagnetic interference and the range is such that it can be received by the aerial in the ignition switch. If the code is recognized as valid, the NBC sends the NCM, on request, a coded signal allowing the engine to be started. Up to 5 keys can be programmed in the NBC. Transponder in the key Specifications The transponder in the key has the following stored in its memory: SECRET CODE which is the same for each transponder in the same key kit; IDENTIFICATION CODE which is different for each transponder produced; PROGRAMMING DATA for the secret code The identification code differs from transponder to transponder to guarantee that no two transponders have the same identification code even if there is a request for a duplicate in the Network.

COMPONENTS The windscreen wiper consists of two blades moved through a "butterfly" kinematic motion. There is a position in which the blades can be raised to facilitate maintenance (washing the windscreen or replacing the blades). If, within 60 seconds of the key contact closing, there is an impulse on the lever that operates the windscreen wiper, the windscreen wiper blades rotate until they are in a vertical position and then stop. At this point the blades can be cleaned or, if necessary, replaced. The windscreen wipers can only be activated with the ignition ON; like at the front, the rear blade returns to the stop position as soon as the key is switched OFF. After the interruption of the washing control, the windscreen wiper blade completes another three strokes. The front and rear washing functions can only be activated with the ignition ON. The activation of the windscreen wiper functions is controlled by the steering column switch unit module. The 5 windscreen wiper control lever positions are as follows: low speed, timed (low speed impulses), high speed, automatic intermittent, fixed stop The operation of the front windscreen wiper in the AUTO position involves the automatic switching on of the dipped front headlamps. With the wiper control lever in the intermittent position, the speed of the rear strokes is selected on the basis of the vehicle speed. The rain sensor is fitted in the centre of the front windscreen to manage the front windscreen wiper automatically. all the manual controls always take priority over the automatic settings. Automatic activation of front windscreen wiper In the automatic wiping position, the operating speed of the front windscreen wiper varies according to the amount of water detected by the rain sensor. The automatic mode is activated/deactivated by pressing the windscreen wiper control lever for a long time and this is signalled by a message on the multifunction screen. Sequence of the actions: the NVO acquires the automatic wiper control from the position of the windscreen wiper control lever and transmits the information to the NBC via the VAN CAR1 network, the rain sensor is supplied by the NBC to which it transmits information relating to the presence of water on the windscreen, the NBC signals the move to the automatic mode towards the NDVM via the VAN CAR1 network for the activation of the windscreen wipers, towards the VAN Conf network for information to the driver. The activation of the AUTO position produces an initialization stroke. 1 - Front windscreen wiper motor 2 - Engine Compartment Derivation Node (NDVM) 3 - Steering Wheel Node windscreen wiper control lever (NVO) 4 - Rain sensor 5 - Body Computer Node (NBC) 6 - Multifunction Screen Node (NSC) 7 - Milometer Warning lights Node (NSO) Manual operation of front windscreen wiper Sequence of the actions: the NVO acquires the automatic front windscreen wiper control from the position of the windscreen wiper control lever (5 possible positions) and transmits the information to the NBC via the VAN CAR1 network, the NBC receives the vehicle speed information from the NFR via the CAN, the rain sensor is supplied by the NBC to which it transmits information relating to the presence of water on the windscreen, on the basis of these elements, the NBC transmits the front windscreen wiper motor activation control to the NDVM via the VAN CAR 1 network, the NDVM activates the relays that control the front windscreen wiper motor, the NBC guarantees the thermal protection of the engine by means of "fixed stop" information supplied by the windscreen wiper motor. 1 - Front windscreen wiper motor 2 - Engine Compartment Derivation Node (NDVM) 3 - Steering Wheel Node windscreen wiper control lever (NVO) 4 - Rain sensor 5 - Body Computer Node (NBC) 6 - Brake Node (NFR) Features If the vehicle speed is below 5 km/h, the windscreen wiper intermittent speed decreases by one level, e.g. from high speed to low speed. The initial setting level is automatically recovered when the speed of the vehicle is above 10 km/h. It is therefore possible to maintain the desired wiping speed by operating the windscreen wiper control lever. One impulse of the windscreen wiper control lever produces: a single stroke of the blades, keeping the lever towards the driver controls: the continuous activation of the blades, front windscreen washing, headlamp washing (if switched on). Manual operation of rear windscreen wiper Sequence of the actions: the NVO acquires the rearsreen wiper control from the position of the windscreen wiper control lever (2 possible positions: stop and rear intermittent) and transmits the information to the NBC via the VAN CAR1 network, the NBC receives the vehicle speed information from the NFR via the CAN and the "reverse gear engaged" information, on the basis of this information, the NBC manages the operation of the rearscreen wiper and controls the operation of the motor directly, the NBC guarantees the thermal protection of the engine by means of "fixed stop" information supplied by the windscreen wiper motor. 1 - Steering Wheel Node windscreen wiper control lever (NVO) 2 - Rearscreen wiper motor 3 - Body Computer Node (NBC) 4 - Reversing sensor 5 - Brake Node (NFR) Features The operating speed of the rearscreen wiper varies inversely according to the speed of the vehicle (as the speed of the vehicle increases, the frequency of the strokes decreases and viceversa). The rotation of the rearscreen wiper ring nut activates the rearscreen wiper, keeping the ring nut turned, in addition to activating the rearscreen wiper also activates the rearscreen washer function. The rearscreen wiper is automatically activated when reverse gear is engaged with the front windscreen wiper working. Front and rear screen washing Sequence of the actions: the NVO acquires the automatic headlamp washer control (rearscreen washing) from the position of the windscreen wiper control lever and transmits the information to the NBC via the VAN CAR1 network, the NBC transmits the two-way washing pump activating control, for washing the front or rear screen, to the NDVM, the NDVM controls the operation of the screen washer pump directly, the NBC transmits the front windscreen motor activating control to the NDVM, the NDVM controls the operation of the front windscreen wiper motor directly, the NBC controls the operation of the rearscreen wiper directly, 1 - Steering column switch unit: if the steering wheel switch unit detects a fault the "defective switch" information is memorized by the NBC. OPERATION IN CASE OF FAULTS The rain sensor If there is a rain sensor fault, the steering column switch unit auto position corresponds to a fixed intermittent operation of 4.5 secs. In this case, the multifunction screen will display the "Automatic windscreen wiper not available" message. Front windscreen wiper If there is a fault in the VAN CAR1 network, the NBC will force the automatic operation of the windscreen wiper. If there is a fault in the steering column switch unit, the NBC will force the automatic operation of the windscreen wiper. If there is a fault in the steering column switch unit and the rain sensor, the NBC will operate the windscreen wiper motor with a fixed intermittence of 4.5 secs. If the "vehicle speed" information is lost, the front windscreen wiper speed reduction function dependent on the vehicle speed will be lost. The intermittent operation in this case will be 4.5 secs. Rear windscreen wiper If there is a problem with the VAN CAR1 network, the operation of the rearscreen wiper will be inhibited. If there is a problem with the steering column switch unit, the operation of the rearscreen wiper will be inhibited. If there is a problem with the steering column switch unit or the VAN CAR1 network, the rearscreen wiper will consider the operating mode of the front windscreen wiper controlled by the rain sensor. If there is a problem with the front windscreen wipers, the rearscreen wipers will work as described in the table below: Decreasing speed Increasing speed Duration of intermittence V < 5km/h V < 10km/h rapid 5 < = V < 40km/h 10 < = V < 50km/h medium 40 < = V < 80km/h 50 < = V < 90km/h slow V > = 80km/h V > = 90km/h very slow If the "vehicle speed" information is lost and the front windscreen wipers are faulty: for vehicles fitted with a rain sensor, the rearscreen wiper will consider the front windscreen wiper operating mode controlled by the rain sensor, for vehicles not equipped with a rain sensor, the NBC will force fixed intermittent operation at 4.5 secs. If the following occur simultaneously: loss of "vehicle speed" information, faulty rain sensor and if the front windscreen wipers are not working properly, the NBC will force fixed intermittent operation at 4.5 secs. If the "reverse gear engaged" information is lost, the rearscreen wiper function when reverse gear is engaged will be inhibited. Washing If the washing request persists for more than thirty seconds, the washing function is inhibited. COMPONENTS The vehicle is equipped with: a function that automatically switches on the dipped headlamps when light conditions are poor. the function known as Parking (follow me home) keeps the exterior lights on for a timed period after the ignition key has been removed. If the light is below 850 LUX, the dipped headlamps remain on for 45 seconds. after having turned the ignition OFF, a flash switches on the dipped headlamps for 1 minute. It is possible to interrupt this by operating the headlamp flasher switch again (this function does not control the buzzer for lights remaining on when the doors are opened). A funciton for automatically switching on the direction indicators in the case of strong deceleration or an impact with the activation of a two tone horn. The direction indicators are located: in the door mirrors, in the front and rear light clusters. The rear light clusters include: the direction indicators, the brake lights, the 3rd brake light is located at the top of the tailgate, the reversing lights, the rear fog lamps. INTRODUCTION The vehicle is equipped with: two front doors with a lock barrel and manual opening device on the doors for opening them from the inside, when one of the internal opening controls is operated (even for the sliding side doors) with the vehicle is locked mode, the vehicle is unlocked. a tailgate with an electric lock and an exterior opening button, two sliding side doors, for the second row of seats with a manual opening control on the inside that can be switched off mechanically or electrically for child locks and can be switched off electrically for total locking and an exterior opening control that can be switched off electrically, a central locking button with a display of the status of the parts that can be opened, a remote control with two buttons for locking/unlocking the vehicle (and a remote control with 4 buttons, 2 of which are designed for the electrical opening of the motorized side doors). a fuel tank flap which cannot be electrically locked (fuel tank cap with key). Versions/options Depending on the devices fitted and the configuration of the vehicle, the locking system may be the following types: simple (regular locking), total in 1 stage (superlocking is engaged the first time the button is pressed or the first time the key is turned in the driver's door lock), total in 2 stages (superlocking is engaged the second time the button is pressed or the second time the key is turned in the driver's door lock if this is done within 5 seconds of the initial locking action). Superlocking means that the doors cannot be opened from the inside using the electrical switching off mechanism for the interior door control. Optional alarm connected to the total locking. The possibility of electrically operating the child locks using a button on the front courtesy light to activate or deactivate this safety feature (if electric rear windows are fitted, this button is used for the electric rear windows). The motorized opening/closing of each sliding side door using the control buttons on the front courtesy light and at the base of the doors and a remote control with four buttons (locking, unlocking, right door and left door). Central locking The first locking control (simple locking or superlocking) using the remote control or the key, involves the central locking of the windows and the closing of the roofs that have been opened using a sliding movement (this control is not effective if the roofs have been opened at an angle). Composition The control devices are: a remote control transmitter, 4 internal opening controls, one on each door, an external opening button located on the tailgate, a central locking button located near the centre front courtesy light. The devices controlled are: one driver's door lock, one front passenger door lock, 2 passenger door locks, one electric lock in the tailgate. Remote control transmitter The keys are designed for: the ignition switch the driver's and passenger door locks the remote control door opening/closing system the alarm system (if fitted) the disabling of the passenger air bag the fuel tank cap lock the glove compartment lock. The key may have 2 or 4 buttons: A for activating the central locking control, switching on the alarm and the location function. B for activating the release of the central locking and switching off the alarm. C for activating the right sliding side door opening/closing control. D for activating the left sliding side door opening/closing control. Pressing button A for longer activates the "location" function: all the interior courtesy lights, together with the direction indicators, come on for a few seconds. The key is also fitted with a metal insert E which can be enclosed in the actual key fob after pressing button F. Press button F again to make the metal insert come out of the key fob. The remote control functions (locking, unlocking, window management) are deactivated if: the key is in position +ACC, the key is in position +MAR, the key has been inserted in the anti-theft device a minute after the driver's door has been opened, the key is inserted, one minute after chaning from position +ACC to the OFF position. As a general rule, the remote control will be switched off so that the vehicle is capable of identifying the ignition OFF position. Resynchronization of remote control In order to synchronize the remote control: turn the ignition key to the +ACC position, keep one of the remote control buttons pressed for 10 seconds, remove the key from the ignition switch. Central locking button and LED The central locking switch is the type with a button with a red LED. The button is located in the centre courtesy light. The button makes it possible to lock and unlock the vehicle; it is activated in the following conditions: the moment the vehicle is unlocked using the remote control, the moment the vehicle is unlocked using the door lock. This button is not activated simultaneously by a command received from the remote control, the door lock or following a new automatic closing operation. FUNCTIONS One of the sliding side doors is managed exactly the same way as a conventional door for the vehicle locking function: when there is a command to lock the doors there is a "refusal" if one of the sliding side doors is open an opening command from the inside unlocks all the parts that can open, a door open signal is displayed (on the multifunction screen) if one of the sliding side doors is open whilst the vehicle is moving. Simple or super-locking lock in 1 stage The locking strategies for the parts of the vehicle than can open can be configured in such a way that a locking command using the button in the remote control or turning the key in the lock barrel directly implements the superlocking function. A locking command using the central locking button produces a "refusal" if one of the parts that open (door, sliding side door or boot) is open. The vehicle locks allow a direct move from the superlocking condition to the simple locking condition. The simple locking condition can be accessed: by pressing the locking button in the remote control within 5 seconds of the previous pressing and with the parts that open in the superlocking condition, by turning the key in the locking direction within 5 seconds of turning it previously with the parts that open in the superlocking condition. Simple or super-locking lock in 2 stages The locking strategies for the parts of the vehicle than can open can be configured in such a way that a locking command using the button in the remote control or turning the key in the lock barrel implements the simple locking function: a second locking command (within 5 seconds of the first one) produces the superlocking function. In practice there is a: move from the unlocked condition to the locked condition by pressing the locking button in the remote control or turning the key in the locking direction with the opening parts unlocked, move from the locking condition to the superlocking condition by pressing the locking button in the remote control or turning the key in the locking direction within 5 seconds of the previous command with the opening parts locked, move from the superlocking condition to the unlocked condition: by pressing the unlocking button in the remote control or turning the key in the unlocking direction. COMPLEMENTARY FUNCTIONS Automatic closing with vehicle driving The locking of the parts that can open takes place automatically, if the relevant function is activated, when the speed of the vehicle reaches 10 km/h. The tailgate is locked automatically whether the function is activated or deactivated. When the following conditions occur simultaneously: automatic locking function whilst driving, ignition key in ON position, vehicle locked after activation speed has been exceeded, pressing the central locking button briefly (for less than 3 seconds) deactivates the automatic locking function until it is switched off. Activation/deactivation of function The switching off and activation of the automatic locking function whilst driving can be activated by pressing the central locking button for a while. The activation/deactivation of this function does not change the vehicle locking condition. The activation/deactivation of the function is signalled by means of an auditory signal accompanied by a message (on the multifunction screen) that informs the driver of the new function condition; this only takes place if the ignition is ON with the engine either running or switched off. Vehicle location The location function (switching on of the interior courtesy lights plus the direction indicators for several seconds) can be activated in the following cases: with the vehicle in the simple locking condition, by pressing the locking button on the remote control, with the vehicle in the superlocking condition, by pressing the locking button in the remote control after having recorded the last locking or superlocking command. When this function is activated, all the direction indicators flash in unison for 10 seconds at a frequency of 5 Hz. This function is recognized by the system at a maximum distance of 30 metres from the vehicle. Vehicle ventilation A second unlocking command (remote control or key) in the 5 seconds following the first command to unlock the vehicle results in all the windows (except the sun roofs and the rear panels) being fully opened. Door opening in the case of an accident In the case of an accident, the NBC receives the air bag activation from the NAB and controls the opening of all the doors. The NBC carries out the adjustment for these 2 ways (through the front locks) and identifies the vehicle condition (door open/closed, vehicle locked/unlocked, etc.). The door open contacts condition for the rear doors (including the boot lock) is also recorded by the NBC. Door lock operation function The NBC receives and manages the orders controlling the locking of the vehicle: it manages the orders controlling the total locking, the child lock motor ensures the control of the total rear locking, it ensures the thermal protection of the locks, it controls the motors for the various locks (if the conditions are satisfied), it manages the display commands in parallel to the lock operation. Boot lock operation function The boot lock does not have a locked, unlocked or superlocked condition, only a "boot open or closed" condition. The NBC manages the boot lock opening motor when the doors open contact provides the "boot closed" information. Child lock operation function The NBC manages the orders that control the child locks. The child lock motor controls the total rear locking. ELECTRICAL STRUCTURE There is one less lead for each front door lock/NBC connection for locks with simple locking. The boot/NBC connection always comprises three leads. The total locking of the rear doors is guarnteed by the child lock motor. Lock heat protection The door locks are equipped with heat protection implemented by the NBC. The boot lock is not equipped with heat protection. INTRODUCTION The vehicle may be fitted with two motorized sliding side doors with an anti-crush safety system and child locks. Each of the two sliding side doors is fitted with a motor fastened above the left and right rear wheel arches. 1 - Door operating motor The management of the electric side doors is carried out by the Sliding Door Node (NPS) which is located above the right rear wheel arch. 1 - Sliding Door Node (NSC) The door opening/closing control buttons are located in the front centre courtesy light and on the left and right side door pillars. The button for activating the child locks is located on the control panel on the driver's front door. A - Left rear sliding door opening/closing button B - Right rear sliding door opening/closing button C - Sliding door opening button on rear pillar The motorized assembly comprises the following mechanical and electrical components: an electric motor capable of rotating in two directions by reversing polarity, an electric brake, an optical sensor, a speed reducer, protection for the motor against overheating, two leads that connect the reducer to the door pulley, a cable clearance recovery system, two idler pullies, sound insulation systems (e.g.: end of travel, silentblocs, etc., if necessary), a separate electronic node located on the bodyshell. 1 - Cable clearance recovery 2 - Electric brake 3 - Two cable idler pullies 4 - Optical sensor 5 - Speed reduction unit OPERATING PRINCIPLE Motorized sliding side door module function Interface with the VAN The NPS sends / receives the signals listed below via the VAN. For the left door: Acquisition of information: Control button on front courtesy light (left button), Control button on rear pillar (left), Lock contact (left), Door sliding sensor: power supply for sliding sensor, brake control, control of door sliding motor, control of (left) lock actuator. For the right door: Acquisition of information: Control button on front courtesy light (right button), Control button on rear pillar (right), Lock contact (right), Sliding sensor: power supply for sliding sensor, brake control, control of door sliding motor, control of (left) lock actuator. The NPS also allows the fault diagnosis of the function. Action in progress The NPS detects the following information: pressing of one of the front or rear buttons or the remote control, action on the interior or exterior controls. The NPS activates the door involved depending on the vehicle conditions and the user requests. If the NBC sends the NPS impact information (priming of a pyrotechnic component), the latter halts the movements in progress. The anti-crush safety function is controlled internally by the NPS. The two doors are controlled by the same node and are independent. Remote control The NVO contains the high frequency receiver. When a signal to operate one of the sliding side doors issued by the remote control is received, the NVO produces a signal at the VAN CAR1 networt (DATAB) so that the NBC activates the network (determining the appearance of the +VAN) and then the NBC sends the command to the NPS. Child locks In the case of mechanical child locks, the information is supplied by the rear door locks; in this case, the management of the child lock function is independent for each door. In the case of electric child locks, the information is joint with the rear electric windows inhibition information and is activated simultaneously at the two doors. Sliding side doors operating condition The go ahead for operation is managed by the NPS. The lighting of the front buttons is activated when the front seat controls are enabled. The lighting of the rear buttons is activated when the rear seat controls are enabled. Standby mode and function standby exit The NPS moves to standby mode when the +VAN is intertupted if the two sliding doors are closed. If there is a break in the +VAN whilst there is movement, it continues until the door has stopped completely even if an obstacle is detected. The change to standby mode only takes place later on. In standby mode the NPS examines the system input signals and sends the NBC a request to exit the standby mode if there is an input signal. In standby mode, when one of the doors is opened, the NPS detects the sliding of the door and makes a request to the NBC to end the stanby condition. In this case the NPS will not be completely in the standby condition because the position sensors remain activated but the system consumption will be minimal. End of standby for NPS The end of standby for the NPS is determined by the presence of the +VAN. If, after a request to end the standby by the NBC, the +VAN does not appear, the module remains in the standby condition. Physical interface The NPS reactivates the NBC via the VAN CAR2 network. The "door open contact" information reactivates the network directly via the NBC. Problem with left and right doors: fault = the module has detected a fault that prevents the operation of the door. Request to unlock doors: door unlocking request = there is an opening request when the vehicle is locked. Power supply The power supply comes from the +Perm. There are two independent power supplies.
