Anti-crush safety function during closing Anti-crush safety function activation conditions: the door is electrically locked, the device detects the presence of an obstacle. If both conditions occur, the NPS starts the anti-crush safety cycle which includes the following stages: a: stopping the door, b: controlling the activation of the lock if the door is almost closed and reversing the sliding direction of the door, c: opening the door by a predefined amount (reopening value), d: stopping the door. whilst the anti-crush safety cycle is being carried out, the commands coming from the switches and the remote control are ignored. Anti-crush safety function during opening Anti-crush safety function activation conditions: the door is electrically open, the device detects the presence of an obstacle. If both conditions occur, the NPS starts the anti-crush safety cycle which involves stopping the door. To limit the current absorption when the door opening motors start, their movement is offset by a certain time. If the two commands are simultaneous, the right door is operated first. The above strategy is not applied to an anti-crush safety sequence. Request to unlock doors If the vehicle is locked, before opening the door following a command using the button or the remote control, the NPS requests the unlocking of the vehicle doors. The door unlocking request can only be carried out if the vehicle is locked and if the opening of the door has been authorized. Operating sequence Opening request using the front or rear button or the remote control Possible request for end of standby for VAN Central unlocking of vehicle doors via the NBC, Receipt of vehicle unlocked information, Opening of the door, this action is carried out even if the order has disappeared. If no information is received concerning the unlocking condition within 1500 ms of the unlocking request, the NPS ignores the opening request and waits for a new command. an opening with the internal opening command mechanically unlocks the door. Manual door drive The manual drive for a sliding door is inhibited after the start of an anti-crush safety function procedure. Each new command reactivates the possibility of operating the doors manually. The manual sliding of the door in the closing direction causes the electrical closing of the actual door. This function is activated with the +VAN present and the +VAN absent, door open, in this case the sliding of the door reactivates the network. To check the closing of the door, the NPS does not wait for the presence of the +VAN (the enablement conditions are satisfied when the door is open). System heat protection The lock is thermally protected. The two door motors are controlled independently, if they are overloaded the system stops any movement in progress; in this case no electrical movement can be made until the overheated motor cools down. Operation with key in + AVV The +AVV present information halts all movements with the exception of those connected to the anti-crush safety function. When the +AVV information disappears, the previous movement continues until it reaches its conclusion. If a locking operation is interrupted, a new control relaunches a complete opening procedure. If a command is carried out in the presence of +AVV information, the latter is ignored and no sound is produced Opening electronic end of travel To reduce the stresses on the door mechanical end of travel, the system stops the door during the opening stage before it reaches the mechanical end of travel. This function is defined as the electronic end of travel. The system never operates the door beyond the electronic end of travel, including the following cases: closing anti-crush safety function procedure, reversal of closing movement. Reduced mode operation Contact at the locks with interrupted circuit: whilst opening: it is only possible to open the door manually, with an external or internal control whilst closing: activation of the anti-crush safety function, manual closing of the door. Contact at the locks short circuited: inhibition of the electric controls for the corresponding door, opening/closing of the corresponding door manually only, production of an auditory signal for each command not carried out, +VAN interrupted. Sound information The system includes three types of sound signals: a sound when the door is opened and closed, a sound for the activation of the anti-crush safety function and for the failure to carry out a command, following unauthorized operation, a sound for the failure to carry out a command, following irregular operation. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE The initialization procedure is carried out in the following cases: battery disconnection, removing/refitting sliding door motor. The initialization procedure is independent for the two doors and can only be carried out if the door in question is closed. If the door is open, the commands are ignored and a sound is produced (failure to carry out a command). To initialize the system it is necessary to: start with the door closed, control an opening (electrical), control a closing (electrical), control another opening (electrical). The initialization is not lost from the system after the door is closed manually. DIAGNOSTICS General remarks The NPS analyzes and memorizes faults. Fault codes are transmitted to the NBC via the VAN CAR 2 network. The detection of a permanent system fault prevents the nominal operation of the door. The following are permanent door faults: processing unit faults, sensor supply faults, button faults, lock contact faults, position sensor faults, lock operation faults, motor faulty, brake faults. List of faults Button or switch fault When the button (switch) has an interrupted circuit (not detected by the NPS): no action can be taken. When there is a short circuit: the corresponding input is inhibited and the +VAN interrupted. A contact is considered to be short circuited if it remains stationary for more than 20 seconds consecutively. This fault is memorized and the corresonding input is inhibited. The interruption of the contact for more than five seconds cancels the inhibition of the corresponding input and the fault is preserved in the memory. Position sensor fault Types of faults: interrupted circuit: logic level kept at high condition, short circuit to earth: logic level kept in low condition. If the position sensor is faulty: inhibition of the electric controls for the corresponding door, the corresponding door can only be opened and closed manually, production of an auditory signal for each command not carried out. No sensor information Types of faults: short circuit to earth, short circuit to +12V. This fault can only be detected if there is a power supply If a command to operate the motor is made and a sensor signal is not detected or disappears: an anti-crush safety function sequence is activated, the corresponding door can only be opened and closed manually, production of an auditory signal for each command not carried out. Lock operation fault Types of faults: interrupted circuit, short circuit to earth. The faults can only be detected with the door closed, during the actuator control. If the operation of the lock is faulty: inhibition of the electric controls for the corresponding door, the corresponding door can only be opened and closed manually, production of an auditory signal for each command not carried out. Brake fault Types of faults: interrupted circuit short circuit to earth The faults can only be detected whilst the operation of the brake is in progress. If the operation of the brakes is faulty: inhibition of the electric controls for the corresponding door, the corresponding door can only be opened and closed manually, production of an auditory signal for each command not carried out. Door motor fault Types of faults: The faults are only detected at the start of the motor operating stage. If the operation of the motor is faulty: inhibition of the electric controls for the corresponding door, the corresponding door can only be opened and closed manually, production of an auditory signal for each command not carried out. Fault + perm The disappearance of one or more permanent faults should not affect the VAN, irrrespective of the +VAN condition Earth faulty If one of of the two earths disappears or is not connected, the corresponding door will not work. Power output fault (motor, engagement, lock operation) An auditory signal will be produced for each command not carried out. When the +VAN disappears, no power output is activated. A power output short circuited to +12V will result in the two doors failing to work. Speed information fault Types of faults: receipt of invalid vehicle speed information. If the value of the speed information is not valid, the NPS will consider the vehicle speed to be above the limit. Beyond limit voltage fault Types of faults: supply voltage below the minimum operating limit, supply voltage above the maximum operating limit. When this type of fault occurs: the electric controls for the two doors are inhibited, any movement started is completed, production of an auditory signal for each command not carried out. The restoration of the voltage to the operating limits authorizes the electrical controls. Mechanical end of travel opening position fault If the module detects a manual movement of the door beyond the mechanical opening end of travel position, the end of travel recognition procedure starts again after the next electrical opening of the door. This can occur if an obstacle is detected whilst opening during the initialization procedure. Lock contact fault Types of faults: interrupted circuit (no signal during a lock operating command with the door closed), short circuit to earth. In the case of a short circuit to earth, the end of standby for the NPS is only possible via the +VAN. A lock contact is considered to be short circuited if it remains stationary for more than 20 seconds consecutively. This fault is stored in the memory. The operation of the corresponding door is inhibited. The interruption of the contact for more than 5 seconds with the door closed cancels the inhibition of the operation of the corresponding door. Initialization fault Types of faults: initialization not carried out, initialization not finished, initialization impossible, manual sliding of the door beyond the mechanical end of travel. Processing unit fault Types of faults: VAN protocol management system fault, EEPROM fault (reading or writing), CAN line fault.

INTRODUCTION The system comprises 3 dual movement sun roofs. tilting and sliding. Each sun roof has its own controls. A switch located on the front courtesy light allows the simultaneous operation of the roofs in the second and third rows. The sun roofs can be operated using the control buttons with the ignition key in the ACC or M positions. If the key is turned to the OFF position or after it has been extracted, the sun roofs remain activated for about 1 minutes; if the driver's door is opened during this period, the movement of the roofs is permitted until the door is closed. The anti-crush safety function is only available for the sliding movement; if an obstacle is detected whilst it is closing, the movement is halted and the roof retracted by around 15 cm. The tilted opening and closing function is impulse operated and the control must therefore be pressed for a long time. The sliding opening and closing function is impulse operated and the control must therefore be pressed for a long time or sequentially (automatic operation) by pressing briefly.. The sun roof nodes do not activate the VAN. The lighting for each switch is activated when the operation of the relevant sun roof is authorized. Switching off anti-crush safety function Proceed as follows to switch off the anti-crush safety function: keep the button pressed for a while in the opening direction until the end of travel opening position is reached, release the button, keep the button pressed for a while in the closing direction for less than five seconds after the moving panel stops. Operating mode in case of failure In the case of a problem, the operation is as follows: automatic opening or closing of the moving panel prohibited. manual opening of the sun roof authorized. initialization authorized by pressing the control for a while. closing only possible by pressing the control for a while: closing of sun roof through stepping type operation: sliding with a maximum movement of around 45 mm each time the control is pressed for a while in the closing direction, tilting with a maximum movement of around 5 mm each time the control is pressed for a while in the closing direction. Diagnostics The following information assists in the fault diagnosis: geared motor defect (sensors, relays, etc.), detection of an obstacle (number, position of the obstacle, etc.), initialization problem (type, cause, etc.), engine speed/transfer time too high/too short, problem with the sensors and actuators managed by the sun roof.

The electric windows are equipped with an anti-crush safety system. The door nodes that manage the system are capable of detecting the presence of an obstacle whilst the glass is closing by means of the anti-crush sensors. In this case, the system interrupts the travel of the window and reverses the direction immediately. The windows work: when the ignition key is in the ACC or MAR position, if the ignition key is in the AVV position, the manual controls for the windows are interrupted, except for the sequential commands in progress, for a minute after the interruption of the +ACC, until the closing, after the opening of the driver's door if this intervenes before the end of the timed preriod. The vehicle may be equipped with electric windows at the front only or at the rear as well. Versions with electric front windows Driver's door. There are two switches in the driver's door inner trim which operate the opening and the closing of the front windows when the ignition is switched ON. A - left front window opening/closing; A - right front window opening/closing To open or close the window, press the button; when it is released, the window stops in whatever position it is in at the time. The driver's window is equipped with the "continuous automatic operation" device (which works when the engine is running) for both lowering and raising the window. Simply press the button briefly to start the travel which continues automatically. the window will stop in the desired position by pressing the button a second time. Passenger door. There is a button for controlling the relevant window in the door trim. Versions with electric front and rear windows Driver's door. There are five switches in the driver's door inner trim which operate the opening and the closing of the front and rear windows and the child lock button when the ignition is switched ON. A - left front window opening/closing; B - right front window opening/closing; C - left rear window opening/closing; D - right rear window opening/closing; E - inhibition of operation of electric window buttons located on the rear doors and (where fitted) inhibition of rear sun roof control buttons. To open or close the window, press the button; when it is released, the window stops in whatever position it is in at the time. The driver's window is equipped with the "continuous automatic operation" device (which works when the engine is running) for both lowering and raising the window. Simply press the button briefly to start the travel which continues automatically. the window will stop in the desired position by pressing the button a second time. Passenger door. There is a button A in the door trim for controlling the relevant window. Sliding doors. A - window opening/closing Press the button to activate the window opening/closing control. The commands sent via the buttons on the driver's door take priority over all the others. The operation of the electric rear windows is inhibited when a sliding door is opened. Operation in case of faults If there is a fault with the VAN, the local control for the electric windows allows the: interruption of the rear passenger electric windows control coming from the driver's door, the automatic cycles in progress at the rear electric windows continue until the end, rear electric windows command from the rear doors authorized, without taking into account the previous state of the inhibition command. If there is a problem, the windows cannot be closed automatically if the vehicle has been locked using the remote control. Central window closing function When the central locking command is received from the remote control: activation, if necessary, of the network by the NBC (appearance of the +VAN), the NBC sends the command for the central locking of the windows to the front door modules and interrupts the authorization of the electric rear windows (electric rear windows switch power supply), the NBC sends the command for the automatic closing of the left rear window and the right rear window. If there is a problem, if the NBC does not receive the command from the steering column switch unit it supposes that there has been no request to move the window and, as a result, there is no central control. Vehicle ventilation function Press the remote control unlocking button a second time, at the time of unlocking or turning the lock a second time at the time of unlocking, activates the ventilation function (windows completely lowered). In this case: the NBC sends a command for the automatic opening of the windows to the front door modules, then carries out an automatic descent control for the left and right rear windows. If there is a problem, if the NBC does not receive the command from the steering column switch unit it supposes that there has been no request to move the window and, as a result, there is no central control. ELECTRIC REAR VIEW MIRROR ELECTRIC SYNOPTICS The functional diagram for the electric management of the door mirrors is illustrated below. 1 - Remote control 2 - Steering Wheel Node (NVO: incorporates the high frequency receiver and manages the signal reception) 3 - Body Computer Node (NBC: manages the folding and opening of the door mirrors) 4 - driver's seat memorizing button (where fitted) 5 - Driving Position Node (NAG: manages the seat memorizing (where fitted)) 6 - Passenger Door Node (NPP: manages the adjustment of the passenger door mirror) 7 - Passenger door mirror (incorporates the adjustment and folding motors) 8 - Driver's door mirror (incorporates the adjustment and folding motors) 9 - Driver's Door Node (NPG: acquires the status of the door mirrors adjustment button and manages the adjustment of the driver's door mirror) 10 - door mirror adjustment controls OPERATION Electrical adjustment The operation of the rear view mirrors is guaranteed: when the ignition key is in the +ACC or +MAR position, for a minute after the interruption of the +ACC, the NBC delays the placing on stand-by by a minute if a sequential or manual command is made at the end of the minute. All commands are inhibited during the 2nd minute, if the user sends a command from a rear switch, it will be interrupted when the timed period expires if a manual command is involved and, on the other hand, will continue through until the end of a sequential command is involved. until the closing, after the opening of the driver's door if this intervenes before the end of the timed preriod. for the folding using the remote control (interrupted contact), the NBC activates the door nodes to carry out the command. Adjust the special switch (D) in all four directions to regulate the mirror. Switch C selects the mirror to be adjusted. These mirrors are equipped with an electrical demisting device; it is automatically activated when the heated rear windscreen button is operated; this function is automatically deactivated after a few mintues as it works on a timer. Electric folding (if fitted) The folding can only take place with the ignition key in the ACC or MAR position. Operate button C in position 3 to fold the mirrors. A - Folding mirrors selection control B - Mirrors without folding function selection control C - Mirror adjustment switch 1 - Left rear view mirror adjustment 2 - Right rear view mirror adjustment 3 - Rear view mirror folding function Pressing button C alternately controls the folding or opening of the rear view mirrors. The rear view mirror folding function can also be controlled automatically the moment there is a "locking request" for the vehicle doors using the remote control. Operating diagram Rear view mirror adjustment: the driver's door control panel permanently transmits its status to the NPG (rear view mirror selected, movement direction required), the NPG transmits the status of the control panel switches for the door to the NBC, the NBC sends the command for the movement of the rear view mirror in the required direction to the door node involved depending on the status of the door panel, the door node carries out the command. Folding/opening rear view mirrors using the folding button: this operation takes place as described in the previous paragraphs as far as the acquisition of the folding request by the NBC is concerned, the NBC sends the folding/opening command for the driver's rear view mirror to the NPG and for the passenger rear view mirror to the NPP, the door nodes carry out the command received (folding or opening). Door mirror defrosting: the defrosting order comes from the rear windscreen defrosting control. After having acquired the defrosting request, the NBC sends the defrosting command to the door node involved. Automatic folding (if activated) Automatic folding is systematically carried out the moment the locking request is sent via the remote control. This function is available at any time. The mirrors are opened automatically when the ignition key is turned to the +ACC position. In the case of automatic folding or opening, pressing the folding button reverses the direction of rotation of the door mirror. It is possible to select the activation or deactivation of the automatic folding function using the door mirror selector: each time it is pressed for more than 3 secs, the configuration changes state to go from active to inactive and viceversa. An acoustic signal indicates the change in configuration. Initialization procedure After a forced mechanical movement, the door mirror folding mechanism is switched off (or uncoupled). As a result, the electrical state no longer corresponds to the mechanical state; to switch the folding mechanism back on and ensure that the mechanical and electrical states for the rear view mirror position corresopnd, the following actions should be carried out after the folding or opening of the rear view mirror. Acquisition of outside temperature The NPP acquires the outside temperature value from the sensor in the right door mirror. The NPP transmits the outside temperature information to the NBC. 1 - Body Computer Node 2 -Passenger Door Node 3 - Right door mirror 4 - Outside temperature sensor (on right door mirror) Operation in case of faults If there is a fault with the VAN, the local control for the door mirror allows: the stop of the passenger door mirror manual adjustment controls, the stop of the driver and passenger door mirror defrosting controls, the folding cycles in progress reach a conclusion, then the (driver and passenger door mirror) extension position is assumed. the manual adjustment of the driver's door mirror, Diagnosis The door nodes carry out the fault diagnosis for the various inputs/outputs. REAR VIEW MIRRORS DEFROSTING FUNCTION The functional diagram for the electric management of the door mirror defrosting is illustrated below. 1 - Driver's door mirror (incorporates the door mirror heating resistance) 2 - Driver's Door Node (NPG: controls the defrosting of the driver's door mirror) 3 - Passenger Door Node (NPP: controls the defrosting of the passenger door mirror) 4 - Passenger door mirror (incorporates the door mirror heating resistance) 5 - Heated rear window 6 - Body Computer Node (NBC: manages and controls the timed defrosting of the door mirrors and the heated rear windscreen) 7 - Engine Management node (NCM: provides engine running information) 8 - Climate Control Node (NCL: acquires the defrosting activation request made using the special button, or through the activation of the demisting function (MAX button in climate control system control panel), manages the button warning lights, 9 - heated rear windscreen actication button The rear view mirror defrosting function includes the following stages: the NBC determines the forced switching off level for the loads, the NCL acquires the defrosting activation/deactivation request from the button on the front panel and transmits it to the NBC via the VAN Confort network. the NBC sends the switching on command for the heated rear windscreen button warning light to the NCL via the VAN Confort network, the NBC manages the timed operation of the defrosting, the NBC controls the heated rear windscreen and transmits the defrosting request for the door mirrors to NPG and NPP via the VAN car 2 network, the NCL switches the heated rear windscreen warning light on or off depending on its operating state. Operation in case of faults If the battery voltage is above or equal to 15V, the defrosting function is deactivated. Forced switching off of loads The load deactivation function (implemented by the NBC) is aimed at preventing the battery from being run down or even ruined, by temporarily interrupting the current; depending on the deactivation level, the defrosting function can be deactivated; it is not taken into consideration for the windscreen wipers/washers but for defrosting.

INTRODUCTION Where the driving position memorizing option is fitted, the driver's seat and rear view mirrors are equipped with electric motors that allow the adjustment of the position (a movement motor). Each adjustment mechanism is equipped with a sensor that allows the Driver's Position Node (NAG) to identify the position of the seat and the rear view mirrors at any time. With the assistance of specific memorizing controls, the user can request the memorizing of the driver's posotion and can request that the seat and the rear view mirrors return to a position memorized previously. This function can be applied: to the driver's seat where the following four movements are memorized: seat forwards-backwards (sliding), seat height adjustment (parallel lifting), seat angle, backrest angle, the two door mirrors where the following movements are memorized: up-down adjustment for each mirror, left-right adjustment for each mirror. There are two methods for memorizing and recalling the driver's position: memorizing and recall using the memorizing control panel located on the seat, memorizing and recall of the last position using the remote control. Electrically adjustable heated front seats (where fitted) The adjustments can only be made with the ignition key in the ON position. A - button for lengthwise movement (forwards/backwards) and height adjustment; B - button for backrest adjustment; C - seat heating on/off control, D - seat position memorizing controls. There are 4 levels for the seat heating: 0 (off), 2 (medium heating), 3 (maximum heating), 1 (minimum heating), To carry out the memorizing, proceed as follows: move the seat to the desired position, press button M on control panel D, press button 1 on control panel D, if the seat position is to be memorized in memory 1, press button 2 on control panel D, if the seat position is to be memorized in memory 2, The position of the door mirrors is also memorized in conjunction with the seat adjustment. The NAG carries out: the memorizing of the information in the memories for a position if button M is pressed and then one of the two memory number buttons is pressed, the management of the manual seat controls using the manual control, the operation of the seat activators following a memorizing control, the acquisition of the positions indicated by the seat sensors, the management of the memorizing control panel located on the seat, the memorizing of the position of the seat and the door mirrors. the management of the memorizing control panel located on the seat, the memorizing of the position of the seat and the door mirrors, the VAN interface with the network for controlling the rear view mirrors via the NBC and the driver and passenger door nodes, the fault diagnosis of the system: seat motors and sensors, seat controls, memorizing control panel (when connected to the NAG). The NBC manages: the authorizations for memory recall and memorizing, the authorizations for automatic or manual memory recall the authorizations for the operation of the seat, the authorizations for the operation of the rear view mirrors. Procedure for memorizing positions With the key in position M (driving position) the user U1 makes the adjustment 1 (seat and rear view mirrors) by pressing button 1 and the memorizing by pressing button M and then button 1; similarly, for user 2, position 2, button 2, memorizing M2. Memorizing a new position cancels the previous one. Memorizing using remote controls Memorizing using the remote control consists of memorizing the current position of the seat and the rear view mirrors in the specific areas of the NAG memory known as Me1 and Me2 (irrespective of the control panel memories known as: M1, M2). The function consists of memorizing the current position of the driver's seat when the user presses the remote control locking button. The NAG can memorize two positions: Me1, dedicated to current positions known at the time of locking using remote control 1, Me2, dedicated to current positions known at the time of locking using remote control 2, Procedure for recalling regulation 1 or 2 With the engine switched off: simply press button 1 or 2 briefly to recall the corresponding position memorized. After the same position has been recalled five times in succession, the function is neutralized until the engine is started up. With the engine running: press button 1 or 2 until a sound signal indicates the end of the adjustment of the position set previously. Operating strategy With the key in position M, user U1 carries out adjustment 1 which is memorized (M1) after having pressed button 1 and the remote control becomes T1; each time U1 uses remote control T1 the latter will ensure adjustment 1. Two remote controls are always supplied with electrically adjustable seats, but if user U2 does not have remote control T2: user U2 opens the vehicle using remote control T1 and when button 2 is pressed this adjusts the seat to position 2 set previously. The memory recall for the positions memorized in Me1 or Me2 is achieved when the user presses the remote control unlocking button corresponding to the associated memory irrespective of the vehicle locking condition (vehicle locked or unlocked). The memory recall for the positions memorized in Me1 or Me2 is achieved at the same time as an unlocking when the user has pressed the "luggage compartment opening" button using the remote control (the vehicle was locked previously). Memory recall authorization conditions During a memory recall, any operation of the memorizing control panel or a direct control (seat or rear view mirror), stops the seat memory recall procedure (by pressing continuously or impulse recall). If a rear view mirror memory recall has been initiated, this operation is brought to a conclusion. To prevent the battery from being run down, a maximum number of 5 impulse memory recalls are allowed with the engine switched off, after this the recall requires continuous pressing. This number is reinitialized the moment the +VAN is interrupted or when the engine running information appears. Memory recall sequence The positioning of the seat is achieved through the following stages: simultaneous sliding and raising adjustment, then backrest adjustment. The positioning of the rear view mirrors is managed by the NBC, the adjustment takes place in parallel at both rear view mirrors. Acoustic warning device An acoustic device is activated to improve the user's pereception when there is recourse to the memorizing functions. The acoustic signal used is the one for the NVO. The NAG makes an acoustic signal production request to the NBD via the connection at the VAN CAR 2 network. The following cases are signalled: recording of the memorizing of a position: 2 sounds are produced, recording of the pressing of one of the memory recall controls: 1 sound is produced, normal conclusion of a recall sequence for a position memorized: 1 sound is produced. Operation in case of faults If there is a problem, any memory recall by pressing briefly or for longer is inhibited. If the +VAN is present, the seat can be operated directly using the manual controls. The NAG operates in local mode (predefined mode when the seat is fitted on the vehicle in the production plant). If there is a problem, the memorizing cannot be carried out using the memorizing control panel or the remote control. Safety In memory recall situations, if the motors are not operated and the node does not identify any variation in the position for 2000ms ± 10ms for the rear view mirrors and 300ms ± 15ms or the seat, the operation of the motors is interrupted and the memory return continues for the other mechanisms as if the mechanism in question was in position. In direct control situations, if the motors are operated and the node does not identify any variation in the position for 300ms ± 15ms for the seat motors, the node interrupts the operation of the motor. If pressed for more than 15 seconds ± 1 second, the node memorizes the fault. This action is stopped after the autodiagnosis and the elimination of the errors. If the fault disappears, the system becomes operational again. If a memory recall button, except the memorizing button (M), is stuck in the button activated position, the control line is not available. Controls can be made using the other lines. If an output is detected whilst a sensor does not identify any variation in position (and without a direct control or memory recall being requested), the system searches for the axis in question and activates the two outputs (this fault can occur, in particular, when a relay is stuck and the mechanism in question is in the end of travel position). Seat motors The maximum consumption for each motor below 13V, is between 20A at 23°C and 24A at -30°C A thermal switch incorporated in the motor ensures that it does not remain in torque conditions for longer than 10 seconds. Memorizing control Memorizing is only possible if the +APC is present. The memory recalls are recorded and remain valid as soon as the +VAN is detected. The memorizing control panel switches are independent and operating a voltage levels. The current passing through the contacts is between 5 and 50mA (pull up resistance at electronic node). Pressing either of button 1 or 2 is recorded and accepted even if the user has released button M. Manual seat controls The direct operation of the seat motors takes place via the contacts. The control takes place through voltage levels. The information is recorded and validated as soon as the +VAN is detected. Seat sensors The sensors used for identifying the positions are the impulse type, i.e. the identification of the position is relative. The maximum consumption for each sensor is 15 mA. A current of between 2 and 5 mA circulates at the sensor output when it is low (node pull up resistance). The power supply for the sensors is interrupted when the node is on standby (given that the mechanism is irreversible, there can be no movements if there is no power supply for the motors). Rear view mirror sensors The position sensors are the potentiometric type. There are two for each rear view mirror (one per axis). The power supply for the sensors is interrupted when the node is in the standby position. The variation in voltage supplied by the sensor is linear between each end of travel position. The position sensor is a potentiometer of 3.7k%OHgr; ± 20% protected by a resistance of 1k%OHgr; ± 20%. Diagnostics The diagnostic function is designed to facilitate maintenance and indicate whether a component is defective: control switches, sensors, motors, relays and nodes. The NAG carries out a fault diagnosis of the seat system and memorizes any faults. The possible faults are: when at least one of the motors should be activated (direct control or memory recall), the node detects no output activated, a rear view mirror direct control switch is activated later in both directions and the node does not receive information concerning the movement of the sensor for one than one second in each direction when the corresponding output is activated (fault in the sensor or the rear view mirror motor), a seat or column direct control switch is activated later in both directions and the node does not receive information concerning the movement of the sensor for one than 200ms in each direction when the corresponding output is activated (fault in the sensor or the seat or column motor), the node receives information concerning the movement of a snesor without a direct control or memory recall having been made and without an output being activated (movement as a result of an electronic fault), a memorizing request is not carried out correctly (memory fault). Keeping a control panel button pressed for more than 180s ± 5s at the end of the memory recall procedure means that a message indicating that this button is stuck is recorded in the memory. INTRODUCTION The parking assistance system provides the driver with distance information whilst reversing when they are approaching obstacles behind the vehicle; therefore the system helps when parking by identifying obstacles outside of the driver's field of vision. The information of the presence/distance of an obstacle is transmitted to the driver by means of acoustic warnings whose frequency depends on the distance of the obstacle. The system is deactivated when the speed of the vehicle exceeds 30 km/h Obstacle presence detection system display when reverse gear is engaged COMPOSITION The parking assistance system fitted on the vehicle consists of an electronic control unit and 4 ultrasound sensors located on the rear bumper. All the control unit input and output is protected against battery voltage and earth short circuits. Parking Sensor Node (NSP) The node is located on the right rear pillar near the speaker as illustrated below. A - Parking sensor node B - Acoustic indicator The electronic node carries out the following functions: it receives the information that reverse gear has been engaged from the main electronic control unit it activates the sensors it processes the signals received by the sensors it controls the operation of the sensors it activates the speaker located in the right rear pillar it manages the fault diagnosis and test functions Technical specifications The main technical specifications of the electronic system are described below. Max absorption 100mA approx Weight 80g Stand-by absorption around 50 Ma Dimensions 24 X 65 X 85 mm Discreet connections: Presence of trailer +12 V nominal supply (controlled by the ignition), Connections to rear sensors NSP Pin Out Black 18-way connector Pin Function 1 + VAN 2 + (buzzer signal) 3 Not connected 4 Not connected 5 Date B 6 Not connected 7 Earth 8 Not connected 9 Not connected 10 - (buzzer signal) 11 Not connected 12 Not connected 13 Not connected 14 Date 15 Centre asx sensor signal 16 Centre adx sensor signal 17 Asx sensor signal 18 Adx sensor signal Black 6-way connector Pin Function 1 Centre pdx sensor signal 2 Psx sensor signal 3 Pdx sensor signal 4 Rear sensor signal + 5 Centre pdx sensor signal 6 Rear sensor signal - ULTRASOUND SENSORS The sensor is an ultrasound transducer which acts as an intelligent transmitter and receiver of ultrasound impulses; both the frequency and the voltage of the impulses are generated in the transducer. The impulses produced are reflected by any obstacles; the transducer therefore receives an echo: the time measured between the emission and the echo alloes the distance of the obstacle to be defined. The sensors all have the same electrical and mechanical properties; the maximum detection distance for each sensor can be adjusted using software according to the location of the actual sensor. The arrangement of the parking sensors in the rear bumper is illustrated below. 1,2,3,4 - Parking sensors Main technical specifications The main specifications of the obstacle sensors are: Maximum distance at the centre 1.5 m Maximum distance at the side 0.6 m Minimum / maximum distance 0.25 %divide; 1.5 m Max absorption 5 mA Weight 35 g The power supply for the sensors is protected by an electronic fuse; the sensors are also fitted with hermetic connectors. Input signals via VAN Confort network: Vehicle speed Reverse gear engaged Output signals via VAN Confort network: horn via speaker (on right rear pillar) OPERATION The operating logic for the system in accordance with the multiplex network is illustrated below. 1 - Reverse gear engagement signal 2 - Trailer power supply signal 3 - Buzzer When the control unit is switched on (ignition ON) an autodiagnostic test and a test on all the peripheral functions are carried out. the system is ready to use in under 0.5 seconds. When reverse gear is engaged, the sensors are activated and, if there is an obstacle, the buzzer produces a warning light whose frequency increases as the obstacle gets closer. MEASURING DISTANCE OF OBSTACLES The electronic control unit controls the sensors which convert the control unit electrical signals into ultrasound signals at a rhythm of 10 measuring processes per second. The signal, reflected by any obstacles, is received by the sensor and the control unit compares the signal transmitted with the one rececived and, using suitable algorhythms, calculates the time elapsed between the issue of the signal and the reception of the echo (flight time). This information is translated into distance and communicated to the driver by means of sounds whose frequency is inversely proportional to the distance from the obstacle. Each measuring cycle involves checking that the entire system is working properly. OBSTACLE DISTANCE SIGNALS The control unit processes the information supplied by the 4 rear sensors activating the vehicle's audio speaker irrespective of whether this system is ON/OFF. During the warning signals, the programme which may be in the process of being transmitted via the audio system is muted. The tone produced by the speakers advises the driver that the vehicle is getting close to an obstacle; the tone lasts for 75 ms, whilst the pause between the tones is directly proportional to the distance of the obstacle: impulses in rapid succession indicate that an obstacle is very close; a continuous tone indicates that the obstacle is less tthan 25 cm away. The acoustic signal stops immediately if the distance of the obstacle increases. The table below indicates the minimum dimensions of an obstacle that can be detected by the sensors depending on the distance. OPERATION Possible system states Possible CONNECT statuses from the viewpoint of power supply and operation in general are as follows: OFF state, Normal state, Stand-by state (the DIN housing is on but the screen is off only if awaiting the exclusion of the +VAN signal). Operation still depends on the "system configuration". The configuration of the system memorizes which functions the user has selected as active. The functions are: Tuner, CD, CD Changer, Telephone, Service Call and Video (Dark on/off). OFF status All CONNECT functions are disabled and the various hardware modules are not supplied (excluding the control panel). NORMAL status In the NORMAL state, the CONNECT system is fully active and all system functions are managed in accordance with the system configuration. Internal modules are operational, as are the internal communication lines. When leaving this state the configuration of the system is memorized; later on, it is restored on re-entry to the normal state (with the exception of the dark on/off which is always set at off so that the TFT display is always activated). STAND-BY status In this status, the CONNECT system is active but looks exactly as though it were OFF to the user. In any case the only internal module that is fully operational is the GPS. Planned actions Ignition The user can switch the system on (move from OFF state to NORMAL state) by operating the: ON/OFF button SOS button (on the front panel) TARGA SERVICE button, pressed for a while (starts a service call) hand set lifting button inserting a CD turning the ignition ON (first rotation) Deactivation The user can switch the system off using different methods that depend on the status of the actual system. Also, if the key is present, the ON-OFF button only switches the audio function off, whilst if the key is not present, this button switches the entire system off. NORMAL STATE If the key is removed and neither a telephone call or a call to the call centre is in progress, the system switches off (or moves to the OFF state), obviously after the system configuration and the backup data is saved. If a phonecall or a Service Call are in progress, a timed period will be activated before the deactivation of the CONNECT (30 mins operation without the key and without any intervention by the user on the front panel buttons or the steering column switch unit remove control). At the end of the 30 minutes, the system will move to "economy mode" and switch off unless a telephone call or a service call is in progress. If the system is in the NORMAL state with the key off, it may switch off for the following reasons: automatically if the time out described above elapses, through the intervention of the user pressing the ON/OFF button (unless a Service Call or a telephone call is in progress). NAVIGATION MANAGEMENT AND LOCATION The navigation module receives data concerning the advance and change in direction from the vehicle sensors. This data is accumulated and processed by a specific algorhithm which, also taking into consideration the current position obtained by the GPS satellites, makes it possible to caculate the estimated positon of the vehicle (location of the vehicle). The estimate is produced thanks to the ABS which provides information concerning the wheels to the CONNECT; the node is capable of calculating the distance and refining the GPS co-ordinates to improve the precision. Navigation ("CONNECT NAV"/"CONNECT NAV +" only) The navigation module is capable of carrying out the following functions. Interface functions with other modules TRAFFIC DATA ACQUISITION FROM TUNER MODULE. The module receives traffic information from the tuner module via messages in the geographical areas where they are available. The information referred to is only the text type (useful message for the driver) or graphic (icon which is positioned on a map). Route Guidance Route Guidance involves all the activities of extracting, managing and processing the information required for guiding the user to the destination they have set. These activities are, basically: ROUTE CALCULATION: Calculation of the route between the current position and the destination; automatic recalculation of the route in the case of deviation from the current route, calculation of an alternative route, if the user requests a deviation. ROUTE GUIDANCE (NAVIGATION): Identification of the position of the vehicle on the route (and calculation of the distance to the destination); Identification of junctions along the route; Identification of manoeuvres at the junctions along the route (and graphic and voice instructions for the user): Calculation of the distance to the next junction where the user has to make a turn; Presentation of the manoeuvre at the next junction. COMPLETE DATA BASE MANAGEMENT: If a map CD-ROM is present, the navigation function uses the entire data base available (map list, points of interest, etc.). USE OF REDUCED DATABASE WHEN CD-ROM NOT PRESENT (LISTENING TO A MUSIC CD): It is possible to listen to an audio CD in the CD player during the navigation process. Simply following the procedure described. The map CD should be inserted in the CD player for the entire duration of the entering the destination and route calculation activities. At the end of this processing, the CD ROM can be removed using the eject button. At this point the system will: 1) automatically load the route calculated into the memory; 2) eject the map CD. The audio CD can now be inserted to start listening. Under these circumstances one part of the map information is available (names of towns and names of roads) relating only to the segments of the route. In any case, the reduced data base in the CONNECT memory allows deviations to the route with automatic recalculations without the need to reinsert the CD-ROM. However, the efficiency of these recalculations depends very much on the length of the original route. When the route data in the memory is not sufficient to continue the navigation process, there is a request to reinsert the map CD. If the system is switched off during navigation without a CD ROM, the next time it is switched back on, the map CD must be inserted to access the navigation functions. It cannot therefore work on another vehicle. If there is an attempt to install the radio on another vehicle, it will move to a mode where it will not be operational for the entire time until it is set up again. If the radio is removed and refitting on the original vehicle, it will start to work again normally the next time it is set up. The user should not carry out any particular actions to get the radio to work after a break in the power supply (no reinitialization is required if the battery is disconnected). Interference mode The anti-theft function is carried out through a VIN code test. The operating principle consists of superimposing a repetitive beep on the sound which is sufficiently annoying to the user. The interference mode functions by simply switching the radio on when it is not unlocked by the VIN code. The radio VIN code To implement the anti-theft protection, the radio memorizes the last 8 characters of the VIN code. The radio VIN code is programmed into the radio by means of a session during the configuration in the factory. The code can be reprogrammed using the diagnostic equipment. Radios are delivery in locked mode. The radios therefore work in the interference mode until the equalizing condition between the (radio VIN code) and the (NBC VIN code) is satisfied. Sound level adjustments In addition to the manual adjustment of the volume, the volume can be adjusted automatically The radio makes automatic changes to the volume in the following cases: Setting up of the radio The sound volume is memorized when the radio stops. If the volume is higher than 20, the next time the module is switched on again the value memorized for the volume will be gradually restored to a value of 20. Automatic correction of the volume based on the speed: if the user activates the automatic volume correction (VOLUME AUTO = ON) using the audio menu (adjustment carried out via the NSC), the sound volume increases or decreases depending on the speed of the vehicle. RDS functions The RDS function is activated and deactivated by pressing the RDS button briefly. When the RDS function is activated, the change from one frequency to another for the station being listened to is automatic based on a local radio decision. Regional mode (REG) The regional is activated or deactivated by pressing the RDS button for more than 2 seconds in FM mode when the RDS function has been selected. In this case, the equipment selects the best frequency from those broadcasters transmitting the same station. This option facilitates listening to one programme. The function is applied to all stations on the same network. Listening can change from one programme to another. TA functions Traffic news (TA) The request for traffic news can be activated or deactivated using the TA button. Pressing this button briefly tells the radio system to search for and tune into the stations (enabled for this service) which are broadcasting traffic bulletins. The traffic news replaces the source being listened to (except in the case of a phonecall or parking assistance or other similar communications). During a traffic news bulletin, the CD stops and pressing the TA button briefly or changing the audio source interrupts the bulletin. If the radio was in the mute condition, the NSC cancels the mute function. When the TA bulletin is finished, the mute function is cancelled and the previous source is returned ot. PTY mode (Type of programme) When the equipment is in the tuner source mode and FM band, pressing the TA button for a while activates the PTY mode. This function allows the type of programme to be selected, a change to a station broadcasting the PTY programme selected or a search throughout the entire the FM band for a station broadcasting a particular type of programme. The table below contains a list of available PTY programmes 4 Sport 5 Educational 6 Drama 7 Culture 8 Science J9 Miscellaneous IO Pop Music 11 Rock Music 12 Varied Music 13 Light Music 14 Classical Music 15 Other Music 31 Alert When the PTY selection mode is activated the screen will display the last type of programme selected. It is also possible to memorize the type of programme selected by pressing one of the numbered buttons (1-6) for a while and recalling it by pressing the appropriate button briefly. INTRODUCTION The CD Changer, located in the dashboard oddments compartment, has the task of reading the numerical information contained on the CDs and converting it into analogue audio electrical signals that can be read by the radio/Connect equipment. The system includes a CD player / changer, an extractable cartridge for 6 CDs and a CD eject button that is lit up. The CD module converses with the other devices on the VAN Confort network in order to carry out the commands sent, provide information concerning its own status and indicate any changes. The dialogue with the other devices only takes place via the NSC (multifunction screen node). In the case of problems, the CD changer has an automatic reset function available for the software and notifies the radio of a possible fault through messages displayed on the NSC multifunction screen (disc not introduced correctly, high temperature, etc.). Ten seconds after the power supply (+30) has arrived, the CD changer undergoes a compulsory automatic initialization stage. This period is necessary to ensure the correct operation of the module. Having received the STOP signal, the changer interrupts the reading in order not to wear out the head, keeping the position at the time of stopping in its memory in order to be able to resume from the same point later on. Pause mode In this mode the changer does not read the CD but the latter continues to turn and the head remains in the same position in order to resume from the same point. Normal reading mode The CD changer reads the CD tracks normally in order. Fast forward or backward reading mode Following a fast forward or reverse command, the CD changer starts the acceleration procedure. The radio volume is turned down in this mode. The procedure can only be cancelled if a reading in normal mode or pause command is received. Sequential reading of introduction of tracks mode The listening time for each introduction is 10 seconds. The procedure can only be cancelled if a reading in normal mode or pause command is received. Reading mode The CD changer (normal, fast foward or backward, introduction of the tracks) should manage the succession of tracks depending on the mode requested. The succession modes are indicated via the VAN. Random track mode The tracks on a disc are played in random order. Once all the tracks on a CD have been played, the next CD is played or, if that was the last CD, then the first one is played. Random CD mode The tracks on a disc are played in order. After the last track, the move to another CD is random. Track repetition mode The tracks on a CD are played in sequence. CD repetition mode All the tracks on a CD are played in order. Eject control The CD changer has a CD eject button. This button is lit up and the lighting logic depends on the state of the connections. If the +VAN signal is present, the warning light is on whilst if the signal is interrupted the warning light remains on for 10 minutes and then goes out. The CDs can be removed in this condition. pressing the eject button takes priority over all other actions received by the CD Changer module. In the case of problems, the CD changer has an automatic reset function for the software and notifies the radio of a possible fault (via messages such as: disc not correctly introduced, high temperature, etc.) displayed on the NSC multifunction screen. Ten seconds after the power supply signal (+30) is received, the CD changer undergoes a compulsory automatic initialization stage. This period is necessary to ensure the correct operation of the module.

INTRODUCTION The airbag system fitted to the car is activated following moderate to severe front or side impact to protect the occupants. The system is equipped with a smart system capable of activating the front activation devices, either partly or completely, depending on the seriousness of the accident, whilst the Side Bags and Window Bags guarantee protection for the chest and the head, respectively. It is NECESSARY for occupants to wear their seat belts correctly to ensure the air bags work to maximum effectiveness. The side protection system (Window Bags and Side Bags) do not have a dual stage (smart) system which is only fitted on the two front modules Air bag system components are designed to work on a specific vehicle. They therefore CANNOT be tampered with, adapted or installed on other types of vehicle. Any attempt to reuse, adapt or install on another type of vehicle may cause severe or fatal injury to car occupants during normal use or in the case of impact. The car must be handed over to the customer with the passenger airbag deactivation switch in ON position and control panel warning lights off. For safety reasons, NO continuity checks can be carried out on the wiring. GRAVE DANGER! The front airbag module MUST be deactivated using the special switch if a child seat is fitted to the front passenger seat. COMPOSITION The system consists of the following devices: one Air Bag Node (NAB); twin (driver and passenger) front air bags with dual stage activation, two side air bags (side bags) on the front seats; two seat belt sensors for the front seats; two seat position sensors (left and right); passenger air bag manual disabling switch, two electronically activated front seat belts with pretensioners with load restricter: a front module for protecting the driver´s knees; two side protection window modules; two side impact sensors fitted on the side pillars (one for the right side and one for the left side); two electronically activated rear seat belts with pretensioners with load restricter: The following indications show the system is working properly: fault warning light (red) in the milometer warning lights node; passenger air bag disabled warning light in the milometer warning lights node; tester input, which converses on the K line, to check operation using an EXAMINER.
