The node is rigidly secured to the body beneath the central car consule near the centre of gravity. This location allows interior deceleration sensors to detect car deceleration with accuracy. The NAB should always be fitted with the arrow, stamped on the adhesive plate, facing the direction of travel of the vehicle. Always check that there are no foreign bodies between the Air Bag Node and the bodyshell and tighten the fixing bolts to the recommended torque. The Air Bag Node contains deceleration sensors including one electromechanical safety sensor that activates an activation enablement function independently of the electronic sensor. If the car deceleration level detected by the electronic sensor and processed by the ECU in terms of impact severity, exceeds the severity level set for the device deactivation control, the system allows the command to be sent only if the safety sensor is closed at the same moment. The following functions are present to ensure the system is correctly managed: energy accumulation: the presence of a condenser, which acts as an energy reserve, ensures the full operation of the front primers to guarantee operation if there is a break in the power supply at the time of the impact fault memory: with the key ON, the Air Bag Node continuously monitors circuit operation (including energy reserve circuits) during normal vehicle operation and impacts. It also diagnoses all electrical parts of the system and indicates the presence of faults by turning on an airbag system fault warning light on the instrument panel and saving the fault code. crash memory: records information on crash events that trigger activation of the pretensioners and front or side modules. The Air Bag Node interfaces with the VAN Car 1 network which is connected with the body computer node as illustrated below 1 - Webasto fuel pump disabling 2 - Air Bag modules 3 - Passenger Air Bag disabling key 4 - Fuel injection pump disabling L1 - CAN L2 - VAN CAR 1 network L3 - VAN Comfort In the case of an impact, the Air Bag Node sends the activation command to the modules involved; the activation signal, which travels on the VAN Car 1 network, reaches the Engine Compartment Junction Unit Node (NDVM) which inhibits the injection pump (4 in the diagram). The signal is forwarded by the NBC to the CAN and to the VAN Confort network: The NBC controls the release of the door locks and activates the hazard warning lights (warnings in the diagram) On the VAN Confort network, the NIT (if fitted) informs of the activation of the Air Bags by sending an emergency call. (see note) The signal is received on the CAN by the NCM which inhibits the fuel pump (1 in the diagram) for the Webasto additional heater (if fitted) An automatic call is always followed by a confirmation phonecall from the service centre to check the circumstances of the call. This ensures a type of "filtering" and prevents the emergency services being sent unnecessarily guaranteeing that they are available if a serious accident should take place. Operation The activation of the protective devices is subject to the information acquired directly from the actual node and via the vehicle network. In the case of a frontal impact, the system receives and filters the information, processes it, confirms it and determines the nature of the impact. In particular, the system makes use of information relating to whether or not the front seat belts are fastened (for the activation of the front air bags), the position of the front seats (for the activation of the front air bags) and the speed of the vehicle in order to lower the activation levels for the pyrotechnic components. The front air bags, in turn, feature dual stage activation by means of a twin pyrotechnic charge The dual stage system makes it possible to activate the front bags using different inflation methods: witht maximum inflation energy or with minimum inflation energy. This energy is controlled by using two charges for each air bag which are primed in sequence in accordance with a logic processed by the actual NAB. Side impact Similarly, when side impact occurs, the system is able to recognise direction and intensity and thus activate the airbags present on the side affected by impact. To provide total cover against side impacts, two satellite sensors located in the centre pillars (one on each side) are used. When a side impact takes place, the satellite sensors detect the impact signal directly along the transverse axis of the vehicle and send it to the Node. This signal, processed by the microprocessor, makes it possible to detect the seriousness of the side impact and, as a result, to decide whether to activate the side air bag on the side involved. Vehicle roll over The Air Bag Node is capable of determining the angular speed (through a dedicated sensor) checking whether the vehicle has turned over. In this situation, the system activates both Window Bags, the Side Bags and the pretensioners fitted. the activation of the air bag modules is independent of the activation of the pretensioners. System self-diagnosis The Air Bag Node carries out continuous self-diagnosis of system operation. More specifically: it detects and stores faults; it indicates the source of these fault by turning on an instrument panel warning light. it recognises the various components and the fault type; Faults stored in the control unit may be deleted only after the fault has been repaired by means of the EXAMINER device. Driver´s AIR BAG module The driver´s air bag module is illustrated below 1 - Driver´s airbag module A - Green connector B - Blue connector Composition The driver´s air bag is a device designed to protect the driver in the case of medium-serious frontal impacts by placing a bag between the occupant and the steering wheel. The module comprises: a 60 litre bag, made out of silicon polyammide cloth designed to minimse skin abrasions in the case of contact and folded in such a way as to ensure that inflation is gradual and not directed toward the driver; a hybrid pressurized gas generator a containment case. A warning plate on the base of the gas generator shows handling instructions Operation Bag inflation is determined by a gas generator that offers two intervention stages that can be activated separately according to impact severity. The two pyrotechnic charges explode in sequence: the difference in time between the activation of the first and second charges determines the inflation energy of the bag. Depending on the extent of the impact, whether or not the seat belts are fastened and the distance of the seat from the steering wheel, the system controls the activation of the air bags in accordance with the different operating modes. Passenger AIR BAG module The following figure shows an assembly view 1 - Connector 3 - Bag support 4 - Panel support 2 - Inflatable bag Composition The module comprises: a metal mount containing the hybrid gas generator and bag; a cover that tears at preset points when activated to allow the bag to expand correctly; a 100 litre fabric bag designed to keep skin abrasions to a minimum in case of contact which is specially folded; a gas generator comprising a hybrid pressurized gas container a connection point to the electrical system; A warning plate on the bag cover shows handling instructions The passenger air bag flap is located at the top of the dashboard in a position so that the bag comes out towards the passenger tearing the flap built into the dashboard at pre-set points. The passenger air bag module activation principle is the same as that described for the driver´s air bag module. Passenger Air Bag disabling switch with key View showing location on car 1 - Passenger air bag on/off position plate 2 - key-operated switch 3 - Passenger side disablement warning light An ignition key-operated switch allows enablement (On) and disablement (Off) of the air bag module on the passenger side. Deactivation takes place using the ignition key and a special switch and key located on the right side dashboard trim. The switch is only accessible with the door open. There are two positions for the switch and key: position 1 (On): front passenger air bag activated, warning light off; position 2 (Off): front passenger air bag deactivated, warning light on; babies can be carried protected by special child seats on the front seat. In the Off position, the NAB excludes the activation of the passenger air bag, but leaves the activation state of the pretensioner and side bag unaltered. Switch faults are indicated by activation of the air bag system fault warning light. The deactivation logic of the passenger air bag is illustrated below 1 - Passenger air bag inhibition on signal 2 - Acoustic signal 3 - Signal on NQS display 4 - Passenger air bag disabled warning light on L1 - VAN CAR 1 network L2 - VAN Comfort The information on the inhibition state of the passenger air bag is managed by the NAB, whilst the command to switch on the passenger air bag disabled warning light is produced by the NBC on the VAN Confort network (the NSO operates the passenger air bag disabled warning light on the basis of the command received). The inhibition of the passenger air bag causes a message to be displayed on the screen and the steering column switch unit module produces an acoustic warning. The NBC manages the switching of the displays and sends a display command to the NSO. the switch is not operated with the ignition key ON (e.g. using the second key). In this case, the electronic control unit saves an error, indicates it by turning on the air bag system fault warning light and deactivates the module. Side impact satellite sensors View of location of left sensor A - Satellite side impact sensors The side protection system consists of the airbags and also an electronic control circuit that ensures the system operates correctly. There are two satellite sensors (one on each side) containing an accelerometer, fastened to the underbody close to the front side pillar, which measure the acceleration resulting from a side impact. A pin on the rear part of the sensor is used to position the sensor correctly in its seat. The case also contains a connection point for connectoin to the electrical system (green connector). Operation If the acceleration value measured by the sensor gives rise to a certain level being exceeded, the information is sent to the air bag system control node. If the values measured do not exceed a certain acceleration level, the NAB controls the activation of the side air bags (window bags and side bag) on the side affected by the impact. SIDE BAG modules The following figure shows an assembly view 1 - Side Bag housing cover To ensure maximum front seat occupant safety in the case of side impact, side bag modules are installed on the seat backrests; they are fitted on the outside of the seat backrest, under the cover. This solution means that it is possible to always have the cushion in the optimum position for the occupant, whatever the seat adjustment. This configuration is considered one of the most effective because it ensures the airbag is always in optimum position in relation to the occupant regardless of seat setting or occupant size. The side bag is capable of mainly protecting the chest and abdomen, even if the seat occupant is not sitting properly because bag opening dynamics (11 litre volume) minimise the risk of body damage caused by impact with the airbag. Operation The module gas inflation generator is electrically activated by means of a signal from the NAB. Following this signal, a pyrotechnic activation is set off that causes the gas in the generator to expand and inflate the bag. The increase in bag volume breaks the plastic container in the set areas and causes the squab cover seams to yield along the preset sections to allow the bag to emerge correctly. The bag deflates immediately after being inflated by the gas thanks to the presence of s epcial opening. It is not possible to carry out operations on seats fitted with air bags, apart from seat removal/refitting. It is strictly forbidden to dismantle seats fitted with air bags. This operation must be carried by trained, authorised technical personnel. Do not cover the front seat squab with extra covers. Do not wash the seat squab with water or steam under pressure. WINDOW BAG module (side blind AIR BAG) Assembly view 1 - Connector 2 - Gas generator All versions of the car come with a system for protecting the head of front and rear side occupants in the first, second and third rows. The head protection air bags (i.e. window bags) work in conjunction with the front air bags to offer front seat occupants the best possible protection in the case of impact. They also eliminate the risk of injury to arms and shoulders and protect the heads of rear side occupants. Of all the different types of window bag, the drop-down type offers the best performance due to the extensive area covered and its ability to support itself even in the absence of a backing if the side windows break. Composition The window bag module consists of: a gas generator secured by mounts to the rear car pillar; a flexible pipe in permeable cloth secured by a band to the gas generator that diffuses the gas evenly over the entire length of the bag; a bag of about 48 litres in volume secured to the gas generator together with a flexible pipe. It is made out of nylon (PA 6.6) and folded inside a containment sleeve. When inflated, the bag is designed to ensure impact energy is correctly absorbed while maintaining the occupant´s head at an appropriate disatnce from the impact area. Once inflation is completed, gas is expelled immediately through the porous fabric. easy-opening plastic clips that secure the bag to the ceiling rail; a retaining belt that holds the bag in position once inflated; a connector for connection to the electrical system; a warning plate with instructions. Operation The module gas inflation generator is electrically activated by means of a signal from the NAB. Following this signal, a pyrotechnic activation is set off that causes the gas in the generator to expand. The expanding gas emerges through special openings and is distributed evenly along the length of the bag through the hose to make the bag inflate. the increase in bag volume causes the fastening container to break, the sleeve seams to yield and the trim to open. Everything is arranged so that the bag emerges correctly downward. The bag is made to inflate correctly by a retaining belt on the front end of the bag. When fully inflated, the bag is in an optimal position to protect the occupant. The bag deflates immediately after being inflated by the gas because the fabric is permeable.

INTRODUCTION The Body Computer Node (NBC) is an electronic component comprising a hardware base and a software - hardware interface (ILM). The NBC guarantees the following functions: - bodywork functions (lighting, visibility, memorizing, passenger compartment protection, etc.) - functions of connection between the various multiplate networks; - bridging functions between through and multiplate functions; - diagnostic functions; - acquiring data coming from the sensors; - distribute and protect power supplies to devices supplied through the body computer; - manage communication protocols of devices connected to the CAN networks. The NBC interfaces with the other vehicle nodes by means of three networks: - a multi-master type CAN known as an intersystems network (I.S.) which connects the NBC to the nodes which supervise the mechanics in general (engine management, ABS, information for the driver, etc.), - a second CAN network, multi-master type VAN known as a COMFORT network which connects the NBC to the information or comfort equipment. - a master/slave CAN network known as a CAR network that connects the NBC to the safety and service equipment. The NBC is also connected to some sensors and actuators and to the diagnostic socket. NBC ROLE AND FUNCTIONS The NBC carries out the following processing: - it manages the system operating status; - it runs the application program; - it loads codes and manages the diagnostic line; - it guarantees time management (timer and delays); - it communicates via the CAN networks; - it acquires direct inputs; - it allows the diagnosis of some direct outlets; - it provides power supplies. Nbc trim levels The are 3 possible different NBC configurations. In the low range configuration the NBC implements the following functions: - front electric windows; - heated seats; - automatic climate control with dusk and air temperature sensor; - central locking for the doors; - rear windscreen wiper. In the mid-range configuration the NBC implements the following functions: - automatic climate control with dusk and air temperature sensor; - front sill light (under the door), - front electric windows; - rear electric windows; - electric child locks; - heated seats; - central locking for the doors; - rear windscreen wiper. In the top of the range configuration the NBC implements the following functions: - rain sensor information management, - automatic switching on of the lights; - automatic climate control with dusk and air temperature sensor; - front sill light (under the door), - front electric windows; - rear electric windows; - electric child locks; - heated seats; - super locking; - rear windscreen wiper. Operating procedure The multiplexer offers four operating modes: - "inactive system", which corresponds to body computer off status; - "system in stand-by", which corresponds to key off status (absence of +15 signal); - "system active", which corresponds to staus of key inserted and turned to ON or START-UP (presence of +15 signal) during which all functions are active, particularly CAN network communication; - "system activating", defines the stage when the body computer is activated (this status includes software initialisation). ACTIVATED There are three ways to activate the body computer node: - activation via bus, which takes place using the remote control; - activation by turning the ignition key to ON or START-UP; - activation by manual operation of vehicle accesses or the passenger compartment lighting system. FORCED ELECTRICAL LOAD ACTIVATION/DEACTIVATION The NBC is equipped with a control function for the electrical loads to prevent overloading (deactivation of electrical consumers) or to force the engagement of the alternator (activation of electrical consumers). Forced deactivation of electric loads The load deactivation function is designed to prevent the battery from being run down or even destroyed through the application of temporary current interruptions. The NBC intervention levels are as follows: - level 0: no deactivation; - level 1: interruption of heater plugs power supply (if supplied for the function of the artificial regeneration of the particle filter), - level 2: interruption of engine cooling fan power supply, at medium speed (if supplied for the function of the artificial regeneration of the particulate filter), - level 3: interruption of engine cooling fan power supply, at medium speed (if supplied for the function of the artificial regeneration of the particulate filter), - level 4: interruption of the heated rear windscreen power supply (if supplied for the function of the artificial regeneration of the particle filter), - level 5: interruption of the power supply to the heated rear window (if the activation time exceeds six minutes) if authorised by the climate control node; - level 6: reduction in the climate control fan speed (with automatic climate control); - level 7: interruption of the compressor power supply (with automatic climate control). With a manually operated climate control system, the compressor is not switched off because the NBC does not recognize the climate control fan rotation speed. Forced activation of electric loads The forced activation of certain electrical loads required by the Engine Management Node for the regeneration of the particulate filter does not take priority. The forced activation levels are as follows: - level 0: no forced activation, - level 1: heated rear windscreen power supply; - level 2: power supply of engine cooling fan, low speed; - level 3: power supply of engine cooling fan, medium speed; - level 4: glow plug power supply. INTRODUCTION The engine compartment node is located on the right side of the actual engine compartment (near the windscreen washer fluid reservoir). NDVM FUNCTION The function of the engine compartment node is to protect and distribute the power supplies to the various functions via: - relays; - fuses; - minifuses; - maxi fuses. The NDVM consists of two combined modules (A and B): Module A (BOO1) consists of an electronic card that houses relays fuses and a microcontroller that communicates via the CAN network with body computer (M001). Module B contains the maxifuses (fuses with a high amp rating). The main functions of the NDVM are: - to distribute and protect (by means of fuses) the electrical power supplies of devices connected via the main wiring and engine wiring; - to supply an electrical power supply to the maxifuse casing. The clutch is single dry plate type, with a thrust bearing in permanent contact with the pressure spring. The driven plate is driven by pressure exercised by a diaphragm spring. The clutch release takes place via the hydraulic system operated by the pedal.

The system consists of: a clutch drip tray with diaphragm springs (1); a clutch operating cylinder (2) fastened to the gearbox; linkage (3) operating the thrust bearing; a reservoir (4) shared by the braking and clutch systems; a clutch pump (master cylinder (5) fastened to the pedals assembly that compresses the oil; a pipe connecting the pump and the clutch operating cylinder; a thrust bearing; a clutch plate; 1. Clutch plate 2. Clutch operating cylinder 3. Linkage 4. Brake/clutch fluid reservoir 5. Clutch pump

The pump (5), operated by the clutch pedal, pressurizes the hydraulic circuit and operates the clutch control cylinder (2). The latter acts on the linkage (3) which "pulls" the thrust bearing, overcoming the action of the pressure plate springs. This action causes the release of the clutch plate from the flywheel. When the pedal is released, the action of the diaphragm springs returns the mechanical to the original position. The vehicle interior has been designed and produced with the main aim of offering all the occupants the best that is available in terms of comfort and on board living conditions. With this in mind, in addition to taking particular care over the fundamental aspects: design, high specification level and ergonomics, a great deal of attention has been paid to everything that could contribute to making the consumer truly satisfied. FACIA The structure of the dashboard is in two separate sections: Upper arch Actual dashboard The standard dashboard is illustrated below 1 - Instrument panel: milometer display and warning lights 2 - Rev counter 3 - Speedometer 4 - Fuel gauge with reserve warning light and coolant temperature gauge and overheating warning light 5 - Passenger air bag 6 - Glove compartment 7 - Radio 8 - Automatic climate control system controls 9 - Hazard warning lights button 10 - Cigar lighter 11 - Coin holder 12 - Centre console 13 - Ashtray and oddments pocket 14 - Document holder 15 - Driver's air bag 16 - Headlamp alignment corrector (except versions with xenon headlamps) 17 - ASR system off/on The top of the range dashboard is illustrated below 1 - Instrument panel: milometer display and warning lights 2 - Speedometer 3 - Radio/Connect infotelematic system display 4 - Rev counter 5 - Passenger air bag 6 - Glove compartment 7 - Infotelematic system 8 - Automatic climate control system controls 9 - Hazard warning lights button 10 - Cigar lighter 11 - Connect infotelematic system remote controls 12 - Centre console 13 - Ashtray and oddments pocket 14 - Document holder 15 - Driver's air bag 16 - Headlamp alignment corrector (except versions with xenon headlamps) 17 - ASR system off/on Arc The section above consists of two half casings matched together by "welding" and then, in turn, fastened to the dashboard casing. The two half casings are produced by injecting polypropylene material to ensure good strength properties. The top part is dark grey with opaque embossing which provides it with a non reflective effect whilst the bottom section differs in appearance (aluminium coloured for FIAT and dark grey for LANCIA). Depending on the Marque and the version of the telematic system, there are two very different possible configurations for the instrument panel under the arch: panel with "3 spheres", i.e. 3 analagoue instruments which, located on the longitudinal axis of the vehicle, appear to be suspended from the arch. The three spheres respectively contain: speedometer, rev counter, fuel gauge/coolant temperature gauge. panel with 7" 16/9 colour screen. This instrument panel, which is part of the telematic system, changes the appearance of the dashboard considerably; in effect, the three spheres conceded their position to this single unit which contains the 7" 16/9 high definition colour screen in the centre with the speedometer to its left and the rev counter on its right. Dashboard The dashboard is in three pieces: main insert, front panel and lower panel, the latter is made from a soft foam material, covered in dark grey coloured laminte; the finished surface of the laminate gives it an opaque chrome effect which is aesthetically pleasing on the eye and pleasant to touch as well as having a non-glare effect. There are two oddments pockets with flaps on the horizontal part of the dashboard. As far as the interior of the dashboard is concerned, it is the component that differs the most between the FIAT and LANCIA versions. On FIAT vehicles it is covered with fabric: glove compartments on the horizontal part of the dashboard, passenger side glove compartment flap. On LANCIA vehicles the entire top section of the dashboard is covered in alcantara (horizontal section and front section). The following are inserted in the dashboard: Horizontal section: 2 closed compartments, 1 open compartment (only for the instrument panel with the Connect Nav +) Front section: 2 side ventilation vents and adjustment controls, 1 centre ventilation vent with three sections and adjustment controls, passenger air bag Lower section: ESP deactivation button (where fitted), headlamp alignment corrector, open oddments pocket (on the left of the steering column), passenger oddments pocket. The separation between the front section and the lower section of the dashboard is visually defined by the presence of a trim that continues along the door panels; in this case too, the LANCIA and FIAT versions differ both in appearance and materials: LANCIA: mahogany wood FIAT: plastic material with a satin chrome appearance. The lower section of the dashboard is made from a rigid material in the same colour as the upper section (dary grey). Centre console The upper section is the control area which contains: gear lever (manual or automatic transmission), climate control system controls and display, telematic system controls, hazard warning lights button, small grille (on the right) for the interior temperature sensor. The section straight underneath, which is retractable, contains: ashtray, which can be removed to become a glass holder, 1 glass holder, compartment for placing the cigar lighter (there is a cigar lighter/12V current socket at the side, on the passenger side). In the lower part of the console there is a refrigerated compartment with a flap that can house three cans. The console is made by polypropylene injection moulding. Door panels The door panels, like the dashboard, differ considerably between the FIAT and LANCIA versions: FIAT: the door panels have laminated perimeters, the same as the dashboard and a soft centre insert covered in the same fabric used on the dashboard and colour co-ordinated with the seats. LANCIA: the door panels have alcantara perimeters, continuing the theme of the covered sections of the dashboard and the centre section of the panel is covered in laminate with foam underneath. The front door panel houses: rigid oddments pocket grab handle/door pull electric windows control panel (driver's side: includes 2/4 control buttons, with a special safety design, automatic operation for opening all the windows and for closing the driver and passenger windows) electric child lock button 2 buttons for activating and adjusting the door mirror plastic door opening lever painted to give a metal effect speaker trim, in the lower front section lamp lighting the footwell area and the road (with the door open) reflector warning that the door is open The sliding door panel houses: rigid oddments pocket grab handle/door pull electric windows control panel electric windows control panel safety closing knob, remains flush in closed position Roof The ceiling and front pillar covers are covered in a light grey coloured fabric with a layer of soft foam underneath. Restraining nets (fitted as standard starting from Lev. 2): to prevent objects which would move around constantly whilst driving, a luggage restraining net is available which can be fastened using the rings located on the floor panel High load restraining net: this net, made from a semirigid plastic material, is located behind the 2nd row and is fastened through rings on the floor and the ceiling (hidden behind a cover); it has a safety function to prevent intrusions and is available as an option. SEATS The design of the shape of the seats have been developed with the main aim of providing even support for the entire body to ensure maximum comfort, especially on long journies. In addition, special technology has been used to match the cover and the upholstery which allows the stitching (which can be annoying to the touch) to be kept to a minimum and to produce much more interesting shapes than using conventional technology. This "in situ" technology basically consists of directly matching the defined shape, the foam and the cover during the moulding process. Front seats Backrest It has an ample concave curve and extensive support right up to shoulder level to wrap around the back evenly; lower down, the presence of an accentuated protrusion, supported by a strong spring located behind the foam, guarantees excellent lumbar support. The shape of the backrest created in this way prevents the rotation of the pelvis thereby guaranteeing that the spine is kept in the "S" shape; this configuration avoids the vertebra from coming into contact and compressing the discs. Side container This is sufficiently pronounced to guarantee that the curved shape is maintained but, at the same time, it is still possible to sit comfortably in the seat and, in the case of the rear seats, to move with ease from one seat to another. Cushion The length of the cushion has been designed to provide good support for the legs and ensure that the pedals can be easily reached and used, especially by those who are small in stature. Backrest with plastic shell The adoption of a plastic shell offers various advantages, such as: it does not get dirty when items are placed in the pocket at the bottom this does not disturb the occupant of the seat there is a small compartment at the top for a pen/pencil there is access to the inside of the backrest for servicing operations through a partial dismantling which takes less time In addition, the backrest is fitted with a retractable table with a glass holder. A - open backrest Head restraints The head restraints have two special features: the concave shape of the front section, the possibility of lengthwise adjustment, at the top, all designed to increase the surface area in contact with the nape of the neck, rather than the top of the head, resulting in being less tiring on the neck. The height adjustment (100 mm travel) is continous (no different stages) and effortless and can be done with one hand only. Height adjustment (driver only) This device allows easy and precise adjustment, irrespective of the weight of the driver. It can be extended by 50 mm and the position of the cushion changes during the adjustment, i.e.: the cushion assumes a horizontal position during an upwards adjustment, the rear of the cushion moves downwards during a downwards adjustment to be more comfortable for larger people. The adjustment lever is on the right hand side, halfway along the cushion and is horizontal when in the rest position. A - seat height adjustment lever Backrest angle adjustment The adjustment is carried out using a lever, located on the backrest, which allows the seat to be adjusted through an angle of 69° (- 19° / + 50°) B - seat angle adjustment lever Lumbar adjustment (driver only and level 2) This adjustment is carried out using a reduced travel lever (120° angle) which is more practical and easier than a knob. C - lumbar adjustment lever Reach adjustment This adjustment is carried out by raising the lever located under the cushion at the front; the travel for the adjustment is 200 mm (currently on the Ulysse/Zeta the travel is 150 mm). D - lengthwise adjustment lever Seat rotation (where fitted) The front seats can rotate through 180° which makes it possible to create a "lounge" configuration (which can obviously only be used when the vehicle is stationary). The operations that need to be carried out to produce this "lounge" configuration are: make sure that the seat height adjustment is over halfway so that the mechanical lock is exceeded (for the driver's seat) place the seat in the completely forward position and the backrest in a vertical position, then lift up lever E, located behind the lengthwise adjustment control, turning the seat at the same with the handbrake lever applied, the rotation of the driver's seat is limited to 180 °; button F must therefore be pulled forward and the lever lowered. The vehicle is, however, braked in this position. E - seat rotation release lever F - handbrake button Armrest (from level 2) This adjustment device in addition to being precise, allows the armrest to be placed in a horizontal position even when the backrest is tilted completely backwards (50° in relation to the vertical position). Proceed as follows to adjust the armrest: lift up the armrest and place it in position 1, lower the armrest until the end of travel position, position 2, lift up the armrest placing it in the desired position, position 3. Seat with heated cushion From level 1 onwards heated seats are available on request for the 1st row seats with the controls (three position) located on the right side of the seat. Electrical adjustments with memories There are three possible adjustment for the electric seats that can be memorized, namely: lengthwise height backrest angle the adjustment of the door mirrors are also memorized in conjunction with the seat adjustment. The memorizing system comprises: a special control unit incorporated in the seat which has two possible memories (M1/M2) 2 buttons for carrying out all the electrical adjustments 3 buttons on the right side of the driver's seat casing: button 1 for defining adjustment 1, button 2 for defining adjustment 2 and M for confirming the memorizing of positions 1 and 2 (which become M1 and M2), electronic system on the steering column switch unit which receives information from the seat control unit and compares it, when the door is opened using the remote control or the key is inserted, with that memorized by the specific control unit when the door is first shut. 1 - backrest angle adjustment 2 - seat height and lengthwise adjustment 3 - seat position memorizing contol panel 4 - seat heating regulator 12 Volt socket The 12V socket is located in the rear of the driver's seat casing and is easily accessible for the driver, 1st row passenger and the passenger in the centre of the 2nd row. The socket can be used for recharging a mobile phone, for connecting a baby bottle warmer or for connecting a games console (play station). Flexible belt Each seat ian the 1st row, from level 2 onwards, has a flexible belt attached to the casing that can be used to house objects like maps; in addition, the two belts (located on the left and right seats) can be attached between the two seats creating a flexible space where items such as bags or laptops can be placed. Rear seats The main new features compared with the current version of the Ulysse are: all the rear seats are the same size, including the middle one in the 2nd row (470 mm), the centre seat has an inertia reel belt, all the controls are dual (left and right sides), the lengthwise adjustment is continuous on guides, the lengthwise adjustment can be carried out from the next row, dual function folding control, seat packing on the left and right sides, backrest with plastic shell, retractable head restraint, ISOFEX fastenings. All the seats in the 2nd and 3rd rows can be easily extracted from the guides and are interchangeable; the middle seat in the 2nd row can therefore even be relocated to the 3rd row on the left (area with a reinforced floor). Backrest angle adjustment This operation is carried out using the lever on either the left or right side of the backrest which allows a rapid adjustment through an angle of 69° (-40° / +65°). To carry out the adjustment, whilst remaining seated, lift up lever A and place the backrest in the desired position, then release the lever. A - backrest adjustment lever Reach adjustment This adjustment is carried out using the lever under the cushion at the front which allows the seat to slide on aluminium guides through a travel of 150 mm (current versions of the Ulysse/Zeta have two fixed positions, 120 mm apart). For the adjustment of the rear seats, lift lever B then move the seat forwards or backwards until the desired position is reached. The second row seat can be slid lengthwise, from the third row, by pulling handle C and moving the seat at the same time. B - lengthwise adjustment lever (front) C - lengthwise adjustment lever (rear) Seat folding To faciliate access to the 3rd row, all the rear side seats are fitted with a control (a small lever located on both the left and the right on the backrest) which folds the seat in a single manoeuvre. The seat remains in position, even whilst driving, thanks to a spring. The operation of folding the seat can be carried out easily in one go. For the third row seats: to get in from the outside, lift up lever A from the outside and fold the complete seat forwards, to get out, lift lever D and fold the seat forwards. A - seat folding lever (backrest adjustment) D - seat folding lever (rear) Seat with backrest folded over into horizontal position If you wish to place the backrest in a horizontal position, proceed as follows: Side seats: place the seat in the folded position and then turn the seat backwards or gently operate the control (located on the left/right of the backrest) which releases the backrest and place it in a horizontal position Centre seat: adjust the backrest release control located at the top of the backrest in the centre E - backrest folding lever Dual function control for "wallet" configuration The side seats in the 2nd and 3rd rows are fitted with a control, located on the right near the backrest/cushion adjustment, which allows two functions to be carried out in quick succession: firstly, releasing the seat rear feet from the guides, then continuing to rotate the seat it assumes the "wallet" configuration; whilst adjusting the head restraints, if they are in the raised position, they retract with the seat forwards. Before bing placed in a horizontal position and later on, by pulling the handle, positioned behind at the bottom on the left, the centre seat rotates and assumes the "wallet" position. The "wallet" configuration produced in this way remains stable, even whilst driving, thanks to the opposing force of a spring, whilst a belt is used connected to the head restraint of the middle seat in the 2nd row; this prevents the sudden and unwanted fall of the seat onto the guides. This control with a kinematic motion makes a normally complicated movement simple: the operation can be carried out quickly and with minimum effort, the head restraint does not have to be placed in the rest position because, at the time of folding over, the head restraint is retracted into the seat backrest. In addition, when loading luggage, access can be gained from the luggage compartment to the 3rd row seats by placing them in the "wallet" position using the handle at the bottom left and, as a result, the capacity of the luggage compartment can be increased through a quick, simple manoeuvre. Seat packaging on one side The arrangement of the sliding guides, used for the lengthwise adjustment, has been designed to allow "packing" of the four seats, in a row, behind the front seats (on both sides) after they have been folded over. Seat lifting control All the rear seats have a control at the rear of the seat (lever at the bottom right) which allows the seat to be raised from behind (see rear seat folding). Rear backrest The plastic shell on the backrest has two housings for two cans and a larger area (~ A4) with the backrest folded. The height adjustment is continuous and can be carried out using one hand. To lower the head restraint simply push the top part forward and then press downward: this operation can be done with one hand. A - head restraint release mechanism Side seat seat belt adjustment The seat belt mountings for the 1st and 2nd rows are adjustment by pressing the knob and, at the same time, moving the ring (on the centre pillar) up or down; the mounting for the 3rd row is fixed. CLEANING SEATS Cloth or velour seats Remove dust and foreign matter using a vacuum cleaner and then a dampened brush made from natural bristles. Alternatively, adhesive roller brushes can be used to remove any foreign bodies. Rub the seats with a sponge soaked in a solution of neutral detergent and water. The use of special products available on the market is recommended for the removal of any grease marks, taking special care to follow the instructions. The formation of down on velour is not a sign of any defect/wear: this effect is caused by static electricity and can be removed by cleaning appropriately. Leather or alcantara seats Remove dry dirt using either a chamois leather or a slightly dampened cloth without rubbing too hard. Remove any liquid or grease stains using an absorbent dry cloth, without rubbing. Then go over with a dry cloth or chamois leather dampened with neutral soap foam and water. If the stain persists, use special products taking care to follow the instructions. Never use alcohol or alcohol based products.

The vehicle comes with manual and automatic gear levers positioned on the central console. This new location is very user-friendly, leaves room to pass between the two front seats and also allows passengers to move easily between the 1st and 2nd rows. Three different types of manual gearboxes are available according to the different engine types, namely: BE4 type 5 speed manual gearbox for the 2.0 16v engine; ML5C type 5 speed manual gearbox for the 2.0 16v JTD engine; ML6C type 5 speed manual gearbox for the 2.2 16v JTD engine. The clutch is hydraulically operated for these types of gearboxes to ensure that minimum effort is required and to prolong its life. Two different types of automatic transmissions are available according to the different engine types, namely: AL4 type manual gearbox for the 2.0 16v engine; 4HP20 type automatic transmission for the 3.0 V6 24v engine;

INTRODUCTION - ZF 4HP20 AUTOMATIC GEARBOX - View of ZF4HP20 automatic gearbox 1, Automatic gearbox assembly 2, Automatic gearbox components DESCRIPTION The ZF 4HP20 automatic gearbox, with 4 forward speeds plus reverse, is operated completely by means of electro-hydraulic devices. This type of gearbox has been designed to be fitted on front wheel drive vehicles with transversely mounted engines and has an electronic management system connected, via the CAN line, to the engine management and ABS electronic control units. A management programme, in the electronic control unit, makes it possible to use the gearbox both fully automatically and manually (sequential). Identification The automatic gearbox is identified by a plate (1) rivetted to the casing that contains the serial number (A), the ZF code (B), the component reference (C) and the type of gearbox (D). 1, Plate A, serial number; B, ZF code (the last 3 digits); C, component reference; D, type of automatic transmission. VIEW OF ASSEMBLY 1, Gearbox casing 2, Oil filler plug 3, Torque converter 4, Gear selector shaft 5, Electro-hydraulic unit cover 6, Electrohydraulic unit 7, Position sensor 8, Heat exchanger AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION ASSEMBLY INTRODUCTION The ZF 4HP20 gearbox is fully automatic and electro-hydraulically operated with 4 forward speeds plus reverse. It is equipped with an electronic control system connected, via a CAN line, to the engine management control unit and the ABS control unit. The automatic transmission electronic control system logic is contained in an electronic control unit that manages: - the torque converter, - the gear changes, - the specific programmes. The control system makes it possible to use the gearbox either fully automatically or sequentially manually. The management is self-adaptive, i.e. capable of adjusting to the driving style of the driver. This makes it possible to transmit power continuously, with very rapid gear engagement times (electro-hydraulic). The electronic control unit is connected: - to the various sensors and actuators, - to the engine management ECU, - to the ABS control unit, - to the selector lever. This information is processed and sent to the instrument panel/display to show the various operating conditions. CONSTRUCTION SPECIFICATIONS The gearbox is equipped with a hydrodynamic torque converter with an anti-slip device that makes it possible to produce reduction gear ratios. This gearbox has the special feature of operating without a free wheel because the gear shift takes place by means of overlapping the couplings in order to allow: - increased compactness and a reduction in weight, - improved output due to the reduction in friction losses, - lower torque points on the components and on the kinematic chain. - Cross section of gearbox-differential unit 1, Input shaft 2, Torque converter 3, Oil pump 4, Brake F 5, Electrohydraulic unit 6, Gearbox output rpm sensor 7, Brake d 8, Brake C 9, Clutch B 10, Gearbox input rpm sensor 11, Clutch E 12, Second epicyclic satellite gears 13, First epicyclic satellite gears 14, Centre cylindrical gear 15, Gear for parking lock 16, Intermediate shaft 17, Differential OPERATION The electronic management of the gearbox makes it possible to produce gear changes that are suited to the temporary specifications of the engine with a certain degree of flexibility. The control unit has the task of: - adjusting the oil pressure to the engine torque for the gear change, - implementing the safety functions, - defining the gear change programme, - carrying out the system fault diagnosis. - The following signals are used by the control unit for managing these operating logics: - engine rpm (via the engine management control unit), - throttle position (via the engine management control unit), - engine temperature (via the engine management control unit); - converter turbine number of revs - gearbox output number of revs - vehicle speed (A.B.S.), - transmission fluid temperature, - gear selector lever position, - accelerator pedal position (kick-down, via the engine management control unit) - brake pedal position (A.B.S.). - Diagram showing information entering/leaving the control unit 1, Gearbox shaft input rpm sensor 2, Gearbox output rpm sensor 3, Driver's door switch 4, Gearbox oil temperature sensor 5, ABS control unit/CAN line 6, Engine management control unit/CAN line 7, Water/oil cooling fan 8, Display 9, Control panel 10, Buzzer control 11, Solenoid valves MV1 - MV2 12, Lever in P release control (shift-lock) 13, Pressure regulators REG1 - REG2 - REG3 - REG4 14, Ignition key extraction release control (key-lock) 15, Diagnostic socket 16, Switch on gear lever recognizing automatic/manual management 17, Selector lever position sensor (P - R - N - D) 18, Starting enablement 19, Reversing lights control Gear shift program The winter programme can be selected, in poor grip conditions, using the special button. Through this programme the control unit ensures that the vehicle sets off in second gear and later on it manages the engagement of the gears using a special map. The electronic control unit also contains the following programmes: Manual operation (tip) The Tip function makes it possible to use the gearbox manually. Moving the gear selector: - forwards (+) produces an increase in the gear (shift-up); - backwards (-) produces a downwards gear change (shift-down). Each time the gear control lever is moved only one gear change is carried out: commands are not cumulative. The control unit inhibits a gear change if the gearbox output shaft rpm, measured by the gearbox output rpm inductive sensor, is not within the levels set by the programme to prevent the engine going beyond or below the permitted revs. Warm-up programme (wml) This is a programme derived from a special configuration of the SKT programme that contributes in helping the engine reach operating temperature quickly adapting the gear change points according to the temperature of the engine. It is activated, after starting, if the temperature of the engine coolant is below 30°C and remains activated up to 34°C. High transmission fluid temperature safety programme (skt) This programme is activated when the temperature of the transmission fluid reaches 120°C and remains activated up to 117°C. There are both shift-up and shift-down gear change inhibition functions in this programme. The control unit implements the following strategies to facilitate the cooling of the transmission fluid: - it activates the lock-up clutch to reduce the Jaule effect in the converter, - it sends information on the oil temperature to the engine management control unit, via the CAN line, to manage the cooling fan. Safety functions The gearbox electronic control unit implements and manages the safety functions described below. Inhibition of the gear change when cornering The control unit inhibits a change to a higher gear (shift-up) in the case of strong transverse acceleartion, for example, when cornering, with the accelerator pedal released very rapidly. The system enters the "engine lock" mode maintaining the last ratio selected. When the critical conditions are over, the automatic programme is automatically restored. This strategy allows: - improved vehicle stability, - responsive acceleration when coming out of a bend because the vehicle is in the ideal gear. Change to a lower gear (shift-down) whilst braking In the case of emergency or quick braking, the control unit selects the lowest possible gear to produce the maximum engine braking effect. The automatic downshift depends on: - type of braking, - gradient of the road, - type of driving (degree of sportiness) Shift-lock A safety system locks the gear selector in position P until, with the ignition ON, the brake pedal is pressed at the same time as the enablement button, on the gear lever grip. In case of a failure, there is a manual release safety system. 1, Gear control lever 2, Enablement button Key-lock The key can only be extracted from the ignition switch with the selector lever in position P and a within 25 seconds of the key-off. In case of a failure, there is a manual release safety system. 1, Ignition key 2, Ignition switch Buzzer A special buzzer warns the driver: - for maximum period of 15 seconds if the gear selector lever is in a position other than P when driver's door is opened; - when the engine is operating beyond the correct revs with the gearbox in a manual position; - when reverse gear is engaged with the doors closed for a period of 4 seconds. Beyond revs This function avoids damage to the engine through too high a rotation speed. The Automatic Transmission electronic control unit sets a higher gear before the speed becomes too high or it prevents (delays) the shift to a lower gear to avoid a similar risky situation. Start-up The engine can only be started up with the selector lever in position "N" or "P". Reverse gear Reverse gear cannot be engaged, with the selector lever in position "R", if the vehicle speed is above a certain level (8 km/h). When the speed goes below the set level, reverse gear is engaged and remains engaged even if the speed later exceeds the set level. The reversing lights come on and the buzzer is activated with the lever in position "R". Gearbox failure warning light A single warning light in the control panel signals: - transmission fluid overheating with the warning light on constantly (on when the fluid temperature is >140°C and off with the fluid temperature <137°C); - automatic transmission failure with the warning light flashing (on for 4 seconds and then flashing); - system working efficiently (on for 4 seconds at the key-on and then off). Parking It is only possible engage the selector lever in position "P" with the vehicle stationary or the speed of the vehicle below a certain level (4 - 6 km/h). A shift-lock system locks the gear lever when it is in position "P" until the brake pedal and the button on the gear lever are pressed with the ignition ON. In case of a failure, there is a manual release safety system. AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION COMPONENTS INTRODUCTION - View of main gearbox components 1, Gearbox casing 2, Torque converter 3, Electrohydraulic unit 4, Position sensor 5, Heat exchanger DESCRIPTION Torque converter It is fitted between the engine and the gearbox in place of the conventional disc clutch. The torque converter consists of: 1, a casing containing the oil and various components; 2, a pump impeller connected to the crankshaft and to the oil pump; 3, a turbine impeller connected to the gearbox input shaft; 4, a stator, fitted on the free wheel, with the task of directing the flow of oil towards the pump impeller; 5, a lock-up device; 6, friction gasket. The hydro-dynamic torque converter has the function of ensuring a (hydraulic) connection between the engine and the gearbox with the advantage of even torque transmission without jerking. Where appropriate, a torque converter locking device (lock-up), operated by the control unit by means of a solenoid valve (MV2) and a regulation solenoid valve (REG3) mechanically connects the gearbox to the engine flywheel excluding the hydro-dynamic function. The operation of the converter takes place in the following stages: - converter stage, where the torque is multiplied, - coupling stage, where the torque is transmitted 98% to 100% depending on whether the lock-up is activated or not. Operation As soon as the engine is started the pump impeller (1) behaves like a centrifugal pump and the oil is thrust by centrifugal force into the radial ducts. The oil that comes out of the pump impeller vanes is directed to the turbine impeller (2) where it flows through the ducts from the outside towards the centre. In these circumstances, if the oil flows directly onto the pump impeller, it comes into contact with the vanes in the opposite direction to its direction of rotation. 1, Pump impeller 2, Turbine impeller To avoid this, there is a stator (3) between the two impellers. The stator is designed to divert the flow of oil to the pump impeller (1) in the same direction of rotation. In this way the energy from the oil directed to the pump impeller inlet is added to the kinetic energy of the impeller at that time. 1, Pump impeller 2, Turbine impeller 3, Stator The greater the difference in speed between the pump impeller (1) and the turbine, the greater the multiplication of the torque (max. with turbine stationary). When the turbine impeller starts to pick up speed the multiplication of the torque gradually decreases. A, During starting B, Intermediate speed C, Coupling stage 1, Pump impeller 2, Turbine impeller 3, Stator LV, Engine flywheel side LC, Gearbox/differential side Lock-up clutch This function checks or locks the sliding between the pump impeller and the turbine impeller. If the oil were the only element transferring torque, there would always be a difference in the number or revs between the pump impeller and the turbine impeller known as "sliding". To prevent this condition the torque converter is fitted with a lock-up device, managed by the control unit by means of a regulation solenoid valve (REG3) and a solenoid valve (MV2) which, by reversing the flow of the oil in the converter, activates the lock-up device. There are three operating states for the device: - open state (see the paragraph on the operation of the torque converter, described previously); - closed state in which, with all sliding between the pump impeller and the turbine impeller prevented, the torque is transmitted in its entirety from the engine to the gearbox; The pressure of the oil thrusts the sliding device (2) towards the wall of the converter casing (1), activating the locking of the sliding between the pump impeller (4) and the turbine impeller (3) through the effect of a fricition gasket (5). - Lock up device in closed state 1, Gearbox casing 2, Lock-up device 3, Turbine impeller 4, Pump impeller 5, Friction gasket operated state, the control unit maintains controlled sliding between the pump and the turbine. - Lock up device in operated state Oil pump The oil pump, fitted between the torque converter and the gearbox casing, if the geared type and is operated by the converter pump impeller. The pressurized oil controls the gear engagement and lubricates the various gears. The pump comprises two eccentric gears: - drive gear (6) with outside teeth, - driven gear (7) with inside teeth. The two gears are housed in a pump casing (3) which contains an asymmetric partition to produce two different chambers: an intake chamber (1) and a supply chamber (2). 1, Intake chamber 2 - Drainage chamber 3, Pump casing 4, Washer 5, Gasket 6, Drive gear (operated by the torque converter pump impeller) 7, Driven gear 8, Centering pin Clutches There are two oil-bath multiple disc clutches in the gearbox alternately comprising: - driven discs (2) covered in high friction coefficient material, - steel drive discs (1). The coupling between the drive and driven discs takes place by means of a hydraulically operated piston (3). The release takes place by means of a release disc spring (4). 1, Drive discs 2, Driven discs 3, Piston 4, Release spring 5, Input shaft 6, Disc carrier plate Brakes There are three oil bath multiple disc type braking units in the gearbox. The only difference is that the drive discs do not transmit torque to the driven discs because the latter form one piece with the gearbox casing. INTRODUCTION The vehicle is fitted with an AL4 automatic transmission and differential with four speeds and reverse specially designed for front-wheel drive, transverse-engined vehicles. It belongs to the category of epicyclic gearboxes with a hydraulic torque converter electronically controlled by a microprocessor control unit. The self-adaptive automatic transmission features two operating programs. 1st Program: self-adaptive with electronic control The transmission adapts permanently to the driver's driving style and service conditions, depending on road profile and vehicle load. The control unit chooses the most suitable speed transfer law from a range of 9: 3 driving style laws: these three laws refer to the driver's driving style (economic law, medium law, dynamic law) and are activated according to the driver's action on the accelerator pedal. 3 laws relating to road profile: these three laws refer to road profile (slight hill, steep hill, descent). When these are active, they preferentially select lower ratios and take priority over the driving style laws, with the exception of the dynamic law that takes priority over the slight hill and descent. 3 theoretical condition transfer laws: low temperature law: this activated during cold starts to ensure the gear casing is in the best possible conditions (oil temperature increase). High temperature law: this is activated when the engine/gear casing temperature becomes high yet not high enough to require the driver to be alerted. Anti-emission law: this is activated due to an increase in catalytic converter temperature. The self-adaptive program is selected automatically when the engine is started (with the economic law). Snow program. When the snow button located to the left of the lever is pressed (snowflake symbol), a program is activated that prevents the front wheels sliding during take-off or acceleration. 2nd Sequential program: This program allows the driver to shift gears (1 to 4) directly as with a manual gearbox. From the self-adaptive program drive position (D), the driver may access the sequential program at any time, and viceversa. To do this, the gear lever is simply moved to the right. The speed is shifted by pressing the lever: forward to shift up, backward to shift down. While in the sequential program, the snow program is inactive but take-off is possible while in the second or third speed. The system is able to download the following parameters through specific sensors and interface with the Engine Control Node: engine rpm; engine load; coolant temperature; gearbox input speed; gearbox output speed; transmission fluid temperature; transmission fluid pressure; selector lever position; program selection (if applicable); throttle position and drift; brake operation (if applicable); battery voltage; The control unit memory contains a management program (software) that includes a set of strategies, each of which manages a very specific system control function. Each strategy uses the information (input) described above to process a set of parameters based on data maps stored in specific areas of the control unit. The strategy then controls the system actuators (output), i.e.the devices that allow the vehicle to operate, namely: sequential solenoids; modulation solenoids; exchanger solenoid; electromagnetic actuators; control relays; interface with Engine Control Node; interface with the vehicle (system failure warning light, diagnostic tester, instruments and controls) The automatic transmission may be schematically subdivided into three main units: HYDRO-MECHANICAL UNIT, consisting of: an oil-dynamic torque converter with a dynamicallyi-controlled lock-up clutch; two epcyclic gear trains interconnected in cascade formation that implement the various transmission ratios; a hydraulically-controlled brake and clutch set that creates the locks between the various components required to obtain the four forward speeds and reverse; a selector lever with a gearbox parking lock when the selector lever is in position P; an oil pump that supplies the necessary hydraulic pressure to the entire system; ELECTROHYDRAULIC UNIT, consisting of: a hydraulic lock that contains the clutch and brake control circuits; a set of solenoids controlled by the NCA that cut out the hydraulic circuit as appropriate. an oil-water heat exchanger to cool the oil with a by-pass solenoid. CONTROL UNIT, consisting of: a microprocessor control unit; a set of sensors for acquiring the parameters required for gearbox operation; interfaces with the vehicle (diagnosis, instruments and controls, control buttons). To avoid an untimely set-off due to involuntary action of the gear control lever, the automatic transmission is equipped with a Shift Lock that obliges the driver to press the driver to press the brake pedal to leave the parking position. The "foot+brake pedal" symbol on the selection grid reminds the driver of the obligatory procedure for leaving parking position. In the sequential system: + to shift up, - to shift down Information to the driver The driver is informed of the automatic transmission operating mode by means of a display that shows the following information: gear lever position, program selected by the driver, poorly-positioned gear lever (lever between two stable positions: the last stable position engaged flashes). Advantages of the self-adaptive gearbox: 1st adapts to the driving system of each driver, 2nd in the case of steep descents: a normal gearbox shifts from 3rd to 4th when speed increases but with a self-adaptive transmission the computer registers the speed increase but also the fact that the accelerator pedal is raised and therefore uses the engine brake. 3rd during emergency braking: when the accelerator pedal is raised, the engine brake is activated in real time and does not allow a longer ratio. The gearbox shifts down as soon as the brake pedal is pressed. Clutch E1 E2 - Clutch E2 F1 - Brake F1 F2 - Brake F2 F3 - Brake F3 Main components of hydromechanical unit Torque converter The torque converter transmits power from the engine to the gearbox hydraulically and inceases torque when the vehicle is accelerating. Rotary motion is transmitted to the epicylic gear set via two propeller shafts: the crankshaft connected to the converter pump via the flywheel; the gearbox mainshaft that engages with the converter turbine hub. P - Pump S - Stator T - Turbine The converter consists of a pump P integral with the crankshaft, turbine t, integral with the gearbox mainshaft and stator S integral with the outer gear casing. The converter is full of fluid that allows transmission of drive torque due to the kinetic energy expended by the pump. The torque converter is not subject to any type of wear because there is no mechanical link between the driven part and the drive part. Impeller P is connected to the crankshaft and acts a pump when turned clockwise to transfer its energy to the fluid. The centrifugal force pushes the fluid toward the outside of the impeller where it flows at high speed toward turbine T. Here the kinetic energy of the fluid imposes a clockwise rotary motion to the turbine. The fluid then passes through stator S, where it is diverted through an angle that allows it return to the pump with high efficiency. The stator is connected to the gear casing by means of a idler wheel engagement that prevents it turning anticlockwise and supplies a reaction torque proportional to the fluid flow diversion, which is added to that of the turbine. The ratio between the torque acting on the turbine and the torque supplied by the pump is known as the torque multiplication ratio and is proportional to the difference in rotating speed between pump and turbine. When the wheels are still, the torque approximately double that delivered by the engine. As turbine speed increases, torque multiplication reduceds continuously and tends toward a 1:1 ratio. This corresponds to a turbine speed equal to 80-90% of pump speed. When turbine and pump speeds are almost the same, the stator is struck by an fluid flow that is angled to a degree that causes the direction of rotation to reverse. Because it is not locked by the idler wheel, it turns clockwise without impediment and the torque converter acts as an ordinary hydraulic coupling. Lock-up clutch A lock up clutch is a device that creates a mechanical link betwen the converter input and output when engaged, i.e. between the pump, integral with the crankshaft and the turbine, integral with the epicyclic gears. When the lock up clutch is engaged, pump (P) and turbine (T) cease to slide in relation to one another to convert the gearbox into a manual transmission. This eliminates viscous friction loss in the torque converter. This leads to a reduction in fuel consumption and the clutch slipping sensation typical of hydraulic transmissions that is caused by the difference between engine speed and vehicle speed. Operation Clutch released The fluid flowing inside the converter acts with the same pressure on the rear and front side of clutch engagement piston (1): turbine (T) is free to turn in relation to the cover of the converter, integral with pump (P). Clutch engaged The NCA controls the EVM solenoid that brings about a pressure reduction at the rear so that piston (1) slides to lock the clutch. Turbine (T) is therefore connected to pump (P) and they cease to slide in relation to one another. During speed shifts, the lock-up clutch is controlled in modulated manner. During this stage, pressure in the area is modulated in order to allow controlled slide between pump and turbine, which is very reduced. Engine driver torque delivery irregularities are absorbed by a set of damping springs (2) arranged along the outside of the converter casing. These operate in a similar manner to ensure optimum driving comfort. Epicyclic gear set The gearbox offers five transmission ratios (four forward speeds and reverse) by means of two simple epicylic gear sets that are designated gear set 1 and gear set 2 respectively. These gear sets are interconnected so that differential gear C1 is integral with gear train carrier PS2 and differential gear is integral with gear train carrier PS1. The various ratios are obtained by transmitting drive torque via certain parts of the assembly while locking others. The torque input is via gear train carrier PS1, differential gear C1 or both, while the output is always from gear train carrier PS2. Control elements The gear set control elements comprise the brakes (that prevent a gear element and the outer casing from turning in relation to one another) and the clutches (that prevent two parts of the gear set from turning in relation to one another). These are controlled to achieve four forward speeds and one reverse. They are locked hydraulically by oil under pressure and unlocked through the mechanical action of a cup spring that acts on the piston. The oil bath operating system allows drive torque to be transmitted with practically no wear. these parts do not therefore require periodic adjustment. The clutches are all multiplate type. The brakes are all multiplate type (F1) or band type (F2) and (F3). They consist of a set of alternate steel plates (1) that are coated in friction material (2) and used on bell housing (3) and hub (4) respectively. clutch released (plates not transmitting torque) because there is no pressure in chamber (5), operating piston (6) is held back by return spring (7). clutch engaged (plates do not transmit torque) oil under pressure is sent via channel (8) connected to the control solenoid: the pressure causes the piston to move, overcome the spring pressure and compress the plates to prevent them turning in relation to one another. Operation - brakes The multiplate brakes work in exactly the same way as the clutches. The band-type brakes consist of a steel band (1) that is wound on a drum (2) integral with the part of the gear set to be locked. Brake released (the drum is not locked): since there is pressure in chamber (3), operating piston (4) is held back by return spring (5) so that there is clearance between band (1) and the drum. Brake engaged (drum locked) oil under pressure is sent via a channel connected to the control solenoid: the pressure causes the piston to move, overcome the spring pressure and lock the drum to prevent it turning. Parking lock ( shift-lock) The gearbox is fitted with a shift-lock safety function to lock the vehicle. This operates by means of electromagnetic actuator (1) located in the selector lever turret and controlled by the NCA: when the actuator is not activated: the selector lever can be moved to position P; the lever cannot be moved from position P (vehicle locked). The actuator is supplied in accordance with the following strategy: actuator not supplied with key OFF (engine off) actuator supplied with key ON and brake pedal operated. Engine start-up is possible only with the selector lever in N or P position. 1 - electromagnetic actuator Oil pump The oil pump is internal gear type. It is located between the torque converter and the gear casing and is driven directly by the converter pump impeller.
