Fully automatic operation (selector in position D) In this situation, the control system manages gear changes (engagement of higher gears) or downward gear shifts (engagement of lower gear) as a result of certain actions or situations, in particular: it engages a higher speed if: the driver presses the accelerator pedal and the vehicle accelerates the driver releases the accelerator pedal after kick-down resistant torque falls while driving the driving style learnt by the system is changed (less sporty) the speed engaged is maintained: if the accelerator pedal is released rapidly throughout the release stroke it engages a lower speed if: if the driver makes a kick-down manoeuvre the driver presses the brake pedal resistant torque increases while driving the driving style learnt by the system is changed (more sporty) Manual operation (Selector in +/- position) The driver can change speed by moving the selector lever up (+, gear change) or down (- downward shift). The system naturally maintains all control settings required to safeguard and protect the gearbox and engine from incorrect manoeuvres. the system notifies the driver that vehicle driving conditions will not allow engagement of the selected speed by making a warning light on the dashboard flash. Gear shift laws The gearbox control system determines whether or not to implement the lock-up clutch automatically and thus shift through the various speeds in accordance with certain stored objectives. The system decides whether or not to shift from one speed to another on the basis of a set of shift laws stored in the node. Each shift law consists a set of curves calculated on the basis of two parameters: accelerator pedal position; Vehicle speed. Each gear shift law contains: upward (shift up) and downward (shift down) shift curves for all speeds; lock-up clutch engagement and release curves; kick-down intervention points. The following figure shows an example of a gear shift law. v - vehicle speed (km/h) a - accelerator pedal position (%) (1) - example 1 (2) - example 2 A - shift 2-1 B - shift 1-2 C - shift 3-2 D - shift 2-3 E - shift 3-4 F - shift 4-3 + - kick-down points Any gearbox service point can be identified by means of two parameters: accelerator pedal position; Vehicle speed. When the gearbox instantaneous service point intersects a curve, the system makes the gear shift associated with the intersected curve. When speed is increasing, the upward shift curve is naturally considered (gear change), while the downward shift curve (shift down) is considered when the speed decreases. Example 1: accelerator pedal pressed through 80% of its travel; ratio engaged: 3rd speed; the gearbox shifts from 3rd to 4th as soon as speed increases to 100 km/h. Example 2: accelerator pedal pressed through 80% of its travel; ratio engaged: 4th speed; the gearbox shifts from 4th to 3rd as soon as speed increases to 72 km/h. the same principle applies for lock-up clutch engagement/release curves. Management strategies Management strategies must identify the shift law best suited to the contingent vehicle operating situation. It must also implement a set of actions in specific cases. The main gearbox management strategies are as follows: self-adaptive strategies (normal service conditions); sport strategy (high-performance service conditions); snow strategy (low ground grip conditions); lock-up clutch lock inhibition strategy (start-up or overheated clutch); warm-up strategy; gearbox thermal protection strategy (transmission fluid overheated). Self-adaptive strategies These are the strategies normally used by the system, which is able to learn external conditions (vehicle and driver) and adapt gear shifts accordingly. Six different speed shift laws may be identified: three laws determined by driver behaviour three laws determined by vehicle conditions. The three laws determined by driver behaviour are as follows: ECO law, MEDIUM law, SPORT law. These are mainly determined on the basis of the following parameters: throttle position; throttle movement speed; average throttle position within a certain time range; gearbox output speed changes. The laws determined by vehicle conditions are as follows: BRAKING 1 law, BRAKING 2 law, DESCENT law. These are mainly determined on the basis of the following parameters: throttle position; vehicle acceleration; Vehicle speed. The NCA selects the most appropriate point according to a strategy that is roughly summarised in the following table. driving conditions vehicle driving conditions descent flat slight hill steep hill normal DESCENT ECO BRAKING 1 BRAKING 2 lively DESCENT MEDIUM BRAKING 1 BRAKING 2 sporty SPORT SPORT SPORT BRAKING 2 The self-adaptive strategies also feature certain operating details: gear shift inhibition when the accelerator is released quickly: this function prevents the gearbox shifting to a higher speed when the accelerator is released to maintain the engine brake effect. It is also enabled with DESCENT shift laws when the accelerator is released. temporary increase in sportiness: if the system suddenly detects accelerator pedal movement, a shift law that is sportier from the current law is temporarily selected - from the driver-determined selection - (i.e. from ECO to MEDIUM or from MEDIUM to SPORT); downward shifting during braking: the system can detect braking intensity by assessing vehicle deceleration. The shortest ratio compatible with instantaneous driving conditions is therefore engaged to achieve maximum engine braking effect. Snow strategy This is activated by pressing the relevant button. The following operating features are displayed: selector in position D; 1st speed engagement inhibition; more widely-spaced gear ratios; enablement of kick-down only for speeds below 15 km/h; compulsory shift to lower speed when brake pedal operated. Lock-up clutch lock strategy This strategy involves torque converter operation with the lock-up clutch off. It is activated under the following conditions: with transmission fluid temperature lower than 0°C upon start-up to promote fluid heating; when the lock-up clutch overheats (determined by means of NCA software, mainly on the basis of engine load, number of engagements/releases over a period and the current shift law); in the case of lock-up clutch failure. Warm-up strategy The warm-up strategy helps the catalytic converter warm up faster and is implemented under the following conditions: transmission fluid temperature between 15°C and 30°C upon start-up; at the end of the lock-up clutch lock strategy. The strategy lasts for a timed period that depends on the vehicle engine type. Gearbox thermal protection strategies The transmission fluid high temperature safety program is automatically selected with transmission fluid temperatures higher than 120°C and is maintained until the temperature drops below 110°C. While this program is active, specific functions are introduced that can inhibit upward or downward gear changes and keep the lock-up clutch engaged for longer than normal to ensure fluid cooling. interface with Engine Control Node The engine control and gearbox control systems communicate with one another to optimise vehicle operation. a) from engine control to gearbox control: throttle position information: it is used mainly to detect idling and over-run situations and also manage the kick-down function, engine speed information: this is mainly used to determine the torque converter slide stage (comparison with gearbox input signal) and manage protection and gear shift strategies, drive torque information (engine load): this is used mainly to determine line pressure and manage gear shift strategies, b) from gearbox control to engine control: torque reduction request: used to ensure smoother shifts, multifunction switch information: used to establish engine idle speed under the various gearbox conditions with the vehicle at a standstill. Device for determining fluid wear level The system is fitted with a counter that is increased whenever the Automatic Transmission Node is supplied electrically. The counter can count up to 32768 units (32kbytes) corresponding to about 6000 hours of operation with fluid temperature at 95 °C. The counter is further increased, for the same time period, on the basis of fluid temperature to take into account the extra ageing caused by the high temperatures. When the counter is full, the snow and sport warning lights flash simultaneously. The value memorized by the counter can be changed, in the following cases, using the EXAMINER in the specific section for the gearbox: 1) Replacing the automatic transmission In this case the calculator must be completely zeroed 2) Replacing the calculator In this case it is vital to make a note of the value of the old counter and rememorize it in the new one 3) Adding new oil In this case for every half litre of new oil added, remove 2750 units from the value memorized in the counter Multifunction switch The switch is coaxial with the gear selection axle connected to the selector lever. It performs the following functions: it displays lever position on the instrument panel; engine start-up is possible only if the lever is in P or N position; it allows the reversing lights to come on with the lever in position R. Gearbox input speed sensor (a) Gearbox output speed sensor (b) The sensor takes the form of a tubular case containing a permanent magnet and an electrical winding. As the toothed wheel passes the winding, voltage changes are set up at the winding terminals due to the changing gap: this change generates a sinusoidal signal at the connector terminals, with signal frequency proportional to toothed wheel speed. the input speed signal is used mainly to: determined converter slide (with lock-up clutch released); determine gear shifting. The output speed signal is used mainly to: determine brake and clutch sliding during speed shifts; determine gear shifts; carry out self-adaptivity actions. a - gearbox input speed sensor b - gearbox output speed sensor Oil temperature sensor The sensor consists of an NTC resistance element (Negative temperature coefficient) whose electrical resistance falls as temperature increases. The fluid temperature signal is used mainly to: Correct line pressure; enable specific strategies in the case of high fluid temperatures; modulate lock-up clutch intervention management. Oil pressure sensor The sensor consists of a resistance bridge screen-printed onto a flexible membrane that separates the measurement chamber (connected to the environment to be measured) and the reference chamber. Membrane shape changes due to the pressure difference between chambers alters bridge resistance and thus output voltage because the supply voltage remains constant. The fluid pressure signal is used mainly to: manage line pressure changes. DIAGNOSTICS Self-diagnostic function The Automatic Gearbox Node is equipped with the following self-diagnostic function. This constantly monitors the sensors and actuators in order to detect faults and malfunctions: these errors are stored and may be read using diagnostic equipment. The following functions are monitored: NCA NCA power supply oil pressure sensor - circuit open sequential solenoid power supply EVS line pressure regulation circuit multifunction switch operation of line pressure modulation solenoid EVM1 operation of lock-up clutch engagement modulation solenoid EVM2 heat exchanger fluid by-pass solenoid manual solenoid VM accelerator pedal positon not stored gearbox input speed sensor gearbox output speed sensor engine speed information analogue sensor power supply The system informs the driver of the presence of an error by flashing a warning light on the dashboard. Recovery function When a fault is detected, the system activates certain hydraulic and mechanical safety strategies to ensure the gearbox operates under safe conditions. The system assesses the extend of the fault and allows the vehicle to be driven if possible. Recovery functions are available for certain fault types. INTRODUCTION The vehicle is equipped with a braking system designed to achieve: a high level of efficiency as an active safety feature durability and reliability excellent flexibility The system is the servo-assisted hydraulic type with two independent cross-over circuits (each circuit acting on one front wheel and the diametrically opposite rear wheel) to ensure braking on both sides of the vehicle if there is a failure in one of the circuits. It is equipped with sophisticated auxiliary electronic systems: EBD (Electronic Brakeforce Distribution) function HBA (Hydraulic Brake Assistance) TC + ASR (Traction control) (Anti Slip Regulation) MSR ESP (Electronic Stability Program) ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) The 2.0 16V petrol and 2.0 16v JTD versions have ABS fitted as standard whilst the top of the range 2.2 16V ITD and 3.0 24V versions have the ESP fitted as standard. ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) Structure ABS prevents the wheels from locking allowing braking to be modulated irrespective of the level of each wheel, metering the pressure at the brackets. The ABS consists of: an electronic control unit incorporated in the electro-hydraulic control unit (with the whole assembly known as the Brake Node NFR) a hydraulic control unit that modulates braking pressure by means of eight solenoids, two for each wheel four active type sensors that detect the angular speed of the wheels wiring with specific connector Using the speed information received from each wheel, the electronic node controls the subsequent pressure maintenance, pressure decrease and pressure increase stages, if necessary. Maintaining the slipping rate at between 10 and 30% during braking makes it possible to ensure optimum stopping distances and preserve good directional stability. Operation All versions of the vehicle are fitted as standard with a Bosch 5.7 anti-lock braking system with 4 active sensors and 4 channels with electronic brakeforce distribution (EBD) incorporated. The active safety features are: guaranteeing maximum braking action for each wheel within the locking limit safeguarding the directional stability of the vehicle, within the locking limit quickest possible reponse the capacity to automatically adapt to the most diverse operating conditions The innovative feature of the active sensors lies in the fact that the signal received by each wheel is processed directly by the sensor rather than being sent to the NFR. The main advantages of this solution are basically that the system intervenes immediately because it is able to read speed signals close to zero (the passive sensors are restricted to speeds above 4 km/h). A further advantage of the system is the reduced sensitivity to outside electromagnetic interference caused by electromagnetic fields present in towns and places of high technological and industrial density plus the fact that it is not susceptible to interference produced by the heating of the road surface (used in some North European countries). Brake Node NFR (ABS version) Specifications and operation The brake node is divided into two sections - an electronic node and an electro-mechanical control unit The electro-mechanical control unit has the task of modulating the pressure of the fluid at the brake calipers via solenoid valves with the following operating stages: brake fluid pressure increase brake fluid pressure maintenance brake fluid pressure discharge The electro-hydraulic control unit consists of: eight 2-way solenoid valves a dual circuit recovery pump two low pressure accumulators two high pressure accumulators The electronic node has the following functions: acquiring the data coming from the wheel sensors memorizing the control parameters defined during the vehicle P.D.I. processing the data acquired checking the braking process, preventing the wheels from locking memorizing the fault codes and activating the ABS and EBD warning lights transmitting and receiving data via the CAN line detecting faults in the braking system components The operation of the ABS is illustrated in the diagram below A,B,C,D - Anti-lock brake sensors for the wheels S1 - Brake fluid level signal S2, S3 - Left and right front brake pad wear signal NFR (ABS) - Brake node with ABS S4 - Stop signal switch Self-diagnosis The basic processing of the NFR software consists of detecting all the problems which could occur. The management of the faults is carried out at three safety levels: Checking the signals whilst the vehicle is driving (presence, value interval and dispersion) Analytical redundance (consistency of the signals starting with one model). Active tests (operation of the pre-loading pump and hydraulic lock during initialization and at the start of driving + slewing sensor test by the brake node). The role of levels 1 and 2 is to check basic operation, whilst level 3 is designed to prevent untimely activation of the adjustment which could be caused following static interference or as a result of a sensor fault. The device carries out checks of a different nature ranging from short circuiting and electrical faults to mechanical problems. If there is a fault, the system only puts the functions involved out of commission, guaranteeing the mechanical braking function. Electronic Brake Force Distribution (EBD) This is the distribution of the brake force between the front and rear wheels; its intevention improves braking efficiency ensuring optimum balance. The incorporation of the EBD device in the ABS guarantees the optimum behaviour of the vehicle during braking through: improved brakeforce distribution adjustments adapted to the actual wheel grip conditions and efficiency of the pads continuous monitoring of the efficiency of the system maintaining the adjustment over a period of time a reduction in the temperature of the front brakes and the force required at the brake servo Assisted emergency braking The assisted braking system is either the hydraulic type HBA (Hydraulic Brake Assistance) or the mechanical type MBA (Mechanical Brake Assistance). In both cases they are systems that automatically increase braking pressure in emergency situations. In effect, in critical conditions, when the driver operates the brake pedal decisively, the system intervenes on the braking circuit, increasing braking pressure to ensure that the vehicle stops as quickly as possbile. The system is calibrated at the pedal operating speed and intervenes when the speed of the pedal vpedal > 450mm/s. The two systems behave in the same way, the only difference being that the pressure increase setting in one case is regulated by the ESP software and in the other case in a mechanical fashion. Traction control and anti-slip system (TC and ASR) The ASR system is available incorporated in the ESP for automatic traction control. The ASR (Anti-Slip Regulation) system prevents the drive wheels from slipping by reducing the excess engine torque on the basis of the grip coefficient for the available road surface. The ASR control unit calculates the slipping of the drive wheels using the difference between the front and rear wheel speeds measured by the ABS sensors. Depending on the driving situation, two different control systems can be activated: If there is a request for excess power with the drive wheels slipping, the ASR reduces the torque through intervention on the throttle, the advance and the fuel supply for petrol engines or by adjusting the injection on diesel versions. If only one wheel is slipping, the TC (Traction Control) system intervenes automatically, braking the wheel without the driver operating the brake pedal, producing a locking effect similar to that of a self-locking differential. The effect of less stress for the mechanical traction components (differential and gearbox) achieved by controlling traction at low speeds is also important. Engine drive regulation. (MSR) This system regulates engine braking torque when changing down: in the case of a rapid gear change to a lower gear, the MSR system ("Motor Scleppmoment Regelung") intervenes, restoring engine torque, preventing the wheel from locking which, especially in poor grip conditions, could lead to a loss in vehicle stability. ESP General remarks The ESP (Electronic Stability Program) (fitted as standard on 2.2 16V JTD versions) is an active safety system for controlling the vehicle during dynamic manoeuvres. This system keeps the vehicle stable during sudden manoeuvres, improving active safety, especially on slippery surfaces. In effect, the ESP reacts quickly to both oversteer and understeer, returning the vehicle to a stable condition and allowing the driver to keep full control. When the ESP is activated, the amber coloured warning light flashes. Switching ESP/ASR off. The ESP is automatically switched on when the ignition is turned ON. The ESP system can be switched off by the driver, by pressing a button located in the lower part of the dashboard, driver's side, thereby allowing the vehicle to be used in certain particularly serious situations. The switching off of the ESP is signalled by the amber coloured warning light on constantly and by a message in the display / NSC screen: "ESP switched off". 1 - ESP/ASR disabling button When the ESP is switched off the ASR is also deactivated as a result of which, when driving on snow-covered roads, with snow chains fitted, it might also be useful to switch the ASR off; in effect, under these circumstances the slipping of the drive wheels during take off allows better traction. The ESP off condition is cancelled both when the speed of the vehicle is above 30 km/h and after the ignition is switched ON. Operation The system detects the state of the vehicle (lateral acceleration, angular speed, grip on the ground) and, if it feels that the vehicle is close to an unstable condition (skidding, understeer, oversteer), it acts on the drive torque and applies suitable differentiated braking action at each of the four wheels. Control of the direction takes place by exploiting the longitudinal and transverse grip of the tyre: the different braking on the two sides of the vehicle produces a straightening torque (slewing control). The management of the ESP function is entrusted to the NFR (brake node) which, by processing the figures acquired from the sensors (steering angle sensor, lateral acceleration sensor / slewing sensor, wheel rpm sensors, braking system pressure sensor), monitors the dynamic control parameters (wheel slipping, slewing speed, geometry angle) and corrects the trajectory of the vehicle producing a stabilizing effect. The management of the system is illustrated below. A,B,C,D - Anti-lock brake sensors for the wheels E - Slewing and acceleration sensor F - Braking pressure sensor incorporated in the hydraulid unit S1 - Brake fluid level signal S2, S3 - Brake pad wear signal S4 - Main stop signal S5 - Parking brake signal S6 - ESP/ASR disabling button S7 - Accelerator pedal potentiometer signal NFR (ESP) - Brake node (electronically and electro-hydraulically controlled node) with ESP system In accordance with the previous table, the system interacts with: the CAN line (to converse with the engine management node (NCM), automatic transmission node (NCA), where fitted, etc.) the specific brake pump, which produces the pressure required to act on the brakes the electronic throttle (for dialogue between the NFR and NCM nodes) the instrument panel Node, the milometer warning lights Node with active type warning lights and with the multi-function screen node. Operating strategies As stated previously, in addition to controlling the slipping of the vehicle in a lengthwise direction, the ESP system also controls slipping in a sideways direction and, as a result, controls the lateral stability of the vehicle. The lateral stability of a vehicle depends on the reaction of the tyres to lateral forces and the adhesion force of the wheel with the road surface. The adhesion force of a wheel depends on the vertical load which depends on the situation the wheel finds itself in (resting or no load) and on the friction coefficient which depends on the road surface and tyre conditions. When the vehicle is travelling in a straight line, the lateral forces do not really have an effect unless outside factors that increase its intensity intervene (e.g. a gust of wind or a change to a different surface), unlike when driving round a bend where there is a strong increase in lateral forces due to the increase in centrifugal force. The action of the lateral forces produce a variation in the drift angle of the wheels and, consequently, a variation in the axle drift (the drift angle refers to the difference between the desired route and the effective route). The lateral forces cannot act in the same way on all four wheels because they are not all in the same load conditions. The load for each wheel: depends on: acceleration (lightening of the front axle and loading of the rear axle) braking (loading of the front axle and lightening of the rear axle) bend to the right/left (loading or the outer wheels and lightening of the inner wheels) accelerating/decelerating round a bend (combination of the cases mentioned above). It is obvious that if the lateral forces acting on the individual wheels vary, there will also be a variation in the resulting forces acting on the vehicle axles. This means that the lateral forces acting on the front axle overcoming those acting on the rear axle and viceversa results in a rotation (moment) in relation to the vehicle's vertical axis (slewing axis). The moment of slewing affects the behaviour of the vehicle producing either understeer or oversteer. Understeer for a vehicle is when, with increasing lateral acceleration, the drift angle for the front axle increases greatly compared with that of the rear axle. In this case the vehicle, when driving round a bend, tends to coincide with the tangent of the actual bend. Oversteer for a vehicle is when, with increasing lateral acceleration, the drift angle for the rear axle increases greatly compared with that of the front axle. In this case the vehicle has a tendency to overturn. In order to keep the effect of lateral forces under control and limit the slewing moment, the A.B.S. must firstly calculate the behaviour of vehicle set by the driver using: steering wheel angle sensor accelerator pedal position brake circuit pressure after which the brake node (NFR) should check the actual behaviour of the vehicle through: the wheel sensors (vehicle speed/wheel speed), lateral acceleration sensor / slewing sensor. As can be deduced from what has been said earlier, the node is capable of: detecting actions carried out by the user, in effect, through the position of the steering wheel it checks the number of degrees (wide radius or narrow radius bends) and the speed for rotating the steering wheel (sharp or gentle rotations) and, using the position of the throttle and the brake pressure when accelerating or braking, how the user is taking the bend or deviating from the straight path. detecting the actual behaviour of the vehicle given the environmental variables, e.g. slippery surface, reaction of the vehicle to incorrect manoeuvres by the user, etc., in order to identify the moment of slewing and the lateral sliding of the axles via the sensors on the four wheels and the slewing/lateral acceleration sensor. These two operations are necessary to superimpose the mathematical model analyzed in the node on the actual behaviour of the vehicle in order to determine the corrective measures to be implemented through the brakes and the engine. Understeer round bends The system verifies the presence of understeer (mainly from the drift of the front axle), corrects the behaviour of the vehicle, braking the inner wheels round the bend in order to create an opposing moment which will lead the vehicle towards the centre of the bend and, possibly, reducing the drive torque. Oversteer round bends In the presence of understeer (mainly from the drift of the rear axle) the NFR corrects the behaviour of the vehicle, braking the outer front wheel round the bend in order to create an opposite slewing moment, if necessary increasing the drive torque. The system intervenes before the oversteer and understeer values are too high in order to limit the corrective measures that have to be taken which could make handling difficult. Sharp variations from the straight path (slalom/overtaking) In the case of sharp variations from the path (e.g. overtaking, slalom), the system identifies possible oversteer and understeer conditions and corrects the path of the vehicle acting as described in the cases mentioned previously. Sharp variation from the straight path (driving on different surfaces) The electronic node is capable of detecting deviations in the path and the prevalence of axle drift, correcting the path through suitable action on the brakes and the engine. Sharp acceleration/deceleration The system uses the A.S.R./M.S.R. strategy also controlling the lateral acceleration of the vehicle and, as a result, regulating the action on the front and rear brakes and on the engine torque in a more complete way than on vehicles with ASR only. Steering sensor The steering angle sensor has the task of measuring the angles in degrees and the rotation speed of the steering wheel and making these figures available via the Bodywork VAN network (NVO). Operation The diagram shows a section of the steering column switch unit and toothed wheels. The sensor, incorporated in the steering column switch unit, comprises three toothed wheels. One main wheel fitted on the column axis which rotates when the steering wheel is operated. Two wheels, each fitted with a magnet that are activated by the main wheel and have one tooth different in relation to each other. This difference is translated into a different rotation speed for the wheels. In order to measure the steering wheel angle, the sensor needs a reference corresponding to an angle of zero. This reference is not determined by positioning the system during the fitting stage, but requires the sensor to be calibrated in the factory so that this equipment is operational, neutralizing the lighting up of the ASR/ESP failure warning light. It is incorporated in the toe in bench at the end of the assembly line. The sensor measures the following via internal electronics: the angular position of the steering column the rotation speed of the steering column. This information is processed directly by the sensor and is made available at the brake node via the network. The sensor has an autodiagnostic function and is capable of carrying out a check on the plausibility of the information processed. Slewing/lateral acceleration sensor Composition and operation The sensor consists of sensitive elements which detect slewing and lateral acceleration and an electronic management function. The sensor is located in the centre of gravity area on the tunnel between the two front seats near the Air Bag node (see diagram). A - Slewing/lateral acceleration sensor The sensor has the task of detecting rotation on the vehicle's vertical axis (slewing) and measuring lateral acceleration. ESP system brake node (NFR) The electro-hydraulic unit located in the engine compartment on the left front wheel arch comprises an electronic node and an electro-hydraulic control unit. The entire system is known as the NFR (brake node). The technology is identical to the ABS / ASR system and the operating principle is the same but this system includes 12 solenoid valves (4 inlet solenoid valves, 4 switching solenoid valves and 4 pre-loading solenoid valves), 2 accumulators and a dual acting piston pump. 1 - Electro-hydraulic control unit 2 - Electronic control node A - Pressure sensor Thanks to the peripheral activators and sensors, the electronic unit analyzes the information concerning the trajectory of the vheicle and implements the corrective measures, whilst the electro-hydraulic control unit has the function of modulating the pressure of the fluid at the brake calipers through the solenoid valves in the following stages: brake fluid pressure increase brake fluid pressure maintenance brake fluid pressure decrease. Anti-lock braking system active sensors Composition and operation Resistive, mangetic type inductive sensors which measure the speed of each of the vehicle's wheels through a toothed wheel are used to acquire the speed of the wheels. The sensor consists of a permanent magnet and a winding. A toothed wheel, in one piece with the vehicle wheel, slides in front of the sensor, the magnetic flow varies and produces an alternating voltage in the winding whose frequency and amplitude are proportional to the rotation speed of the toothed wheel as illustrated in the diagram. 1 - permanent magnet 2 - magnetic poles 3 - winding 4 - sensor casing 5 - toothed wheel 6 - induced magnetic field System warning lights The diagram shows the warning lights at the milometer warning lights node NSO 1 - ESP warning light 2 - ABS warning light ESP/ASR intervention/fault display The intervention of the ESP system is shown by the special warning light in the milometer warning lights Node (NSO) flashing (5 Hz d.c. 50%). If there is a fault or in the case of manual disablement, the ESP system switches off automatically and the warning light comes on constantly together with the message shown by the multi-function display. If the ESP is faulty, the vehicle behaves like a version which does not have this system: it is advisable to seek assistance as soon as possible from the Fiat Dealer Network. the ESP system improves driving safety but there are limited situations which cannot be controlled by the ESP system, therefore it is not seen as a device which improves the performance of the vehicle but as a device that improves the safety of the vehicle. ABS failure display A fault in the ABS is signalled at the NSO, behind the steering wheel, with the warning light with the ABS ideogram, whose color varies depending on the type of fault, coming on. ABS defect - amber coloured warning light (less serious because the EBD is working) ABS + EBD defect - red coloured wanring light. A fault in the EBD is signalled by the ABS warning light and the handbrake warning light coming on simultaneously. In effect, in the case of sharp and prolonged braking, the system automatically switches on the hazard warning lights, allowing the driver to concentrate on keeping control of the vehicle and immediately warning the drivers of vehicles behind of a dangerous situation ahead. The hazard warning lights remain on until the driver accelerates again; however, the manual operation of the hazard warning lights switch by the driver always has priority both for switching the function on or off. Operating principle Deceleration beyond the limit (6 m/s2, if the speed is higher than 40 km/h for a certain period) automatically activates the hazard warning lights. Subsequent acceleration or pressing the specific button switches the hazard warning lights off. A defect in the system or the lack of information concerning the vehicle speed or deceleration does not cause the activation of the hazard warning lights and does not affect manual operation. The system consists of: a hydraulic pump connected to the direction valve, a direction valve incorporated in the gearbox casing with the task of operating the steering power assistance. FRONT SUSPENSION The system has been designed following the McPherson system whose main specifications are: coil springs offset in relation to the shock absorber axis to reduce sliding friction; the springs, which rest on the upper and lower shims with a rubber seal in between to prevent operating noise are extremely flexible to ensure driving comfort in all load conditions, end of travel rubber buffer which intervenes gradually for an improved and gradual response round bends and in the case of impact, anti-roll bar connected directly to the shock absorber to ensure improved responsiveness when cornering, double acting, pressurized, hydraulic shock absorbers to reduce operating noise, forged steel track control arms to limit the weight of the non suspended masses. This type of solution involves a decrease in the steering radius, less roll and more efficient braking. Front suspension diagram The front suspension is illustrated in the diagram below 1 - Crossmember. 2 - Rods. 3 - Springs. 4 - Front load carrying element. 5 - Anti-roll bar. 6 - Cradle. Rear suspension The rear suspension has been designed with a crossmember that can be deformed to improve comfort (maintaining the dynamic properties of the previous models). The suspension consists of: a crossmember 2 suspension arms 2 hydraulic shock absorbers 2 coil springs a rear anti-roll bar (Panhard bar) an anti-roll bar (for the 3.0 6 cylinder and 2.2 JTD versions only) Rear suspension diagram The rear suspension is illustrated in the diagram below 1 - Shock absorber. 2 - Spring. 3 - Panhard bar. To improve the stability of the vehicle on the road in all conditions, the toe in has been increased, altering the wheel geometry and the section of the crossmember compared with the previous model. The diagram below illustrates the different shape and section of the two crossmembers. 1 - Crossmember fitted on the previous vehicle 2 - New crossmember adopted The modification that has been made involves increasing the flexibility of the suspension (from 26% to 32%), an increase in the front anti-roll effect, due to the variation of the bar fastening point (directly on the shock absorber body) and an increase in the rear anti-foll effect, due to the new shape and section of the rear crossmember. Specifications of the components The special features of the components are: steel crossmember 22MV6TN, steel suspension arms HLE 275 (high yield point), hydraulic shock absorbers that operate according to the vehicle load (less rigid with no load), coil springs with bottom coil covered by a rubber outer casing and top coil resting on a rubber support, the hinging with the bodyshell is produced through cellular flexible mountings to reduce bodyshell vibrations, The construction design and technical solutions make it possible to achieve excellent performance levels in terms of comfort and pleasant, safe driving.

General remarks The climate control system fitted to the vehicle is used to alter the environmental properties of air taken into the car (temperature and moisture), demist the glass surfaces and insulate the vehicle occupants from pollutants. The passenger compartment climate control system therefore contributes greatly to the physical wellbeing of the passengers and their comfort. The following image shows system air distribution through the passenger compartment 1 - Fixed upper diffuser for windscreen defrosting and demisting 2 - Fixed diffuser for demisting or defrosting side windows 3 - Orientable and adjustable side windows 4 - Orientable and adjustable central diffusers 5 - Fixed front footwell diffusers 6 - Fixed rear footwell diffusers located behind the third row 7 - Rear orientable and adjustable outlets in the second row 8 - Fixed rear footwell diffusers located in the third row 9 - Orientable outlets in the third row. Specifications The vehicle is equipped with the 2 specifications described below. Automatic Dual Zone air conditioner Passenger compartment temperature regulation is split left/right to the first and second rows (the left and right temperature conditions in the second row are the same as in the first row) Triple zone automatic air conditioner This is a combination of a dual zone system for the first and second row with additional fans (left and right side) that can be managed directly in the second row to alter the flow to the side outlets in the second and third row. For all versions: cooling is not managed directly by the NCM (engine control node), which manages the control of certain functions such as GERM (engine cooling fan unit) and compressor activation. The controls for these functions are, however, issued directly by the NBC. All three systems are governed by electric actuators that manage distribution, recirculation and mixing. Automatic dual zone - triple zone climate control system General remarks Operation of the dual zone module is based on four main fundamental parameters for each climate control system: flow, distribution, mixing, air quality. For more accurate control of climate control operating pameters, the system is equipped with internal and external temperature sensors plus a radiation sensor that sends a solar radiation reading to the NCL to achieve optimum control of dual climate control system temperature. The radiation sensor is located on the facia centre line, while the external temperature sensor is located on the passenger side door mirror. Specifications The automatic climate control system manages the temperature (2 zones), the distribution (2 zones) of the air and the air flow rate inside the passenger compartment on both the driver and passenger sides (front or front and rear) to achieve the desired comfort level. The system is operated by the front passengers by operating a switch on the control panel on the centre console. Another option is another climate control system version known as a triple zone system. In this case, the dual zone system is complemented by additional fans (on the left and right central pillar on the second row). These allow rear passengers to alter the flow by means of controsl on the side outlets. The user is provided with a panel made up of keys, warning lights and an LCD display that are used to set ideal heating conditions and visibility inside the passenger compartment. A button marked REAR on the automatic climate control system can also be used to authorise/prohibit second row passengers from adjusting air flow by means of knobs on the additional fans. Automatic system operating strategy The following figure shows the triple zone climate control system operating architecture 1 - Engine fluid temperature 2 - Linear sensor 3 - Distriubutor unit fan 4 - Climate control circuit compressor 5 - Heated rear window 6 - Radiation sensor 7 - Left rear supplementary fan 8 - Right rear supplementary fan 9 - Passenger compartment temperature sensor CONTROL PANEL The figure shows both types of NCL (dual zone and triple zone) with controls A - Driver side interior temperature regulation button B - AUTO operating button C - Display D1 - MONO button joins driver and passenger side temperatures D2 - REAR button enables or disables use of additional rear outlets E - Passenger side interior temperature regulation button F - Heated rear window on/off button G - On/off button for maximum defrost/demist of windscreen and front side windows, heated rear window and door mirror heater coils. H - Central vent air outlet regulation button I - Lower vent air outlet regulation button L - Rotary wheel for air flow regulation (main fan) M - Central vent air outlet regulation button N - A/C button enabling air condition compresosr on/off O - On/off button for internal air recirculation/additional rear outlets 1 - Driver side temperature display 2 - Fan flow symbol 3 - Passenger side temperature display 4 - AUTO symbol 5 - Rear fan symbol 6 - Compressor symbol 7 - Recirculation symbol If the climate control system is triple zone, the rear outlet controls shown in the figure are included R - Rear air flow regulation knob SETTINGS AND SELECTIONS The system offers various modes: turning main fan knob (L) clockwise; pressing button A (+/-) or E (+/-); pressing one of the buttons (H ,I ,M); if the engine is off for more than 20 minutes, the system always restarts in automatic mode even if it was off before the vehicle was turned off, without altering the temperature level. In the following three cases, the system sets all the operating conditions stored automatically before being turned off: pressing one of the buttons B, N, N; in this case the system switches to automatic mode; pressing button G; in this case the system switches to MAX-DEF mode. The system also stores the situation before deactivation automatically but also takes into account vehicle parking duration and other external parameters, namely: if the engine is parked for up to 20 minutes with virtually unchanged internal temperature, the system restarts with the same settings. If the temperature changes greatly during this period, the system changes to automatic mode and sets itself to the temperature level applied before the vehicle was turned off; if the engine is off for more than 20 minutes, the system always restarts in automatic mode even if it was off before the vehicle was turned off, without altering the temperature level. Setting required temperature level This operation is carried out by pressing button A (+/-) or E (+/-) and checking the required temperature appears on the display (C). If a dual zone temperature system is fitted, the driver and the front passenger can set different temperature levels. The maximum difference permitted by the system is 5 °C. The temperature increases or decreases in 1 °C steps between 14 °C and 18 °C and between 24 °C and 28 °C, while the reading shown constantly on the display changes in 0.5 °C steps between 18 °C and 24 °C. If the system is triple zone and comes with addition fans, the system regulates the temperature in the same way as a single zone system when the + or - key is held down for a long time (for longer than one second) Air distribution selection The operation is carried out by pressing a combination of buttons H, I, M located inside knob L. Five different distribution patterns are possible: ventilation (front), front bilevel/footwell), footwell, windscreen/footwells, windscreen (MAX-DEF). Select the required distribution pattern by pressing the corresponding key and deactivating any other distribution patterns that may be activated. The relevant leds come on and others go off to confirm that selection has taken place. During automatic operation (AUTO), air distribution is managed by the system and the relevant leds are thus all off. Setting fan speed When knob L is turned, the display shows the required speed value by darkening the front fan symbol blades on display C. Compressor activation/deactivation When the A/C key (N in the figure) is pressed with the led on, the compressor is disabled and the led goes off. When the key is pressed with the led off, the automatic system manages the compressor (enabled/disabled). If the system is in automatic mode, the compressor is controlled and managed by the system according to outside temperature. When the compressor is deactivated with the associated led off, recirculation status remains as it was prior to deactivation (closed or open) and it is still possible to activate open recirculation. If the system is in automatic mode, the compressor is controlled on the basis of outdoor temperature in accordance with the compressor deactivation strategy if measued outdoor temperature is < di 4° C. Alignment between driver and passenger side temperatures Setting is carried out by pressing the MONO key which unites driver and passenger temperatures to obtain an even temperature in the passenger compartment. Recirculation activation This setting allows the driver to choose, by pressing button O, to drive with bypass recirculation closed (relevant led on), with air taken in from outside (led off), bypass recirculation on, or system left in automatic mode (led off even if active) The system is not equipped with an AQS pollusion sensor. Setting automatic operation (AUTO) This is carried out by pressing the auto button on the climate control panel, when the display shows AUTO and the symbol (ice). This key sets the system to fully automatic mode, when it manages and controls temperature, air distribution and main fan speed itself; During automatic operation, if button N is pressed, the compressor is deactivated and the cold air flow is turned off, the associated led goes off, the system stays in automatic mode and the symbol (ice) disappears from the display but the AUTO message remains. If one or more functions are selected automatically (distribution, ventilation), the AUTO message disappears from the display in accordance with the following activation strategy Control AUTO (appears on display) Recirculation YES Compressor NO Timing YES Fan knob NO Mixing NO MAX DEF YES Heated rear window NO REAR YES AUTO YES Additional fan activation YES Air distribution selection By pressing a combination of buttons H, I, M, located in central knob L. Five distribution patterns are possible: ventilation (front), front bilevel/footwell), footwell, windscreen/footwells, windscreen (MAX-DEF). Select the required distribution pattern by pressing the corresponding key and deactivating any other distribution patterns that may be activated. The relevant leds come on and others go off to confirm that selection has taken place. During automatic operation (AUTO), air distribution is managed by the system and the relevant leds are thus all off. Three temperature bands have been defined and the automatic device associates a distribution pattern to each as shown below: T outdoor £ 15° C: windscreen or footwell distribution based on other parameters such as solar radiation etc. 15° £ T outdoor £ 25° C: windscreen/footwell or footwell distribution based on other parameters such as solar radiation etc. T outdoor ³ 25° C: ventilation distribution To optimise automatic distribution changs according to solar radiation and vehicle speed distribution. Heated rear window activation The control button activates electrical coils in the rear window to heat, dehumidify and demist. To turn this function off, simply press the button again and ensure the relevant led has gone off. The heated rear window will work if the ignition key is on MAR. It is managed independently even if the system is not activated. Maximum cooling setting Carried out automatically by pressing or holding down the temperature selection key unti the temperature is set to 14 °C, with exterior conditions that require the system to perform to the maximum. This setting forces the system to work in single zone mode and activates the following actions: Mixer in max cooling position; air distribution set to ventilation; Air flow rate at maximum value; engagement of compressor; automatic recirculation closed (for petrol versions), partially open (for JTD versions), even though open recirculation can be operated manually without abandoning the required setting. Maximum heating setting If a temperature of 28°C is set automatically, the system is bound to perform to the maximum. This setting activates: Mixer in maximum heating position air distribution to windscreen/footwells or footwells according to the outdoor temperature; Air flow rate at maximum value; compressor managed in accordance with system software; automatic recirculation closed (for petrol versions), partially open (for JTD versions), even though open recirculation can be operated manually without abandoning the required setting. MAX-DEF activation This operation is activated automatically by pressing button G to ensure window demisting in the least possible time. MAX DEF procedure management takes precedence over "maximum cooling" or "maximum heating" modes and these are suspended when it is activated. The system performs the following actions when the function is activated: stores operating status and displays before the command was given AUTO disappears from the display activation of MAX DEF leds, compressor, heated rear window and MONO mode temperature (shown on display). air flow shown on display Function activation also determines activation of: maximum air flow distribution to the windscreen mixer flaps in maximum heating position bypass recirculation open (100% outside air) compressor heated rear windscreen The only actions permitted during this mode are air flow adjustment and heated rear window deactivation. The system abandons the function if MAX DEF or any other button is pressed a second time. Air flow adjustment Air flow is regulated manually byturning the knob to gradually darken the vanes on the fan symbol shown on the display. The maximum number of 8 steps correspond to possible fan speed settings. If no manual controls are given, speed is managed continuously by the automatic device and shown on the display by constant darkening of 4 half-vanes. The AUTO message on the display goes off if the ventilation control is operated manually. In this case, air flow to the second and third rows may be adjusted (by using the additional fans) if the REAR button is activated. When the compressor is deactivated, the ventilation control may be adjusted until flow is zero. If the compressor is enabled, the system can go no lower than the half-vane shown on the display (equivalent to 20% flow rate) to prevent the compressor icing up. Activating rear outlet air flow regulation (REAR) The interior air recirculation function (for versions with additional fans) allows the heating or cooling conditions required in the second and third row to be reached more quickly. This setting is achieved by pressing button D (REAR). This authorises passengers in the second row to manage air flow regulation by means of the additional fan knobs. Display C then shows the rear fan symbol. The effect of the additional fans depends on knob positions: knob in position "0": additional fan off; knob in position "-": addition fan air output equal to 0% of main fan flow setting; knob in position "AUTO" position: additional fan with same output as main fan; knob in position "+": additional fan with air output equal to 70% of current main fan output. If the REAR button is not not and the climate control system is operating automatically, the air flow to the second and third rows is as supplied by the man fan. In this case, the only way to prevent ventilation is to close the relevant outlets. During automatic and manual operation, if the knob is set to "+", the additional fans work in all air distribution modes apart from "MAX DEF" the REAR key can be activated in dual and single zone modes. Press key a second time to deactivate. System deactivation The system is deactivated by turning fan outlet regulation knob anticlockwise until the display shows the vehicle profile without the fans. The system performs the following actions when it is turned off: stores status prior to deactivation; turns off graphics on display apart from vehicle profile; sets air recirculation to bypass on (external air intake); turns off compressor; turns off fan; sets air distribution to windscreen mode; mixer in max cooling position. FAULT SITUATION When faults are detected (buttons locked, mixer motors, distribution, recirculation, passenger comartment temperature sensor, solar radiation sensor, coolant fluid temperature, vehicle speed - and defects connected with electrical equipment, Van network etc.) the system automatically switches to Recovery mode. The points that separate the decimal numbers on the display begin to flash in this mode. Contact the Fiat Service Network as soon as possible in this case. Operation in Recovery mode If two or more keys are locked, the system switches to Recovery mode. In brief, system operation in this mode is as follows: driver and passenger temperature: these are co-ordinated and change in the same way; if buttons A or E are locked, the system sets the temperature to 21°C; main fan, distribution, compressor, recirculation operation is assured in automatic mode (AUTO); AUTO function: because the function is predefined, recirculation, compressor, air distribution and main fan are managed automatically and pressing the buttons therefore has no effect; MAX-DEF function: The system sets itself to automatic mode, pressing the air distribution, compressor, AUTO and recirculation buttons has no effect while main fan and temperature functions remain active. REAR function: additional fans cannot be activated; Heated rear window: cannot be activated: timing ends first if active before. The capacity of this type of compressor can vary as a result of: variations in the load required from the system, changes in the outside temperature and/of humidity conditions, sharp alterations in the engine load conditions. Coolant pressure safety is guaranteed by a cooling pressure sensor that communicates the circuit pressure condition to the NCM. The NCM supplies information on systm status to the NBC (Body Compupter node) that controls NCL cooling requirements and controls compressor activation/deactivation The main features of the compressor are: Cooling capacity: 760 g Direction of rotation: clockwise. Max continuous number of revs: 7000 rpm. Max non-continuous number of revs: 8000 rpm. Number of pistons: 7. Minimum stroke: 2.2 mm. Maximum stroke: 34.2 mm. Minimum displacement: 10.4 cm³/rev Maximum displacement: 161.3 cm³/rev Quantity of lubricant: 135 cm³ ± 15 cm³. Engine cooling fan assembly operating strategies (GERM) Engine cooling fan control strategies are of two types referred to as FRIC and BRIC FRIC (cooling function integral with engine control). This strategy guarantees control of the engine cooling fan during and after engine operation. The system considers: coolant temperature climate control system function cooling requirements. automatic transmission water/fluid heat exchanger cooling requirements. temperature level to which the thermostat is set. The strategy must also guarantee information to the multiplex line or in sequence to other relevant engine control functions: water temperature information for various systems water temperature warning and prewarning for control panel warning light request to deactivate the climate control system compressor GMV rotation information supply the necessary power to GMV electronic circuits at each stage of operation guarantee emergency operating mode if a system component is faulty. BRAC (air conditioning cooling requirement) This process determines an air conditioning cooling requirement. This requirement is processed using the various possible information sources: Conventional mechanical pressure switch. Coolant pressure sensor signal, acquired via the NCM.

Whilst audio CDs are playing there are problems with the musical reproduction (audio interruptions, skipping one or more tracks, repeating the current track). Given the nature of the CD mechanism and the reading technique, it is absolutely normal that one or more of the above conditions could occur with the CD player, if the vehicle/CONNECT system is subject to strong impacts or stresses that affect the dashboard or driving over potholes or humps at speed. In addition, there cuold be considerable differences between the reproduction or original (pressed) CDs and master copies because the tests are always carried out using original compact discs. Also bear in mind that the introduction of methods to prevent copying can, at times, have effects on the reproduction of the disc. All references to R/R or repair operations and wiring diagrams may be found in the Workshop Manual. Check that the fuel pump suply voltage is not less than 12V. Measure the pump current absorption. Disconnect the negative battery terminal. Disconnect the heater plugs control unit terminal. Disconnect the two connectors for the Webasto control unit (if fitted) Using the Examiner in "Instrument" mode, select "Ammeter" and fit the 10A shunt between the negative battery pole and the system negative terminal. Make sure that the courtesy lights are switched off. Turn the ignition key to the ON position and, within 10 seconds, read the pump absorption (subtracting the consumers supplied by the ignition from the measurement) which should be between 2 and 10A.

Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment pressure transducer between the diesel filter (1a) and the tank (3) fuel return pipe (2). Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Within 10 seconds check that the pressure reading on the gauge is less than 1 bar. The tank electric pump (9) will go off after 10 seconds. Make sure that the taps and the adjustment screws at the side of the pressure gauge are open (except the ones on ducts not connected to the system).

Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment pressure transducer between the diesel filter (1) and the pressure pump (5) supply pipe (4). Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Within 10 seconds, check that the pressure reading on the gauge is between 2 and 3 bar. The tank electric pump (9) will go off after around 10 seconds. Make sure that the taps and the adjustment screws at the side of the pressure gauge are open (except the ones on ducts not connected to the system).

Disconnect the electrical connections (6) from the injectors (7). Disconnect the fuel recirculation pipes from all the injectors. Turn the ignition key to the AVV starting position for 5 seconds and check that jets of fuel do not come out of the top of the injectors. It is normal to see fuel at the tops of the injectors.

Disconnect the electrical connections (6) from the injectors (7). Disconnect the fuel recirculation pipes from all the injectors. Constrict the fuel return pipe (8) to the tank (3) so that fuel does not come out during the test. Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment. Display the "measured diesel pressure" and "engine rpm" parameters on the Control Unit Test parameter screen. Turn the ignition key to the AVV position for 5 seconds and check that the fuel pressure is above 300 bar with the engine speed above 200 rpm and check that fuel does not come out of the top of the injectors.

Fit connector 1.870.792.000 on the turbocharger pipe. Connect the pressure transducer to the tool. Position the diagnostic equipment in the passenger compartment and make the connections. Select "pressure gauge" on the diagnostic equipment and prepare for the acquisition of data in "intake pressure" mode with a 2000 mmHg end of scale and selection time of 10 seconds. Road test the vehicle (sticking to the speed limits in force) as follows: On a motorway route, let the vehicle reach 2500 rpm in 4th gear. Initiate the acquistion by pressing start on the diagnostic equipment and 2 seconds later fully depress the accelerator pedal until the engine speed is 3500 rpm. Once this speed is reached completely release the accelerator pedal. Display the resulting graph and in the pressure constant section, with the exception of the initial peak, the reading should be 1900 - 2080 mbar (1444 - 1581 mmHg) corresponding to a supercharging value of 900 - 1080 mbar. WARNING All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid personal injury. The engine compartment contains many moving parts, components at high temperatures and live wires. Follow the warnings given below very carefully when working in the engine compartment. - Switch off the engine and wait for it to cool down. - No smoking. - No naked flames. - Make sure that there is a fire extinguisher nearby. The use of special Fiat tools is required for certain procedures. The use of these tools is vital for working in safety. Follow the current workshop safety regulations. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific procedures to be followed to prevent dangerous situations from arising. For the use of chemical products follow the safety instructions on the card from the supplier to the consumer (for Italy in accordance with Ministerial Decree No. 47/1992). - Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring, etc.) turn the ignition key OFF and DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. Whenever the battery terminal or terminals is disconnected or the battery is removed, carry out the following procedure to reinitialise the control units that manage information relating to the electric windows, the three sun-roofs and the electrically-controlled sliding side door: - Turn the ignition key to the ON position. - Adjust the relevant switches to move the windows, roofs or door to fully-open position. - Adjust the relevant switches to move the windows, roofs or door to fully-closed position. - This operation resets the relevant control units to "0". WARNINGS All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid damage to components. Avoid the brake/clutch fluid coming into contact with the paintwork; if it does happen, wash immediately with water. Do not reuse brake/clutch fluid drained during the bleeding procedure. To release parts that are sticking, tap gently using an aluminium or lead hammer if iron materials are involved; use a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts. When dismantling, check that components that should be marked have the appropriate references. When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent seizing during the initial operating period. When refitting it is vital to follow the tightening torques and adjustment data. Each time they are refitted, replace gaskets, oil seals, flexible washers, circlips, self-locking nuts and all parts that have deteriorated.

INTRODUCTION The MARELLI M4MP2 system fitted to the 1998 16v engine belongs to the category of integrated systems with digital electronic control via an ignition microprocessor with static advance and distribution and indirect intermittent multipoint injection. The system is able to record a set of parameters via specific sensors or voltage data: engine rpm; the correct cylinder combustion TDC sequence (injection timing); absolute pressure in the intake manifold; intake air temperature; coolant temperature; throttle position and closure/opening speed; presence of oxygen in the exhaust gases; vehicle speed; exhaust gas recirculation solenoid position; knock (if present); air conditioner activation (where applicable); battery voltage. The analogue signals are converted into digital signals by analogue/digital (A/D) converters so that they can be used by the control unit. The control unit memory contains a management program (software) that includes a set of strategies, each of which manages a specific system control function. Each strategy uses the information (input) described above to process a set of parameters based on data maps stored in specific areas of the control unit. The strategy then controls the system actuators (output), i.e.the devices that allow the vehicle to operate, namely: control relays; injectors; ignition coils; actuation solenoids; interfaces with the other nodes on the vehicle (Automatic Transmission Node, Brake Node, Body Computer Node, Climate Control Node via the CAN. The integrated system may be broken down schematically into the following subsystems: ELECTRIC/ELECTRONIC CIRCUIT; AIR INTAKE CIRCUIT; FUEL FEED CIRCUIT; EMISSION CONTROL DEVICES.
