The left and right direction indicators are activated by raising or lowering a special lever on the left of the steering column switch unit. The function is activated with the ignition key turned to ON. The hazard warning lights (all the indicators working simultaneously) are activated by a button in the centre of the dashboard. An LED (at the back of the control button) also comes on synchronized with the flashing of the exterior lights. This function is always activated. The engagement of the direction indicators/hazard warning lights and the frequency of the flashing (sent to all the nodes involved via the CAN) are managed by the body computer. The direction indicator warning lights in the instrument panel are also turned on in this way.

The command for switching on the direction indicators is sent by the steering wheel node M093 via the CAN line (pins 1 and 3 of connector A) to the body computer node M001 (to pins 5 and 3 of connector G respectively). The steering wheel node control unit M093 is connected to earth C015 (connector A) via pin 4 of connector A and receives a supply from two lines: one, from pin 11 of connector B of the body computer node M001 at pin 5 of connector A; the other, from pin 1 of connector G of M001 at pin 4 of connector D, protected by fuse F04. In turn, the body computer node M001 informs the engine compartment junction unit B001 (pins 12 and 11 respectively of connector F) of the request to switch on the direction indicators via the CAN line (pins 25 and 27 of connector E). The engine compartment junction unit B001 supplies pin 8 of the left front lamps F010 and the right front lamps F011 (respectively) via pins 8 and 6 of connector G. The body computer node M001 also operates: - from pin 14 connector H, pin 6 of the left rear light cluster F030 and pin 1 of connector A of the left external rear view mirror P060; - from pin 13 connector H, pin 6 of the right rear light cluster F031 and pin 1 of connector A of the right external rear view mirror. The switching on of the warning lights is managed by the milometer warning lights node M140 which communicates via the CAN (pins 2 and 5) with the instrument panel E050 (pins 6 and 12) and the body computer node M001 (pins 8 and 10 connector D). The body computer node M001 supplies the milometer warning lights node M140, via pin 6 of connector D, at pin 4 and the instrument panel E050 at pin 13. This line is protected by fuse F14. The hazard warning lights are turned on using the special switch H020 which is supplied (pin 6) by the body computer node M001 (pin 2 connector D) and communicates the command (pins 3 and 4) to the instrument panel E050 (pins 7 and 11 respectively). The information is then sent from E050 to M001 (via the CAN line) which simultaneously turns on the direction indicators on the left and right sides.

They are operated each time the brake pedal is pressed via the special switch on the actual pedal. there is a second "redundant" switch on the brake pedal used especially by the engine management control unit and the ABS control unit. [EL5030], [EL7023]. The "basic" switch (I030) is the "normally open" type (when the pedal is pressed, the switch closes), whilst the "redundant" switch (I035) is the "normally closed" type (when the pedal is pressed, the switch contact opens): the system checks the consistency of the "pedal pressed" information in this way.

Description The vehicle is equipped with two reversing lights located in the rear light clusters. These are operated whenever reverse is engaged via a switch on the outside of the gear housing. The reversing lights circuit is supplied when the key is in position M. The signal that reverse gear has been engaged is managed by the Body Computer which sends this information to the steering wheel node for the automatic operation of the rearscreen wiper See E3021 REAR WINDOW WASH/WIPE for the electro-chrome rear view mirror See E3032 DOOR MIRROR ADJUSTMENT and to the parking sensors control unit See E3090 PARKING SENSOR

Operational Description The command to switch on the reversing lights is sent by switch I020 located on the gearbox casing. The switch is supplied by the engine compartment junction unit B001 (pin 10 connector C) through the line protected by fuse F01 located in the actual junction unit. When reverse gear is engaged, the switch I020 closes its internal contact, sending the signal to the body computer node M001 (pin 5 connector B). The body computer node M001 controls the switching on of the warning lights located in the left rear light cluster F030 and the right rear light cluster F031 from pin 7 connector H. The body computer node M001 informs the various control units involved of the engagement of reverse gear via the CAN. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES On versions with automatic transmission, there is no reversing switch on the gearbox, but this function is carried out by a special contact "R" for the automatic transmission solenoid valve assembly L050.

The vehicle is equipped with two reversing lights located in the rear light clusters. The reversing lights are activated each time reverse gear is engaged: there is a switch on the outside of the gearbox casing. The reversing lights circuit is supplied when the key is in position M. The signal confirming engagement is managed by the Body Computer. The information is then forwarded to the steering column switch unit (steering wheel node control unit) which: - if the windscreen wipers are working, activates the automatic operation of the rearscreen wiper; See E3021 REAR WINDOW WASH/WIPE - activates the electro-chrome rear view mirror; See E3032 DOOR MIRROR ADJUSTMENT - enables the parking sensor control unit. See E3090 PARKING SENSOR

The command to switch on the reversing lights is sent by switch I020 located on the gearbox casing. The switch is connected (pin 1) to the engine compartment junction unit B001 (pin 13 connector F) which receives an earth signal the moment reverse gear is engaged. In turn, the engine compartment junction unit B001 informs the Body Computer node M001 (pins 25 and 27 of connector E respectively), via the CAN line (pins 12 and 11 of connector F) of the request to switch on the reversing lights. The latter (pins 15 and 6 of connector H respectively) controls the switching on of the rear lights in the left rear light cluster F030 and the right one F031 (pin 4). In addition, the Body computer node M001 informs all the control units involved that reverse gear has been engaged via the CAN. On versions with automatic transmission, there is no reversing light switch on the gearbox I020: this function is carried out by a special contact "R" of the automatic transmission solenoid valve assembly L050. L050 is also connected (pin A5) to the junction unit B001 (pin 15 connector F).

Description The vehicle is equipped with two additional fog lights, located in the light clusters. The fog lights are activated via the special ring nut control on the stalk unit (steering wheel node); when the lights are on, the warning light in the instrument panel comes on. A relay located in the engine bay control unit controls fog lamp activation via a line protected by a fuse. The relay is managed by the Body Computer relay excitation is activated with: enablement signal with key in position M; control signal coming from the steering column switch unit ring nut; side lights on signal. If the side lights are switched off, the fog lights are switched off even if the ring nut is turned. When the side lights are activated again, the fog lamps come on again. If the key is switched off (position S) and then switched back to position M, the ring nut on the steering column switch unit must be activated again to turn on the fog lights.

Operational Description The command to switch on the fog lights is supplied by the steering wheel node control unit M093 to the body computer node M001. The signal travels via the CAN which connects the two control units. The steering wheel node control unit M093 receives a supply (pin 5 connector A) through the line protected by fuse F11, located in the body computer node M001; it receives a supply via the CAN (pin 6 connector A) from the line protected by fuse F16, located in the body computer node M001. The engine compartment junction unit B001 receives the request, via the CAN, to switch on the fog lights and energizes the internal relay, supplying the fog light bulbs (pin 10 connector F) located inside the left front light cluster F010 and the right front light cluster F011. The power supply is direct from the battery and is protected by fuse F06 housed inside the engine compartment junction unit B001. The warning light is switched on by the milometer warning lights node M140 which communicates with the instrument panel E050 and the body computer node M001 via the CAN. The instrument panel E050 and the milometer warning lights node M140 receive a supply via the CAN (pin 13 of E50 and pin 4 of M140) through the line protected by fuse F24 of the body computer M001.

The vehicle may be equipped with two additional fog lights located in the front lights. The fog lights are activated through the control on the steering column switch unit (steering wheel node control unit): with the lights on, the warning light in the instrument panel lights up. The activation of the fog lights is managed by the Body Computer whilst the control takes place through the engine compartment junction unit. The Body computer must receive the following input signals in order for the fog lights to remain activated: - enablement signal with key in position M; - command from steering column switch unit control; - side lights on. If the side lights are deactivated, the fog lights are also switched off: this operation is also carried out if the control has already been turned. Conversely, if the side lights are turned on again, the fog lights are also reactivated. If the key is switched off (position S) and then switched back to position M, the ring nut on the steering column switch unit must be activated again to turn on the fog lights.

The command for switching on the fog lights is sent by the steering wheel node M093 via the CAN line (pins 1 and 3 of connector A) to the body computer node M001 (to pins 5 and 3 of connector G respectively). The steering wheel node control unit M093 is connected to earth C015 (connector A) via pin 4 of connector A and receives a supply from two lines: one, from pin 11 of connector B of the body computer node M001 at pin 5 of connector A; the other, from pin 1 of connector G of M001 at pin 4 of connector D, protected by fuse F04. In turn, the body computer node M001 informs the engine compartment junction unit B001 (pins 12 and 11 respectively of connector F) of the request to switch on the fog lights via the CAN line (pins 25 and 27 of connector E). The engine compartment junction unit B001 supplies pin 24 of the left front lamps F010 and the right front lamps F011 (respectively) via pins 6 and 6 of connector G. The switching on of the warning lights is managed by the milometer warning lights node M140 which communicates via the CAN (pins 2 and 5) with the instrument panel E050 (pins 6 and 12) and the body computer node M001 (pins 8 and 10 connector D). The body computer node M001 supplies the milometer warning lights node M140, via pin 6 of connector D, at pin 4 and the instrument panel E050 at pin 13. This line is protected by fuse F14.

Description The vehicle is equipped with two rear fog lights located in the rear light clusters. The rear fog lamps are activated via the special ring nut control on the stalk unit (steering wheel node); when the lights are on, the warning light in the instrument panel comes on. The switching on of the rear fog lamps is managed by the body computer: it is activated by: enablement signal with key in position M; control signal coming from the steering column switch unit ring nut; side lights on signal. headlamp signal (dipped or main beams), or fog lights on. If one of the enablement signals fails, the ring nut must be turned again to switch on the rear fog lamps.

Operational Description The command to switch on the rear fog lamps is supplied by the steering wheel node control unit M093 to the body computer node M001. The signal travels via the CAN which connects the two control units. The steering wheel node control unit M093 receives a supply (pin 5 connector A) through the line protected by fuse F11, located in the body computer node M001; it receives a supply via the CAN (pin 6 connector A) from the line protected by fuse F16, located in the body computer node M001. Having received the command, the body computer node M001 energizes the relay coil thereby providing a supply via the line protected by fuse F1 (pin 4 connector H) to switch on the lamps located in the left F030 and right F031 light clusters. The warning light is switched on by the milometer warning lights node M140 which communicates with the instrument panel E050 and the body computer node M001 via the CAN. The instrument panel E050 and the milometer warning lights node M140 receive a supply via the CAN (pin 13 of E50 and pin 4 of M140) through the line protected by fuse F24 of the body computer M001.

The vehicle is equipped with two rear fog lights located in the rear light clusters. The rear fog lamps are activated via the special ring nut control on the stalk unit (steering wheel node); when the lights are on, the warning light in the instrument panel comes on. The switching on of the rear fog lamp is managed by the Body Computer; it is activated by: enablement signal with key in position M; control signal coming from the steering column switch unit ring nut; side lights on signal; headlamp signal (dipped or main beams), or fog lights on. If one of the enablement signals fails, the ring nut must be turned again to switch on the rear fog lamps.

The command for switching on the rear fog lamps is sent by the steering wheel node M093 via the CAN line (pins 1 and 3 of connector A) to the body computer node M001 (to pins 5 and 3 of connector G respectively). The steering wheel node control unit M093 receives a power supply (pin 5 connector A and pin 4 connector D) from the Body computer node M001 (pin 11 connector B and pin 1 connector G respectively) via two lines only the second of which is protected by fuse F04. Once the command is received, the Body computer node M001 provides a power supply: - at pin 5 of the right rear light F031, from pin 4 (connector H); - at pin 5 of the left rear light F031, from pin 12 (connector H). The switching on of the warning light is managed by the milometer warning lights node M140 which communicates via the CAN E1050 (pins 2 and 5) with the instrument panel E050 (pins 6 and 12) and the body computer node M001 (pins 8 and 10 connector D). The instrument panel E050 (pin 13) and the Milometer warning lights node M140 (pin 4) receive a power supply from pin 6 of connector D of the Body computer node M001.

The vehicle can be fitted with a homologated tow hook for caravans or trailers in general. This device must meet current regulations and be installed in accordance with the instructions in the installation kit. This installation kit includes the tow hook and also an electronic control unit for the exterior trailer lighting plus specific wiring for connecting the control unit to the vehicle tail-lights and a specific connection on the vehicle located in the boot on the right side. Parking sensor operation is automatically inhibited if a trailer is connected.

Trailer service control unit M181 is supplied: - at pin 2 of connector A, by a line protectd by fuse MF3 located inside maxifuse box B005 (pin 1 connector C); - at pins 3, 6 and 4 of connector B, from body computer node M001 (pins 11 and 4 connector B and pin 4 connector F respectively): the first of the three lines is protected by fuse F12. A line protected by fuse B070 leaves pin 4 of control unit M181 for pin 1 of connector B of trailer wiring connection D073. Control unit M181 communicates (pins 1 and 2 connector B) with body computer node M001 (pins 37 and 39 connector I respectively), which in turn forwards (pins 36 and 38 connector I) any information to the parking sensor control unit. This information is sent via the CAN network. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES See E3090 PARKING SENSOR Pin 1 of connector C of control unit M181 is connected to the same pins and connector of trailer connection D073. Pins 15, 12, 11, 8, 16, 7, 6, 5, 4, 2 of connector B of M181 are also connected to the same connection; pins 14 and 13 are bypassed to pins 12 and 11 respectively, while pin 3 is connected to earth 096.

Description The front courtesy light and the centre courtesy light have three lamps with three control switches: the corresponding spot light can be switched on using external switches. the centre switch can be used to switch the centre light on or off and the switching on is also subject to a delay timer ("courtesy lights" mode) as described below There is only one bulb in the rear courtesy light which can be switched on or off using the relevant switch or through a delay timer as described below. The courtesy light operation is timed according to a logic managed by the body computer: unlocking the doors using the remote control or by turning the key in the lock causes all the centre lights and the spot lights to come on; their operation is subject to a delay timer and if the doors are not opened after a few seconds the lights gradually go off. when the remote control door locking button is pressed for a while ("location" function) all the interior courtesy lights together with the direction indicators come on for a few seconds. when the key is turned to position S, the front courtesy light comes on; its operation is subject to a delay timer: the lights go out gradually after a few seconds. when one of the front doors is opened the centre light comes on, without the spot lights, so do the "puddle" courtesy lights [EL201]; their operation is subject to a delay timer: the lights go out gradually a few seconds after the doors are closed. See E2021 BRAKE LIGHTS when the engine is started up the lights go out gradually a few seconds later. when one of the rear doors is opened, the centre light comes on without the spot lights: operation is subject to a delay timer: a few seconds after the doors are closed, the lights go out gradually.

Operational Description The courtesy lights in the passenger compartment come on in "courtesy light" mode dependent on the opening of the door. The opening of the front doors is signalled via the switch incorporated in the locks N050 and N051. When the door is opened, the (normally closed type) switch provides an earth signal at pin 4 (left front door) and pin 5 (right front door) for connector L of the body computer node M001. Having received the signal, the body computer node M001, sends the command, from pin 32 connector L, to the front courtesy light G010, with a supply coming from the line protected by fuse F12 of M001. Having received the signal, the body computer node M001, sends the command, from pin 32 connector L, to the front courtesy light G010, with a supply coming from the line protected by fuse F12 of M001. The opening of the sliding side doors is signalled by specific switches I018 (left sliding side door) and I019 (right sliding side door). When the sliding side door is open, an earth signal reaches the body computer node M001 at pins 34 (left sliding side door) and 33 (right sliding side door) of connector L. The body computer node M001 sends a command, from pin 6 connector I, to the courtesy lights G011 and G012 providing a power supply for the bulbs contained inside. The front courtesy light mode can be disabled/enabled via switch I129. The enabling command is given by supplying an earth signal from pin B2 of I129 to pin 25 of connector L of M001; whilst the disabling command is given by supplying the same earth signal from pin A2 of I129 to pin 15 connector I of M001. For operation in manual mode, the body computer node M001 provides a supply, from pin 12 of connector H, coming from the line protected by fuse F07 of M001, directly to the front courtesy light G010 and to the rear courtesy lights G011 and G012. It is possisble to switch on the bulbs manually using the switches inside the courtesy lights G010, G011 and G012.

The front courtesy light and the centre courtesy light have three lamps with three control switches: - the corresponding spot light can be switched on using external switches; the centre switch can be used to switch the centre light on or off and the switching on is also subject to a delay timer ("courtesy lights" mode) as described below. There is only one bulb in the rear courtesy light which can be switched on or off using the relevant switch or through a delay timer as described below. The lighting of the courtesy lights is timed and they are switched on and off gradually, with an operating logic managed by the body computer: - when the doors are unlocked using the remote control or turning the key in the lock, all the centre and spot lights come on. Their operation is subject to a delay timer: if the doors are not opened, the lights go out gradually after a few seconds; - when the remote control door locking button is pressed for a while ("location" function) all the interior courtesy lights together with the direction indicators come on for a few seconds; - when the key is turned to position S the front courtesy light comes on. Their operation is subject to a delay timer: the lights go out gradually after a few seconds; - when one of the front doors is opened the centre courtesy light and the courtesy lights in the doors come on, but not the spot lights. Their operation is subject to a delay timer: a few seconds after the doors are closed, the lights go out gradually; - when the engine is started up the lights go out gradually a few seconds later; - when one of the rear doors is opened, the centre light comes on without the spot lights. Their operation is subject to a delay timer: a few seconds after the doors are closed, the lights go out gradually; - when the tailgate is opened the courtesy light(s) in the luggage compartment comes on (one or two depending on the trim level). They go out gradually when the tailgate is closed.

The courtesy lights in the passenger compartment come on in "courtesy light" mode dependent on the opening of the door. The opening of the front doors is signalled via the switch incorporated in the locks N050 and N051. See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING When the door is opened, the (normally closed type) switch provides an earth signal at pin 4 (left front door) and pin 5 (right front door) from pin 1 (pin 6 for versions with child locks) for connector L of the body computer node M001. Having received the signal, the body computer node M001 (pin 25 connector L) sends the command to the front courtesy light G010 (pin 4 connector A). The opening of the rear doors is signalled by specific switches: I018 for the left rear door and I019 for the right one. See E3095 SLIDING SIDE DOORS Depending on the rear door that is opened, an earth signal is sent (from pin 1 of I018 or I019) to the Body computer node M001 (pin 34 or pin 33 of connector L respectively). Having received the signal, the body computer node M001 (pin 29 connector L) sends the power supply to the courtesy light G011 (pin 4). For operation in manual mode, the Body computer node M001 provides a direct power supply (pin 20 connector I) for the front courtesy light G010 (pin 2 connector A) and for the rear courtesy lights G011 and G012 (pin 2). The various lamps can be switched on manually using the switches in the courtesy lights G010, G011 and G012.

Description When the tailgate is opened the courtesy lights (one on each side) located in the luggage compartment automatically come on. The courtesy lights go off gradually when the tailgate is closed. The courtesy lights go out after a few minutes to protect the battery charge. The light inside the glove compartment comes on - with the key in position M - when it is opened and goes out when it is closed. The lights located under each of the two sun visors come on when the visor is opened; both the courtesy lights at the side of the vanity mirror come on. The light for illuminating the ashtray is on with the key in position M.

Operational Description The glove compartmeng G030 courtesy light is activated when the glove compartment is opened, via the built-in switch: the switch provides the earth for the courtesy light bulb. According to the logic described previously, the body computer node M001 sends a supply, from pin 4 connector D, to the courtesy lights G030, via the line protected by fuse F07 housed in the body computer node M001. The ashtray light G035 is supplied by the body computer node M001 by the line protected by fuse F12 housed inside. The supply is controlled by the ignition and is operated by the relay inside the body computer node M001. The opening of the front doors is signalled via the switch incorporated in the locks N050 and N051. When the door is opened, the (normally closed type) switch provides an earth signal at pin 4 (left front door) and pin 5 (right front door) for connector L of the body computer node M001. Having received the signal, the body computer node M001, sends the command, from pin 32 connector L, to the front courtesy light G010, with a supply coming from the line protected by fuse F12 of M001. The opening of the tailgate is signalled by the specific switch I011: with the tailgate open, an earth signal reaches the body computer node M001 at pin 17 of connector I. In accordance with the logic described previously, the body computer node M001 sends a supply, from pin 4 connector I. to the rear courtesy lights G025 and G026. The body computer node M001 provides a supply for the operation of the sun visor lights G031 and G032, from pin 12 of connector H coming from the line protected by fuse F07 of M001, direct to the front courtesy light G010 [EL2510] and from there to the lights G031 and G032. See E2510 COURTESY LIGHTS

Description The vehicle is equipped with a horn system consisting of two horns with different tones: one high tone and one low tone: the two horns come on simultaneously. The horns are operated by pressing the sides of the steering wheel cover (around the Air Bag). The horn circuit is protected by a specific fuse and controlled by a relay located in the engine compartment junction unit. For safety reasons, the horns can be operated at any time even with the key in position S (or switched off).

Operational Description The command for the horns is supplied by the steering wheel node control unit M093 to the body computer node M001. The signal travels via the CAN which connects the two control units. The steering wheel node control unit M093 receives a supply (pin 5 connector A) through the line protected by fuse F11, located in the body computer node M001; it receives a supply via the CAN (pin 6 connector A) from the line protected by fuse F16, located in the body computer node M001. The signal is sent, via the CAN, to the engine compartment junction unit which supplies the horns P005 (pin 7 connector H of B001) via the line protected by fuse F13. The supply line is managed by a specific relay, located in the engine compartment junction unit B001.

Description The windscreen wash/wipe system is activated by the lever located on the right of the steering wheel, with the following functions: there are five possible positions for the lever, turning it in a clockwise direction, corresponding to: windscreen wiper off (stationary); automatic operation; continuous slow operation; continuous fast operation; "antipanic" temporary fast operation (unstable position, turning the lever in an anti-clockwise direction). In the automatic operation position, thanks to the rain sensor, the frequency of the windscreen wiper strokes can be adapted to suit the intensity of the rain. The frequency of the windscreen wiper strokes is automatically adjusted depending on the amount of water on the windscreen detected by the sensor: the frequency varies continuously from nil (no stroke - windscreen dry) to wiping at the second continuous speed (heavy rain) Activating the windscreen washers with the rain sensor activated produces the normal washing cycle at the end of which the rain sensor resumes its normal automatic operation. The windscreen washer function can be activated by pulling the lever toward the steering wheel: this activates the windscreen washer pump: keeping the lever pulled switches on the windscreen wiper for a three stroke cycle. A check on the functions described above is carried out by the body computer node which produces the intermittent function, controls the operation of the windscreen wiper motor and the windscreen washer pump and manages the rain sensor. The windscreen wiper and the windscreen washer can be activated with the key in position M. To facilitate maintenance, with the ignition key in position S or extracted, if the lever is turned downwards within 60 seconds, the windscreen wipers assume a vertical position and stop; they can be raised to replace the blades or for cleaning. If the windscreen wiper is activated, the lights come on automatically if this device is switched on.

Operational Description The command to switch on the windscreen wiper and the windscreen washer is given by the steering wheel node control unit M093 to the body computer node M001. The signal travels via the CAN which connects the two control units. The steering wheel node control unit M093 receives a supply (pin 5 connector A) through the line protected by fuse F11, located in the body computer node M001; it receives a supply via the CAN (pin 6 connector A) from the line protected by fuse F16, located in the body computer node M001. The body computer node M001 informs the engine compartment junction unit B001, via the CAN, of the request to activate the windscreen wiper and/or washer. The body computer node M001 supplies the coils for the relays, housed inside the engine compartment junction unit B001, connected in series, from pin 5 connector M. When the main relay is energized it closes its internal contact providing a direct battery supply for the secondary relay from the line protected by fuse F17. The secondary relay switches the supply from pin 9 to pin 1 connector F of M001 to the motor N015. When the electric motor reaches the end of travel position, it sends an earth signal to pin 3 connector M of M001. The engine compartment junction unit B001 is informed via the CAN of the windscreen wiper motor being in the end of travel position and switches the supply once again to pin 9 connector F allowing the windscreen wiper electric motor to return to the starting position. The rain sensor K085 receives an earth at pin 2 and sends signals to the body computer node M001 - pins 14 and 3 of connector L - which manages the automatic operation in relation to the weather conditions. The electric motor N022 carries out a dual windscreen and rearscreen washer function depending on the input of the motor power supply. For the windscreen washer function, the direct battery supply, protected by fuse F14, is provided by pin 14 connector F of the engine compartment junction unit B001 to the electric motor N022 whilst the earth is sent from pin 11. In addition to being protected by a specific fuse, the power supply provided is operated by a special relay also housed in the engine compartment junction unit.

Description The rearscreen wiper is activated by turning the ring nut on the end of the lever on the right of the steering wheel. The operation of the rearscreen wiper motor is controlled intermittently by the electronic device that also manages the windscreen wash/wipe function. Pushing the lever gently towards the steering wheel activates the rearscreen washer function, via the windscreen washer (two way) pump, which rotates in the opposite direction and sends the detergent fluid towards the back following the same control logic: the rearscreen wiper is activated and then, when the rearscreen washer command ends, an additional stroke is carried out. With the windscreen wipers working, if reverse gear is engaged, the rearscreen wiper is automatically activated: this function is managed by the Body Computer which sends the steering column switch unit electronic device this information coming from the reversing lights function control logic [EL2022]. See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS The rearscreen wash/wipe function can only be activated with the key in position M.

When the body computer node receives a request to switch on the rearscreen wiper, the electric motor is supplied at pin 1; when the end of travel position is reached, the switch inside the motor sends a signal from pin 2 to the body computer node M001, pin 9 connector I. The rear window washer function is activated by pressing the above stalk slightly towards the steering wheel. This function is achieved with the (two-way) windscreen washer pump: except it is made to turn in the opposite direction to send washer fluid to the rear of the vehicle. Once the rear wiper is activated, an extra sweep is made when the rear window washer control ceases. When reverse is engaged with the windscreen wiper operating, the rear wiper is operated automatically. See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS The rearscreen wash/wipe function can only be activated with the key in position M.

Steering wheel node control unit M093 receives power (pin 5 connector A and pin 4 connector D) from body computer node M001 (pin 11 connector B and pin 1 connector G respectively) via two lines, of which only the second is protected by fuse F04. The rear wiper and rear washer activation command is sent from steering wheel node control unit M093 (pins 1 and 3 connector A) to body computer node M001 (pins 5 and 3 of connector G respectively). The signal travels via the CAN line. Body computer node M001, in turn, sends a signal (pins 25 and 27 of connector E), via the CAN line, to engine compartment junction unit B001 (pins 12 and 11 respectively of connector F) to operate electric pump N022 and simultaneously supply (pin 5 connector H and pin 1 connector L) rear wiper motor N016 (pins 1 and 2 respectively). Electric motor N022 performs the dual function of operating the screen washer and rear window washer. It is supplied at pin 2 of engine compartment junction unit B001 (pin 2 connector G) via a line protected by fuse F03, and the signal returns to pin 1 connected to the same control unit (pin 5 connector G). Reversing switch I020 (or automatic transmission solenoid unit L050), when activated, carries an earth signal (pin 1 or A1) to engine compartment junction unit B001 (pin 13 or pin 15 connector F). The junction unit communicates the event (pins 11 and 12 connector F) via the CAN line to body computer node M001 (pins 27 and 25 connector E respectively), which (pin 5 connector H and pin 1 connector L) supplies rear wiper motor N016 (pins 1 and 2 respectively). See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS

Description The headlamp washer cleans the headlamp lenses as the windscreen is being cleaned. The headlamp washer function is managed by the Body Computer which automatically activates the headlamp washer, with the dipped or main beam headlamps on, when the windscreen washers are activated through the lever on the right of the steering wheel. The headlamp washer consists of a pump that sends detergent to a nozzle located in the bumpers. This in turn sprays a powerful jet on the headlamp. A timer activates the headlamp washer pump by means of a series of pulses lasting about half a second.

Operational Description The headlamp washer function is switched on by activating the windscreen wipers with the dipped headlamps on. Both controls are supplied by the steering wheel node control unit M093 ato the body computer node M001. The signal travels via the CAN which connects the two control units. The steering wheel node control unit M093 receives a supply (pin 5 connector A) through the line protected by fuse F11, located in the body computer node M001; it receives a supply via the CAN (pin 6 connector A) from the line protected by fuse F16, located in the body computer node M001. The body computer node M001 informst the engine compartment junction unit B001, via the CAN, of the request to activate the headlamp washers. The headlamp washer electric pump motor N025 receives a supply at pin 2 from the line protected by fuse F07 located in the engine compartment junction unit B001. In addition to being protected by a specific fuse, the power supply provided is operated by a special relay also housed in the engine compartment junction unit.

Description In the case of poor visibility it is possible to activate the demisting of the rearscreen and the exterior rear view mirrors. The heating resistances for these components absorb a considerable amount of energy and are therefore controlled and, possibly, deactivated after they have been working for a certain length of time: the demisting is subject to a delay timer, managed by the Body Computer, according to the following logic: key in position M engagement signal coming from the special button in the climate control system control panel. Under these circumstances the resistances remain supplied for a maximum of 20 minutes, then the supply is cut off. The supply is cut off in the following conditions: key in position S; disengagement signal from the button; battery voltage below 8.5 V; after the first 10 minutes of operation if the engine speed is below 1000 rpm. The control logic for the climate control system control unit also intervenes in the following situations: MAX-DEF command from the climate control: the defrosting is activated according to the logic described previously automatic defrosting at low outside temperatures: the heated rear windscreen is automatically switched on at low outside temperatures. The rearscreen defrosting circuit is controlled by a specific relay and protected by a fuse, both in the body computer node. The defrosting circuit for the door mirrors, on the other hand, is protected by another body computer node fuse and is controlled by the door control units, in accordance with the logic transmitted by the Body Computer via the CAN.

Operational Description The command for activating the heated rear windscreen is given by the special switched housed in the climate control system control unit M070. The command is sent to the body computer node M001 (pins 6, 8 and 10 connector D) via the CAN; the supply via the CAN is protected by fuse F24 of the body computer M001. The control unit M070 communicates the information that the heated rear windscreen is on to the instrument panel E050 as well at pins 5 and 9 and from there to the various displays [EL4010]. The body computer node M001 activates the internal relay and supplies the heated rear windscreen P055. The line is protected by fuse F26, also located in the body computer. The defrosting of the door mirrors P060 and P061 is also activated simultaneously. The command is supplied by the body computer node M001 to the door nodes M066 and M067 via the CAN, namely from pins 21, 23, and 24, 26 connector L to pins 14, 3 connector A of the driver's door node M066 and the passenger door node M067. The door nodes M066 and M067 receive a supply via the CAN (pin 1 connector A) from the line protected by fuse F04 of the body computer M001. The door nodes M066 and M067 are supplied by the body computer node at pin 16 connector from the line protected by fuse F09. Both the door nodes supply the internal resistance for the door mirrors P060 and P061 from pins 4 and 5 of connector B.

Description The door mirrors can be electrically adjusted in two directions using a joystick located in the door controls on the driver's side. Both mirrors are adjusted using the joystick which moves in four directions: firstly the mirror to be adjusted (left or right) is selected, then the mirror selected is adjusted. Moving the joystick backwards (by around 120°) folds the mirrors, moving it forwards, returns them to the open position. The joystick controls three electrical motors located in each of the two mirrors: one motor allows the rotation of the mirror on the horizontal axis, another on the vertical axis and the third controls the folding. The door mirrors are controlled by the door control units in accordance with the control logic transmitted by the body computer via the CAN. The mirrors can only be adjusted with the key in position M. The interior rear view mirror is the electrochrome type: i.e. it contains an electronic device which controls the automatic anti-glare function. The automatic mode is produced by pressing the button on the actual mirror; an LED signals that it is on. In order to ensure optimum visibility during manoeuvres, the interior mirror switches to automatic mode each time reverse gear is engaged. On versions with seats with a memory, in addition to moving the door mirrors manually, it is possible to memorize 4 positions: This complex logic is managed by the control unit for the seats/mirrors with a memory which converses with the Body Computer via the CAN [EL3076]. See E3076 ELECTRICALLY-ADJUSTABLE SEATS two linked to the remote controls for opening/closing the doors: when the doors are locked using the remote control, the position of the seat and the door mirrors is acquired by the remote control. When the doors are unlocked using the remote control, the seat and the door mirrors resume the position memorized previously; two linked to the memory buttons located on the driver's seat;

Operational Description The door nodes M066 and M067 are supplied by the body computer node at pin 16 connector from the line protected by fuse F09. The door nodes M066 and M067 receive a supply via the CAN (pin 1 connector A) from the line protected by fuse F04 of the body computer M001. The body computer node M001 also communicates with the door nodes M066 and M067 via the CAN, namely from pins 21, 23 and 24, 26, connector L to pins 14, 3 connector A of the driver's door node M066 and the passenger door node M067. The two door nodes M066 and M067 operate the electric motors for the door mirrors P060 and P061 directly. The command for the movement is given by unit H051 where the three specific switches are located: one for selecting the (left or right) door mirror, one for adjusting the mirror and one for folding the mirror. The door node M066 supplies the switch unit H051 from pin 15 connector A; the selection of the door mirror is signalled to pin 10 connector A of M066; the adjustment is managed by the signal sent to pin 6 connector A of M066; The door node M066 communicates with the passenger door node M067 via the CAN to operate the right mirror. The door nodes M066 and M067 control the electric motors for moving the respective door mirrors P060 and P061 from connector B, whilst they control the electric motors for folding the mirrors from connector C pins 2 and 3 and receive feedback signals of the effective position of the actual mirrors - pins 1, 4, 5 and 6. The interior rear view mirror P065 switches to the automatic mode each time reverse gear is engaged. When reverse gear is engaged the reversing switch I020 supplies the mirror P065 through the line protected by fuse F01 located in the engine compartment junction unit B001. The mirror P065 can also be activated manually by pressing the switch housed inside the actual mirror. In this case the supply is provided by the body computer node M001 (pin 12 connector H), by the line protected by fuse F07 housed in the actual control unit. On versions with seats with a memory, the movement of the mirrors in any of the 4 positions memorized is produced using the information transmitted via the CAN by the seats/mirrors with memory control unit M076.

The Body computer node M001 supplies the driver's door control unit M066 and the passenger door control unit M067, both at pin 1 of connector A from pin 9 of connector F. The command is supplied from the Body computer node M001 (pins 36, 38 connector I for the driver's side and pin 38, 40 connector L for the passenger side) to the door control units M066 and M067 (pins 19, 20 connector A) via the CAN. The control units M066 and M067 operate the electric motors for the door mirrors P060 and P061 directly. The command for the movement of the mirrors is given by unit H051 where the three specific switches are located: one for selecting the (left or right) door mirror, one for adjusting the mirror and one for folding the mirror. The door control unit M066 and the switch unit H051 interact to carry out a series of operations: - unit H051 is supplied at pin 2 of connector A from pin 16 of connector A at M066; - the selection of the mirror is communicated from pin 3 of connector A of unit H051 to pin 13 of the same connector of control unit M066; - the type of adjustment made is communicated from pin 1 of connector A of unit H051 to pin 14 of the same connector of control unit M066. To control the right mirror as well, the control unit M066 communicates via the CAN with control unit M067. Control units M066 and M067 control (pins 2, 1, 3 connector B) the electric movement motors for the rear view mirrors P060 and P061 (the same pins and connector) and (pins 2 and 3 connector C) the mirror folding electric motors (the same pins and connector). Lastly, mirrors P060 and P061 (pins 5, 4, 6, 1 connector C) communicate the feedback signals (same pins and connector) to the respective control units. Each time reverse gear is engaged, the interior rear view mirror P065 is placed in the automatic adjustment mode position. The reversing switch I020 (or the automatic transmission solenoid valve assembly L050) when engaged, sends an earth signal (pin 1 or A1) to the engine compartment junction unit B001 (pin 13 or pin 15 connector F). The latter communicates the event (pin 11 and 12 connector F) via the CAN line to the Body computer node M001 (pin 27 and 25 connector E respectively) which (pin 22 connector L) sends a power supply to the interior rear view mirror P065 (pin 3). The mirror P065 can also be activated manually by pressing the switch housed inside the actual mirror. In this case, the mirror will receive a power supply at pin 2 from pin 6 of connector F of the Body computer node M001. On versions with seats with a memory, the movement of the mirrors in any of the 4 positions memorized is produced using the information transmitted via the CAN by the seats/mirrors with memory control unit M076 (pin 3A and 3B connector A).

Description The simultaneous operation of the door locks takes place via: the key; the door handles; the interior button; the remote control; The remote control incorporated in the key has 2 buttons: one for activating the central locking (locking) command, switching on the alarm and the location function; one for activating the release of the central locking and switching off the alarm. Pressing the locking button for a while activates the so-called "location" function: all the interior courtesy lights, together with the direction indicators, come on for a few seconds. See E2510 COURTESY LIGHTS Pressing the unlocking button a second time activates the so-called "passenger compartment ventilation" function: the front and rear side windows open completely to allow the introduction of outside air into the passenger compartment. < R1 > < R2 > See E3051 ELECTRIC REAR WINDOWS The central locking button, located near the front courtesy light, makes it possible to lock and unlock all the doors from the inside. In addition, the handles on each of the four doors allow them to be opened from the inside and when the handle on any of the doors is operated, this operation unlocks all the other doors including the tailgate. The tailgate is fitted with a 2- position electric lock: The tailgate lock does not have a lock barrel, the opening of the tailgate is controlled by a button next to the number plate. This exterior button is switched off if the vehicle is locked, whilst it is activated: with the ignition key in position M or 1 min after the key is in position S. locked position (deactivated position), "released" position (activated position), The operation of the locks is managed by the Body Computer which controls the effective state of the locks by means of signals which arrive from the switches in the actual locks (these signals are also used for the lights delay timer): in this way, the "locking" command is only carried out if all the doors are properly shut and the locks unlocked; conversely, the "unlocking" command is only carried out if the locks are locked; The remote control receiver aerial is incoropated in the steering column switch unit (steering wheel node); the activation and/or deactivation information is sent to the Body Computer via the CAN. The automatic locking of the doors with the vehicle moving takes place, if the function is activated, when the speed of the vehicle reaches 10 km/h; pressing the central locking button briefly ( < 3 secs.) deactivates the automatic locking function until it is next switched off. The switching off and activation of the automatic locking function whilst driving can be activated by pressing the central locking button for a while. The tailgate lock is always activated and cannot be deactivated. In the case of an accident, the body computer receives the Air Bag activation information from the Air Bag control unit and controls the opening of all the doors. [EL 7030]

Operational Description The central locking is managed by the body computer node M001. The steering wheel node M093 receives the door open/closed signal from the remote control. The command (door opening or closing) is provided by the steering wheel node control unit M093 to the body computer node M001. The signal travels via the CAN which connects the two control units. The steering wheel node control unit M093 receives a supply (pin 5 connector A) through the line protected by fuse F11, located in the body computer node M001; it receives a supply via the CAN (pin 6 connector A) from the line protected by fuse F16, located in the body computer node M001. The command for opening/closing the doors can also be sent by the internal switch I110. Pressing the special switch on unit I110 sends an earth signal indicating that the locks have been locked/unlocked from pin 6 to the body computer node M001 (pin 14 connector I). Pins 1 and 4 of I110 receive a power supply to light up the LEDs at pin 9 connector D and at pin 12 connector F of the body computer node M001; the supply provided by pin 12 connector F of M001 is protected by fuse F12 and operated by a specific relay, both housed inside the body computer node. The body computer node M001 sends supplies, from pins 13 and 15 connector F, to the electric motors for the door locks N055, N056, N050, and N051 opening or closing the doors depending on the command received. The front door locks N050 and N051 communicate, from pin 4, with the body computer M001, at pins 27 and 29 of connector L, informing it of the state of the door (locked/unlocked). The locks inform the body computer node, from pin 6, of the door status (open/closed) at pins 4 and 5. The opening of the sliding side doors is signalled by specific switches I018 (left sliding side door) and I019 (right sliding side door) to pin 34 (left door) and 33 (right door) of connector L of M001. The electric boot lock N057 is controlled by the body computer node M001 by pin 2 connector I and the boot closed signal is provided by pin 3 N057 to pin 16 connector I of the body computer node. The body computer node M001 receives the signal coming from the boot switch I011 at pin 17 of this connector.

Description The door node control units control the operation of the driver and passenger side front electric window motors. The electric motors for the front windows are incorporated in the door nodes. Information on the current position of the windows and the opening/closing commands through the operation of the remote control is provided via the CAN. The driver's electric window is equipped with a device (which operates when the engine is started) that works continuously according to the following logic: if the button is pressed is between 60 and 300 milliseconds, operation is manual. the glass goes up/down only with the key pressed; f the key is pressed for longer than 300 milliseconds, operation is automatic: even if the button is released, the glass continues to move up/down until the end of travel position is reached or until the intervention of the anti-crush safety system (if fitted); pressing the button again whilst the window is moving stops it in the position it is in; if the button is pressed for less than 60 milliseconds, this is ignored (it is treated as an accidental knock). The electric windows are equipped with an anti-crush safety system: the control unit in the door is capable of detecting the presence of any obstacles whilst the window is closing by means of anti-crush safety sensors: in this case, the system interrupts the travel of the window and reverses the direction immediately. If the remote control button is pressed in order to activate the "passenger compartment ventilation" function: the front and rear side windows open completely to allow the introduction of outside air into the passenger compartment. See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING After the battery has been disconnected, if the electric windows do not work when there is an attempt to close them, the system must be initialized: release the control and operate it a second time until the roof is completely closed, keeping it activated for more than a second after the end of travel position has been reached: in this way regular operation will be resumed. With the key in position S, the windows remain activated for around 1 minute.

Operational Description The electric motors for the front windows are incorporated in the door nodes M066 and M067. The door nodes M066 and M067 are supplied by the body computer node at pin 16 connector from the line protected by fuse F09. The door nodes M066 and M067 receive a supply via the CAN (pin 1 connector A) from the line protected by fuse F04 of the body computer M001. The body computer node M001 also communicates with the door nodes M066 and M067 via the CAN, namely from pins 21, 23 and 24, 26, connector L to pins 14, 3 connector A of the driver's door node M066 and the passenger door node M067. Information on the current position of the windows and the opening/closing commands through the operation of the remote control is provided via the CAN. It is possible to open/close the two front electric windows using the driver's side switch H051. The supply for the lighting is provided by the driver's door node M066 from pin 15 connector A, the earth from pin 9 connector A; the control unit M066 receives the window activation signal at pins 4 and 5 of connector A. The command for opening/closing the passenger side window also takes place through the switch H050; the supply for the lighting is provided by node M067 from pin 15 connector A which receives the window activation signal at pins 4 and 5 of connector A. The door node control units control the operation of the driver and passenger side front electric window motors. The electric motors for the front windows are incorporated in the door nodes. Information on the current position of the windows and the opening/closing commands through the operation of the remote control is provided via the CAN. The driver's electric window is equipped with a device (which operates when the engine is started) that works continuously according to the following logic: if the button is pressed is between 60 and 300 milliseconds, operation is manual. the glass goes up/down only with the key pressed; f the key is pressed for longer than 300 milliseconds, operation is automatic: even if the button is released, the glass continues to move up/down until the end of travel position is reached or until the intervention of the anti-crush safety system (if fitted); pressing the button again whilst the window is moving stops it in the position it is in; if the button is pressed for less than 60 milliseconds, this is ignored (it is treated as an accidental knock). The electric windows are equipped with an anti-crush safety system: the control unit on the door is capable of detecting the presence of any obstacles whilst the window is closing; in this case it interrupts the travel of the window and reverses it immediately. With the key in position S, the windows remain activated for around 1 minute. When the remote control button is pressed in order to activate the "passenger compartment ventilation" function, the front and rear side windows open completely to allow outside air to enter the passenger compartment. See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING After the battery has been disconnected, if the electric windows do not work when there is an attempt to close them, the system must be initialized: release the control and operate it a second time until the roof is completely closed, keeping it activated for more than a second after the end of travel position has been reached; in this way the system will resume normal operation.

The Body computer node M001 supplies the driver's door control unit M066 and the passenger door control unit M067, both at pin 1 of connector A from pin 9 of connector F. The command is supplied from the Body computer node M001 (pins 36, 38 connector I for the driver's side and pin 38, 40 connector L for the passenger side) to the door control units M066 and M067 (pins 19, 20 connector A) via the CAN. Information on the current position of the windows and the opening/closing commands through the operation of the remote control is provided via the CAN. The door control unit M066 and the switch unit H051 interact to carry out a series of operations: - unit H051 is supplied at pin 2 of connector A from pin 16 of connector A at M066; - the earth signal at pin 5 of the same connector at H051 is supplied from pin 17 of connector A at M066; - the activating signal for the windows is sent from pins 4 and 6 of connector A of unit H051 to pins 3 and 14 of the same connector of control unit M066. The opening/closing command for the passenger window also takes place through switch H050 which interacts with the door control unit M067: - H050 is supplied at pin 2 from pin 16 of connector A at M067; - the windows activating signal is sent from pins 3 and 6 of H050 to pins 7 and 2 of connector A respectively of control unit M067.

If the remote control button is pressed in order to activate the "passenger compartment ventilation" function: the front and rear side windows open completely to allow the introduction of outside air into the passenger compartment See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING

Operational Description The electric motors for the rear windows N065 and N066 are supplied at pin 3 of the body computer node M001 (pin 8 connector F) by the line protected by fuse F15 housed inside the actual control unit. The command for opening/closing the windows is given by the switches H053 (left) and H054 (right). The switches receive the lighting supply from the body computer node M001 (pin 12 connector L) from pin 2, whilst pin 5 is connected to earth The signal for opening the window is supplied from pin 6 of the switch units H053 and H054 to motors N065 and N066 at pin 6. The same signal is also supplied to the body computer node M001, at pin 19 and 9 of connector L. The signal for closing the window is supplied from pin 3 of the switch units H053 and H054 to motors N065 and N066 at pin 6. The same signal is also supplied to the body computer node M001, at pin 20 and 10 of connector L. The door node M066 receives a supply from the body computer node at pin 16 connector A from the line protected by fuse F09; a supply is received via the CAN (pin 1 connector A) from the line protected by fuse F04 of the body computer M001. It is connected to the body computer node via the CAN at pins 21, 23 of connector L of M001. It is possible to disable the opening/closing of the rear windows, using the driver's front switch unit H051, by pressing the special switch housed in the unit. The signal is supplied from pin 2 connector B of H051 to pin 11 connector A of the door node M066. The door node M066 informs the body computer node M001, via the CAN, of the command to exclude the rear windows. The body computer node M001 disables the command coming for switches H053 and H054 from pins 19 and 20.

Description The vehicle may be equipped with three electric sun roofs - front, centre and rear - that can be activated using the control buttons but only with the key in position M. With the key in position S, the roof controls remain activated for around 1 minute. The roofs are fitted with a sliding sun blind and an anti-crush safety system. The control unit is capable of detecting the presence of an obstacle whilst the roof is closing by means of the anti-crush safety sensors: in this case, the system interrupts the travel of the window and reverses the direction immediately. After the battery has been disconnected, if the roof does not work when the closing control is operated, the system must be initialized: release the control and operate it a second time until the roof is completely closed, keeping it activated for more than a second after the end of travel position has been reached: in this way regular operation will be resumed. There are two control switches at the front: one for the front roof; for the simultaneous operation, from the front seats, of the centre and rear roofs; There is a control switch, in the centre and at the back, for the centre and roof roofs, respectively. Each roof can be initially tilted open/closed and then fully opened/closed For the safety of the rear passengers (children) the system allows the inhibition of the controls in the second and third rows by pressing the "locking" button located on the driver's front door which cuts off the power supply to the switches on the rear doors < R1 > and the sliding doors < R2 > See E3095 SLIDING SIDE DOORS

Operational Description The controls for the centre sun roof N155 and the rear sun roof N156 receive a supply, at pin 6, from the line for fuses F35 and F34, respectively, located in the additional fuse box B098. The controls for the front sun roof N036, on the other hand, receive a supply at pin 6 of the body computer node M001 (pin 10 connector F) from the line protected by fuse F09. Pins 1, 8 of N155, 1, 7 of N156 and 1 of N036 are earthed. The electric motors N036, N155 and N156 interface with the CAN, from pins 4 and 5, communicating with the body computer node M001 at pins 11, 13 of connector I; they also receive a supply via the CAN, at pin 10, from the line protected by fuse F01 of the body computer M001. The three sun roofs are opened and closed via switches H061, I120, I121 and I122. Switch H061 controls the opening/closing of the front sun roof N036. Pin 2 receives a positive signal coming from pin 2 of the sun roof motor N036. By pressing the switch in position A, a signal is sent from pin 3 of H061 to pin 3 of N036, controlling the opening of the roof. In position B, the signal is sent from pin 6 of H061 to pin 9 of N036, controlling the closing of the sun roof. Switch I120 controls the opening/closing of the centre sun roof N155. Pin 2 receives a positive signal coming from pin 2 of the sun roof motor N155. By pressing the switch in position A, a signal is sent from pin 3 of I120 to pin 3 of N155, controlling the opening of the roof. In position B, the signal is sent from pin 6 of H120 to pin 9 of N155, controlling the closing of the sun roof. Switch I121 controls the opening/closing of the rear sun roof N156. Pin 2 receives a positive signal coming from pin 2 of the sun roof motor N156. By pressing the switch in position A, a signal is sent from pin 3 of I121 to pin 3 of N156, controlling the opening of the roof. In position B, the signal is sent from pin 6 of I121 to pin 9 of N156, controlling the closing of the sun roof. A positive signal is supplied by pin 2 of the front sun roof N036 to pin 2 of the actual switch. Pressing the switch in position A sends a signal from pin 3 of I122 at pin 3 of the centre sun roof motor N155 and from pin 1 of I122 to pin 3 of the rear sun roof motor M156, controlling the opening of both. Pressing the switch in position B sends a signal from pin 6 of I122 at pin 9 of the centre sun roof motor N155 and from pin 4 of I122 to pin 9 of the rear sun roof motor M156, controlling the closing of both. Switch I122 controls the opening/closing of both the centre sun roof N155 and the rear sun roof N156. Using the driver's front switches H051, it is possible to disable both the opening/closing of the rear windows < R1 > and the controls for the centre and rear roofs. See E3051 ELECTRIC REAR WINDOWS The signal is supplied from pin 2 connector B of H051 to pin 11 connector A of the door node M066. The door node M066 informs the body computer node M001, via the CAN, of the command to exclude the rear windows and roofs.

Description The front seats are available, on request, with a special heating system (comprising two heating elements located in the cushion and the backrest): this allows the seat to be heated to overcome the discomfort of cold passenger compartments in very harsh climates, e.g. when the car is left in the open for long periods in winter. The heating device located in each seat consists of two resistors activated by a switch located on the outside of the seat. There are four positions for the control for switching the heating system on/off: 0 = off; 1 = minimum heating; 2 = medium heating; 3 = maximum heating. A special LED in the actual switches indicates that the resistances are switched on. The resistances can be switched on with the engine running. This logic is managed by a specific control unit for each seat. The circuit for each seat is protected by a specific fuse, located in the additional fuse box

Operational Description The command for the electrical heating of the front seats is activated by switches I065 and I066 housed in the actual seats. The body computer node M001 supplies the switches I065 and I065 and the seat heating control units M110 and M170 from pin 22 connector L (at pin 3 connector A). The switches I065 and I066 provide the control units (pin 2 connector A) from pin 1 with a voltage that varies according to the position of the selector. Having received the signal from connector B, the control unit M170 and/or M110 activates the resistance for heating the cushion of the respective seat O046 and O047. The resistance for heating the backrest of the respective seat O048 and/or O049 is activated by connector C. The power supplies for the control units M170 and M110 arrive from the lines protected by fuses F37 and F36 located in the additional fuse box B098.

The front seats may be equipped with a special heating system comprising two elements located in the cushion and the backrest: this allows the seat to be heated to overcome the discomfort of cold passenger compartments, e.g. when the car is left in the open for long periods in winter. The heating device, located in both front seats, consists of two resistors operated by a switch located on the outside of each seat. There are four positions for the control for switching the heating system on/off: - 0 = off; - 1 = minimum heating; - 2 = medium heating; - 3 = maximum heating. A special LED in the actual switches indicates that the resistances are switched on. The resistances can be switched on with the engine running.

The command for the electrical heating of the front seats is activated by switches I065 and I066 housed in the actual seats. The body computer node M001 supplies (pin 7 connector H) the switches I065 and I065 (pin 3) and the seat heating control units M110 and M170 (pin 3 connector A). The switches I065 and I066 (pin 1) provide the control units M170 and M110 (pin 2 connector A) with a voltage that varies according to the position of the selector. Once the signal is received, the control units activate: - from pins 1, 2, 3, 4 of connector B, the resistance for heating the cushion for the seat O046 and O047 (pins 1, 2, 3, 4 respectively); - from pins 1 and 2 of connector C, the resistance for heating the backrest O048 and O049 (pins 1, 2).

Description The vehicle can be fitted with electrically adjustable front seats a button adjusts the lengthwise movement (forwards/backwards) and height adjustment; a button adjusts the backrest; Each of the adjustments is carried out by a specific electric motor. The backrest lumbar setting can be mechanically adjusted on the driver's seat. The adjustments can be made with the ignition key in position M and for about 1 minute after the key is turned to position S. The circuit for each seat is protected by a specific fuse, located in the additional fuse box.

Operational Description The electric adjustment of the front seats is operated by specific switches, housed in the seats, H066 and H067 and controlled by two specific relays J139 and J140 also housed in the seats. The body computer node M001 provides the CAN supply, via two specific relays, housed inside and the line protected by fuse F01, to the relay J139 and J140 coils at pin 1 which is thereby energized. The relays receive a power supply, at pin 3, from the lines protected by fuses F32 and F36, located in the additional fuse box B098, which is then sent from pin 5 to the switches H066 and H067, pin 3; pin 4 is earthed. The switches H066 and H067 operate the electric motors, from pins 5 and 6, for adjusting the position of the backrest: motors N132 and N135, respectively. The motors for adjusting the lengthwise position of the seat, N127 and N130, are operated from pins 1 and 2.

Description The vehicle can be fitted with electrically adjustable front seats lengthwise movement (forwards/backwards0 height adjustment; backrest adjustment Each of the adjustments is carried out by a specific electric motor. On the versions with "seats with a memory", 4 different positions can be memorized for the driver's seat two linked to the remote controls for opening/closing the doors: when the doors are locked using the remote control, the position of the seat and the door mirrors is acquired by the remote control. When the doors are unlocked using the remote control, the seat and the door mirrors resume the position memorized previously; two linked to the memory buttons on the actual seat. the positions memorized also include the position of the door mirrors [EL3032]. The adjustments can be made with the ignition key in position M and for about 1 minute after the key is turned to position S. This complex logic is managed by the seats/mirrors with memory control unit which converses with the Body Computer via the CAN The circuit is protected by a specific fuse, located in the additional fuse box

Operational Description The control unit for the seats/mirrors with a memory M076 manages the function of adjusting the seats according to the position memorized and also controls the movement of the door mirrors using information transmitted the body computer M001 via the CAN See E3032 DOOR MIRROR ADJUSTMENT The seats/mirrors with memory control unit M076 receives a supply at pins B7 and B8 connector A along the line protected by fuse F32 located in the additional fuse box B098; it is earthed at pins C8 and C7 connector A and converses, via the CAN, with the body computer control unit M001 from pins C5 and A5 connector A. The supply via the CAN arrives at pin A7 from the line protected by fuse F1 of the body computer M001. The adjustment of the driver's seat is controlled by the switch H066 which is connected rom pins 1, 2, 3 and 4 to pins A3, B2, B3 and C2 connector B of the control unit M076. The adjustment signals are managed by the seats/mirrors with memory control unit M076 The left front seat sliding adjustment motor N127, the left front seat front height adjustment motor N126 and the left front seat backrest motor N132 receive the control signals from pins B7 and A7, A1 and C8, B1 and C2 connector B of control unit M076. The height position sensor K178 and the sliding sensor K179 and the backrest position sensor K180 refer the seat position variations to the feedback signals: the three sensors receive a supply from pin C6 of connector B of M076, a reference earth at pin C4 and send a signal to pins C5, A5 and B4 of connector B of M076, respectively.

Description The adjustment of the headlamp light beam according to the load is carried out by means of a special device (located inside the front light cluster) which tilts it appropriately, lowering the light beam if the vehicle is heavily laden and raising it if the load lessens. A rotary selector on the left side of the dashboard allows the headlights to be adjusted from positions 0 to 3: position 0 - one or two persons in the front seats, full fuel tank, fully equipped (vehicle in running order); position 1 - five persons; position 2 - five persons with luggage compartment full; position 3 - seven or eight persons with luggage compartment full, or driver and maximum load, all in the luggage compartment. The device is enabled only with the dipped beams on. A special relay, located in the body computer, supplies the adjustment motors incorporated inside the headlights. on versions with gas discharge headlamps, the light beam is adjusted automatically and there is no rotary selector on the left side

Operational Description Headlamp alignment adjustment is managed by a dedicated selector H015. Pin 2 receives a supply from the battery via fuse F12 located in the body computer node M001. This supply is only provided if the dipped headlamps are switched on, via the relay, also located in the body computer node M001. The relay is controlled by the body computer node M001 as soon as the dipped headlamps are switched on < R1 > . Pin 3 of H015 is earthed, whilst a variable voltage signals is sent from pin 3 to pin 7 of the front light clusters F010 and F011. See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS The correction motors inside the headlamps contain a transducer that estabilishes the travel to be completed on the basis of adjustment signal voltage. The motors receive a power supply from pin 9 of the front light clusters F010 and F011 from the line protected by fuse F12 of the body computer node M001. The dipped headlamps are connected at pin 1 of the front light clusters F010 and F011. See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS

Description The vehicle is fitted with two GAS DISCHARGE headlamps. The function in question is managed by electronics inside the two headlamps by means of two sensor (potentiometer) signals, located on the wheel axles that measure the front and rear geometry. Depending on the inputs, the control unit controls the relevant adjustment motor, located in the headlamps, directly and tilts it as appropriate. The device is enabled only with the dipped beams on. The relay which controls the engagement of the dipped headlamps < R1 > also supplies the geometry sensors, whilst the electronics for the two headlamps is supplied by the line for a specific fuse. See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS on versions with gas discharge headlamps, the light beam is adjusted automatically and the two buttons in the left panel are not activated. The headlamp electronic control units have an autodiagnostic function. When a diagnostic tester is connected to these control units, via the diagnostic connector on the left side of the dashboard, self-diagnosis data can be read (parameters, errors) or the available active diagnostic tests can be carried out.

Operational Description The automatic headlamp adjustment system is only supplied with the dipped headlamps on See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS The sensors K001 (pin 5) and K002 (pins 2, 5) that control the vehicle geometry, are supplied by the engine compartment junction unit B001 (pin 15 connector C) and the supply line is protected by fuse F09 which also protects the supply for the front light cluster F010 dipped headlamp bulb. Pins 1, 2 of sensor K001 and pin 1 of sensor K002 are earthed. Sensors K001 and K002 provide the electronics incorporated in the headlamps F010 and F011, pin 7 with information concerning the vehicle geometry from pin 4. The electric motors automatically correct the light beam according to the information received. The electronics are also supplied at pin 9 of F010 and F011 by the engine compartment junction unit B001 (pin 10 connector C) from the line protected by fuse F01 of the junction unit. The self-diagnostic data for the two control units can be read by connecting to connector F10 - pin 13: it receives signals from pin 5 of F010 and F011 via the special diagnostic line.

The adjustment of the light beam for the headlamps depending on the load is produced using the adjustment device located directly on the headlamps. This device tilts the light beam in order to lower it if the vehicle is particularly laden or to raise it if the load lessens. A rotary selector on the left side of the dashboard allows the headlights to be adjusted in four positions: - position 0 - one or two persons in the front seats, full fuel tank, fully equipped (vehicle in running order); - position 1 - five persons; - position 2 - five persons with luggage compartment laden; - position 3 - seven or eight persons with luggage compartment laden, or driver and maximum load, all in the luggage compartment. Adjust the alignment of the light beams each time the weight of the load transported changes. The device is enabled only with the dipped beams on. The body computer supplies the adjustment motors incorporated in the headlamps. On the version with gas discharge headlamps the light beam is adjusted automatically: there is no rotary selector on the left side of the dashboard.

Headlamp alignment adjustment is managed by a dedicated selector H015. Pin 2 of H015 (like pin 9 of the front light clusters F010 and F011) receive a power supply from pin 2 of connector B of the Body computer node M001. This power supply is only provided with the dipped headlamps on. Pin 3 of H015 is earthed together with pin 8 of connector B of the Body computer node M001, whilst a variable voltage signal is sent from pin 1 to pin 7 of the left front light cluster F010 and the right front light cluster F011. The headlamp alignment correction motors inside the front light clusters contain a transducer that estabilishes the travel to be completed on the basis of adjustment signal voltage. The dipped headlamps are connected to pin 1 of the front light clusters F010 and F011, supplied from pins 25 and 26 respectively of connector G of the engine compartment junction unit B001. See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS
