The device which controls the engagement of the dipped headlamps also supplies the geometry sensors, whilst the electronics for the two headlamps is supplied by a line protected by a specific fuse. See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS On the version with gas discharge headlamps, the adjustment of the light beam takes place automatically: the two buttons on the left side of the dashboard are not operational. The headlamp electronic control units have an autodiagnostic function. When a diagnostic tester is connected to these control units, via the diagnostic connector on the left side of the dashboard, the data can be read (parameters, errors) or the available active diagnostic tests can be carried out.

The automatic headlamp adjustment system is only supplied with the dipped headlamps on. See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS The sensors K001 (pin 5) and K002 (pins 2 and 5) that control the vehicle geometry receive a power supply from the engine compartment junction unit B001 (pin 25 connector G). Pin 1 of K002 and pins 1 and 2 of K001 are earthed. Sensors K001 and K002 provide the electronics incorporated in the headlamps F010 and F011 (pin 7) with information concerning the vehicle geometry from pin 4. The electric motors automatically correct the light beam according to the information received. The electronics are also supplied at pin 9 of F010 and F011 by the engine compartment junction unit B001 (pin 20 connector C) from the line protected by fuse F01 of the junction unit. The self-diagnostic data for the two control units can be read by connecting to the multiple diagnostic coupling R010 (pin 13): it receives the signals from pin 5 of F010 and F011.

Description This is a device that allows easy manoeuvring whilst parking: when reverse gear is engaged, it signals to the driver that an obstacle, which may be outside of the range of vision, is being approached. It operates according to an ultrasound sonar principle: four ultrasound transducers are located inside the rear bumper. They send signals to a control unit which processes this information determining the distance of possible obstacles. A speaker controlled by the control unit emits an intermittent sound, proportional to the distance of the obstacle detected. The control unit is activated with reverse gear engaged: in these conditions, it energizes the transducers and sends them a signal request, receiving the response signals. The control unit emits a signal with an intermittent sound through the special speaker: the frequency of this sound increases gradually as the bumper approaches an obstacle: when the distance calculated goes below 25 cm, the sound becomes high-pitched and constant. If the distance of the obstacle detected increases, or if the driver disengages reverse gear, the sound stops. If the distance of the obstacle detected remains constant, the sound stops after about 3 seconds. The signal that reverse gear is engaged < R1 > is managed by the body computer which sends this information to the parking sensor control unit via the CAN. See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS The operation of the parking sensors is automatically deactivated when the trailer is electrically connected. The sensors are automatically reactivated when the trailer is disconnected.

Operational Description When reverse gear is engaged, the apporpriate command is sent by the switch I020, located on the gearbox. The switch is supplied by the engine compartment junction unit B001 (pin 10 connector C) through the line protected by fuse F01 located in the actual junction unit. When reverse gear is engaged, the switch I020 closes its internal contact, sending the signal to the body computer node M001 (pin 5 connector B). On versions with automatic transmission, there is no reversing switch on the gearbox, but this function is carried out by a special contact "R" for the automatic transmission solenoid valve unit L050 Having received the command, the body computer node M001 closes the contact inside the relay and supplies the parking sensor control unit M084 (pin 1 connector A) via the line protected by fuse F24 (pin 3 connector H); control unit M084 is earthed at pin 7 connector A. The control unit M084 operates the speaker P044, used as an acoustic warning for signalling that reverse gear is engaged and that the parking sensors are activated, from pins 2, 10. The parking control unit M084 receives information, from connector B, from the parking sensor unit K097, located in the rear bumper, which measures the distance between the vehicle and any obstacles. A system inhibition signal reaches pin 12 if a trailer is connected via coupling D73. Connector D73 also receives a supply from the body computer node M001 via the line protected by fuse F10.

This device facilitates the parking stage: when reverse is engaged, it indicates the approach of an obstacle that could be outsid the driver's visual range. The system consists of four ultrasound sensors located inside the bumpers that send given signals to a specific control unit: once processed, the control unit is able to calculate the distance from possible obstacles and communicate it by means of a speaker, emitting an intermittent sound signal at a frequency proportional to the distance from the detected obstacle. When the calculated distance is less than 25 [cm], the sound emitted becomes acute and constant. If the distance of the obstacle detected increases, or if the driver disengages reverse gear, the sound stops. The control unit is activated with reverse gear engaged: If the distance of the obstacle detected remains constant, the sound stops after about 3 seconds. The signal that reverse gear is engaged is managed by the body computer node which sends this information to the parking sensor control unit via the CAN. See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS The operation of the parking sensors is automatically deactivated when the trailer is electrically connected. The sensors are automatically reactivated when the trailer is disconnected. See E2050 TRAILER WIRING

When reverse is engaged, a switch I020 (pin 1) closes its internal contact and sends an earth signal to engine compartment control unit B001 (pin 13 connector F). On versions with automatic transmission, switch I020 is not present: the same function is performed by a contact "R" of automatic transmission solenoid unit L050 that is connected to pin 15 of connector F of B001 from pin A1. Control unit B001 (pins 11 and 12 connector F) communicates reverse engagement via the CAN line to body computer M001 (pins 27 and 25 connector E respectively), which takes action to: - turn on the reversing lights from pins 15 and 16 of connector H; See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS - supply parking sensor M084 at pin 10 of connector A via a line protected by fuse F12 from pin 11 of connector F. If a trailer is connected, body computer node M001 (pins 37 and 39 connector I) receive a connection signal from trailer service control unit and inhibit (pins 36 and 38 connector I) parking sensor M084 (pins 5 aned 14 connector A). See E2050 TRAILER WIRING See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES Control unit M084 receives signals from parking sensor K097 at connector B. In particular: - pins 2 of the sensors are connected to pins 9, 10, 3 and 4; - pins 1 to pin 8; - pins 3 to pin 2. The reverse engagement and obstacle detection buzzer is built into the system.

Description The two sliding side doors can be opened/closed electrically from the inside: from the front seats using the buttons next to the courtesy light from the centre seats using the buttons on the appropriate door pillar. When the button is pressed, the lock unlocks and the sliding door opens; when the button is pressed again, the door closes. The sliding side doors can be opened electrically using the special button on the remote control. The remote control built into the key on the version in question has 4 buttons: one for activating the (locking) command for the central locking, for switching on the alarm and for the location function < R1 > < R2 > (Wiring Diagram ) E7015 ALARM one for activating the unlocking of the central locking and for switching off the alarm < R1 > < R2 > (Wiring Diagram ) E7015 ALARM one for opening/closing the right sliding side door one for opening/closing the left sliding side door The remote control receiver aerial is incoropated in the steering column switch unit (steering wheel node); the activation and/or deactivation information is sent to the Body Computer via the CAN. Both the sliding doors are fitted with an anti-crush safety sensor which intervenes according to two different operating logics: during opening: if there is an obstacle, the door automatically stops; during closing: if there is an obstacle, the door stops and automatically reverses direction, opening fully. In this case, to restore correct operation, an electric command must be given using the remote control buttons or one of the buttons in the vehicle. In addition, for safety reasons, a special "locking" switch, located on the driver's front door, allows the opening/closing of the sliding doors (as well as the operation of the electric windows in the rear doors < R1 > and the rear sun roofs < R2 > to be excluded so that their operation can be prevented, for example if children are present. See E3060 SUN ROOF The operating logic described above is controlled by the sliding door node which supervises the operation of the two movement motors for each door: one unlocks the lock, the other moves the door by means of a geared motor or two cables connected to the door guide pulley The initialization procedure is carried out in the following cases: battery disconnection, removing/refitting sliding door motor. To initialize the system it is necessary to: start with the door closed; control an opening (electrical); control a closing (electrical); control another opening (electrical). the initialization is not lost from the system after the door is closed manually.

Operational Description The steering wheel node M093 receives the door open/closed signal from the remote control. The command (door opening or closing) is provided by the steering wheel node control unit M093 to the body computer node M001. The signal travels via the CAN which connects the two control units. The steering wheel node control unit M093 receives a supply (pin 5 connector A) through the line protected by fuse F11, located in the body computer node M001; it receives a supply via the CAN (pin 6 connector A) from the line protected by fuse F16, located in the body computer node M001. The signal reaches the steering wheel node control unit M093 and is sent, via the CAN, to the sliding side door node M171, connected to the network via pins 11, 13 connector A. The sliding side door node M171 receives a supply, via the CAN (pin 4 connector A) from the line protected by fuse F01 for the body computer node M001. Pins 1, 8 connector A receive a direct supply via the line protected by fuses F01 and F02 of the maxifuse box B005; the control unit is earthed at pins 9, 16. The command for the electrical opening of the sliding side doors comes from the specific switches fitted in the courtesy light I133 (left side) and I134 (right side) or from the switches on the centre pillars I135 (left side) and I136 (right side). All the switches receive a supply, at pin 4, via the CAN, from the line protected by fuse F01 of the body computer node M001. The switches are earthed at pin 3, whilst an earth signal is sent from pin 6 to control unit M171, to pins 2, 15, 3 and 6, connector A, respectively to control the opening of the specific sliding side door. The control unit M171 controls the electric motors for the locks N166 left and N167 right from pins 5, 14 of connector A. The control unit receives the signal, at pins 10, 7, that the locks are correctly locked from the door switches I137 and I138, respectively. The electric motors for moving the sliding side doors N168 and N169 are controlled by pins 1, 2 connector B and pins 1, 2 connector E, respectively. Switches I131 and I132 notify the control unit that the sliding side doors are correctly closed. Switch I131 is connected to connector C of control unit M171 and switch I132 is connected to connector D of the control unit. The control unit provides the switches with a supply from pins 3, 4 of connector C and D for the warning light incorporated in the actual switches.

The two sliding side doors can be opened/closed electrically from the inside: - from the front seats using the buttons next to the courtesy light - from the centre seats using the buttons on the appropriate door pillar. When the button is pressed, the lock IS unlocked and the door opens; when the button is pressed again, the door closes. The same operations can also be carried out using the remote control. The remote control incorporated in the key has 4 buttons: - one for activating the central locking (locking) command, switching on the alarm and the location function; - one for activating the release of the central locking and switching off the alarm; See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING See E7015 ALARM - one for opening/closing the right sliding side door; - one for opening/closing the left sliding side door. The remote control receiver aerial is incorpated in the steering column switch unit (steering wheel node); the activation and/or deactivation information is sent to the Body Computer via the CAN. Both the sliding doors are fitted with an anti-crush safety sensor which intervenes according to two different operating logics: - during opening: if there is an obstacle, the door automatically stops; - during closing: if there is an obstacle, the door stops and automatically reverses direction returning it to the original position. In this case, to restore correct operation, the command must be given using the special buttons on the remote control or from inside the vehicle. For safety reasons, a special "locking" switch, located on the driver's front door, allows the exclusion of the opening/closing of the sliding side doors, the operation of the windows in the rear doors and the rear sun roofs: this is a useful function, for example if children are present. See E3051 ELECTRIC REAR WINDOWS See E3060 SUN ROOF The operating logic described above is controlled by the sliding door node which supervises the operation of the two movement motors for each door: one unlocks the lock, the other produces the movement with the help of two cables connected to the guide pulley. The initialization procedure is carried out in the following cases: - battery disconnection, - removing/refitting sliding door motor. To initialize the system it is necessary to: - start with the door closed; - control an opening (electrical); - control a closing (electrical); - control another opening (electrical). The initialization is not lost from the system after the door is closed manually.

The steering wheel node control unit M093 receives the door open/closed signal from the remote control. The (door opening or closing) command is transmitted, via the CAN, from the steering wheel node control unit M093 (pins 1 and 3 connector A) to the sliding side door node M171 (pins 4 and 5 connector A) and to the Body computer node M001 (pins 5 and 3 connector G respectively); in addition, the latter (pin 11 connector B and pin 1 connector G) provide it with a power supply through two lines (pin 5 connector A and pin 4 connector D respectively) of which only the second is protected by fuse F04. The sliding side door node M171 (pins 1 and 8 connector A) receives a power supply from the maxi-fuse box B005 (connector B) via two lines protected (respectively) by fuses MF1 and MF2. The command for the electrical opening of the sliding side doors comes from the specific switches fitted in the courtesy light I133 (left side) and I134 (right side) or from the switches on the centre pillars I135 (left side) and I136 (right side). All the switches I133, I134, I135 and I136 receive a power supply at pin 4 from the Body computer node M001 (pin 3 connector F) , are earthed at pin 3 and have pin 6 connected to the sliding side door node M171 (pins 15, 10, 14, 11 connector A respectively) from which they receive the command. The control unit M171 (pins 1-2 connector B, pins 1-2 connector E) controls the electric motors for the movement of the right sliding side door N168 (pins 1 and 2) and the left sliding side door N169 (pins 1 and 2). The left sliding side door end of travel switch (131 (pins 3, 4, 1, 2, 5, 6) and the right sliding side door end of travel switch I132 (pins 3, 4, 1, 2, 5, 6) are connected to the control unit M171 (pins 3, 4, 1, 2, 5, 6 connectors C and D respectively). The switches for the left sliding side door lock I137 (pin 1) and the right one I138 (pin 1) and (pins 2 and 7 connector A) and the central locking control unit M080 (pins 9 and 16 respectively) are connected at the same control unit M171. Pins 2 for the left and right sliding side door lock motors N166 and N167 are connected at pins 8 and 1 of control unit M080 respectively. Pins 1 of motors M166 and N167 are earthed with pins 2 of switches I137 and I138. The switches in the left rear door I018 (pin 1) and the right one I019 (pin 1) are connected to the control unit M080 (pins 6 and 3 respectively) and from there to the Body computer node M001 (pins 34 and 33 connector L). The control unit M080 is connected through pins 5 and 11 to pins 11 of connector F and 32 of connector I of the Body computer node M001, whilst pins 13 and 14 are short circuited. Pin 14 is connected to pin 33 of the ESP control unit M050. See E7023 ESP Lastly, the Body computer node M001 (pins 13 and 15 connector F) is connected to the central locking system. See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING

Description The vehicle is prepared for the installation of a radio system. This preparation includes: radio supply leads; front power speakers and separate tweeters; rear power speakers and separate tweeters; cables connecting the radio with the speakers; an aerial at the back mounted on the roof and connected by means of a coaxial cable to the radio. The radio circuit is supplied both with the key in position M and it receives a direct supply from the battery (which allows tuning, safety codes, etc. to be programmed). The main radio controls are duplicated on the steering wheel allowing the driver to operate the radio without taking their hands off the steering wheel. To all intents the radio is a CAN node and is connected to the body computer, the instrument panel and the multifuction screen where information relating to the radio is displayed. A special CD cartridge allows up to 6 CDs to be loaded which are then selected through the radio controls. The CD changer is located in the dashboard console The following is also available, depending on the trim level: RADIO with CD player, described in this section; "CONNECT Nav" device (with navigator with pictograms) See E4091 CONNECT "CONNECT Nav +" device (with navigator with maps) (Wiring Diagram ) E4090 NAVIGATOR All the details of the specifications and operations of these radio systems are given in the "OWNER'S HANDBOOK".

Operational Description The body computer node M001 provides a direct supply, from pin 1 connector D, to the radio P020, pin 7 connector A, via the line protected by fuse F11 of the body computer; the ignition-controlled supply, from pin 4 connector D, to pin 6 of connector of P020 arrives via the line protected by fuse F07 of the body computer. It converses, from pins 2 and 3 of connector A, via the CAN, with the milometer and warning lights control unit node M140, at pins 6 and 3, and the instrument panel E050. A supply for the CAN is received at pin 4 connector A from the body computer node M001 from pin 3 connector D from the line protected by fuse F20 for the control unit. The radio P020 is connected (switched supply) to the aerial P025 from pin 5 connector A and to earth at pin 8. The radio P020 is connected, via connector B, to the various speakers located inside the vehicle: from pins 1, 2 it is connected to the speakers P048 (right rear tweeter) and P121 (right rear speaker); it is connected, from pins 3, 4, to the speakers P036 (speaker in right front door) and P046 (right front tweeter); it is connected, from pins 5, 6, to the speakers P035 (speaker in left front door) and P045 (left front tweeter); from pins 7, 8 it is connected to the speakers P047 (left rear tweeter) and P120 (left rear speaker); Connector C of radio P020 is connected to CD loader P075. Pins 13, 14, 17 are used to exchange data vfia the CAN. Pins 15, 16 of radio P020 supply the earth reference and direct battery supply respectively to the CD loader. Pins 19, 20 are the left and right audio inputs respectively. Pin 18 is the earth reference of the audio channel. It is possible, via the steering wheel node M093, to control several of the radio functions using the radio controls on the steering wheel; this information is sent by the steering wheel node control unit M093 to the body computer node M001, via the CAN which connects the two control units. The steering wheel node control unit M093 receives a supply (pin 5 connector A) from the line protected by fuse F11, located in the body computer node M001; it receives a supply via the CAN (pin 6 connector A) from the line protected by fuse F16 located in the body computer node M001 Information is exchanged, via the CAN, between the instrument panel node E050, the radio P020 and the multifunction screen M172.

The vehicle is wired for the installation of a radio system. This preparation includes: - radio supply leads; - front power speakers and separate tweeters; - rear power speakers and separate tweeters; - cables connecting the radio with the speakers; - an aerial at the back mounted on the roof and connected by means of a coaxial cable to the radio. The radio circuit is supplied both with the key in position M and it receives a direct supply from the battery (which allows tuning, safety codes, etc. to be programmed). The main radio controls are duplicated on the steering wheel allowing the driver to operate the radio without taking their hands off the steering wheel. To all intents the radio is a CAN node and is connected to the body computer, the instrument panel and the multifuction screen where information relating to the radio is displayed. A special CD cartridge allows up to 6 CDs to be loaded which are then selected through the radio controls. The CD changer is located in the dashboard console. The following is also available, depending on the trim level: - RADIO with CD player, described in this section; - CONNECT Nav" device (with navigator with pictograms); See E4091 CONNECT - CONNECT Nav +" device (with navigator with maps). See E4090 NAVIGATOR All the details on the specifications and the operation of the various models are contained in the "OWNER'S HANDBOOK".

Description The information for the driver is displayed by means of three elements: Instrument Panel Node in the centre of the dashboard, Milometer Warning Lights Node located above the steering column, Multifunction Screen Node fitted in front of the instrument panel on the standard version or built into it (DT colour screen) on the Connect Nav + versions. The Instrument Panel Node displays the following information: Speedometer; Rev counter; Fuel level gauge; Coolant temperature gauge; Odometer; Minimum fuel level warning light; Coolant overheating warning light; Oil level gauge. The milometer can be completely zeroed (reset) if the mileage is below 250 km (or 250 miles). This zeroing can only be done once. The Milometer Warning lights Node is connected to the CAN and managed by the body computer, The node is ruled by the instrument panel from which it receives display commands and to which it signals its status via the CAN. Milometer node warning lights: Dipped headlamps warning light Main beam headlamps warning light Direction indicator warning lights Rear fog lamps warning light Fog lights warning light ESP warning light ABS warning light EOBD warning light Cruise Control warning light Brake fluid level and parking brake - EBD warning light Minimum oil pressure warning light Battery recharging warning light Diesel heater plugs warning light Driver's seat belt warning light Passenger Air Bag disabled warning light Air Bag warning light The milometer display is capable of showing the following: on the top line, the trip mileage and the engine oil level gauge (where fitted) on the bottom line, the total mileage and service indicator; In addition, on versions equipped with automatic transmission, the gear engaged is displayed and there is a symbol warning of the presence of ice on the road. (Wiring Diagram ) E7050 AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION The Multifunction Screen Node is incorporated in the CAN and manages the display of the: Time Date Outside temperature Radio information (and CD changer) On board computer (consumption/average speed/range) Status of the doors The lighting for the three modules can be dimmed: the intensity of the lighting is altered by means of a button located in the Milometer Warning Lights Node and is managed by the latter which then controls the Instrument Panel Node and the Multifunction Screen Node. All the details on the specifications and the operation of the instruments is contained in the "OWNER'S HANDBOOK". Operational Description The management of the warning lights and the information shown by the display is entrusted to the milometer warning lights node M140, the instrument panel node E050 and the multifunction screen node M172 which receive information from the control units involved via the CAN. The three modules receive a supply via the CAN (pin 13 of E50, pin 4 of M140, pin 2 of M172) from the line protected by fuse F24 of the body computer M001. The milometer warning lights node M140 communicates, from pins 2, 5, via the CAN, with the instrument panel node E050, pins 16, 22; the instrument panel node E050 communicates, via the CAN, with the body computer node M001, at pins 10, 8 connector D. Pin 1 of M140 and pin 7 of E050 are earthed. The multifunction screen M172 receives a supply, at pin 1, from the body computer node M001 (pin 1 connector D) from the line protected by fuse F11. It communicates, from pins 4, 6, via the CAN, with the instrument panel node E050, at pins 24, 18. Pin 3 is connected to earth. The body computer node M001 communicates, from pin 4 connector F and from pins 30, 28 connector L, via the CAN, with the Air Bag control unit M060 at pins 47, 30, 33. Pin 37, connector L receives the signal coming from the driver's seat belt switch I046 whilst pin 35 of the same connector receives the signal coming from the handbrake applied switch I040. The body computer node M001 receives information, from pins 15, 16 connector M, concerning the fuel level provided by the pump N040. Pins 13, 14, 29 connector M receive information from the engine oil level and temperature sensor K032; this information passes throught the engine compartment junction unit B001, entering at pins 4, 5, 6 connector B and exiting at pins 3, 4, 10 connector E. The engine compartment junction unit B001 receives information, at pin 11 connector B, concerning the engine oil pressure, coming from sensor K030, information transmitted to the body computer node M001 via the CAN. The body computer node M001 communicates, from pins 6, 8 connector M, via the CAN, with the engine compartment junction unit B001, at pins 1 5, connector E. The body computer node M001 also provides a supply, from pin 3 connector D, to the engine compartment junction unit B001, at pin 9 connector E through the line protected by fuse F11. The engine coolant level sensor K026, supplied by the engine compartment junction unit B001, through the line protected by fuse F01, provides a signal to the body computer node M001, pin 1 of connector M. The body computer node M001, communicates, from pins 2, 4 connector M, via the CAN, with the ABS control unit M050, at pins 24, 40 and with the engine management control unit M010, pins A4, A3 connector A. Engine management control unit M010 communicates information on coolant temperature supplied by sensor K036. ABS control unit M050 sends information on brake pad wear supplied by sensors K020 and K021 to pin 32, and brake fluid level, supplied by sensor K025 to pin 22.

Description The vehicle is prepared for the installation of a "CONNECT NAV +" system: it involves a radio built into the CONNECT device and a navigator with maps The telephone system includes: GSM module and SIM CARD reader built into the radio; navigator module with maps incorporated in the radio; hands-free function via the radio speakers; microphone located in the front courtesy light; GSM/GPS exterior aerial. The navigation system makes it possible to know the position of the vehicle at any time. In this way the driver can be guided to their desired destination, step by step, through voice messages and visual information. The system also provides additional information for reaching general services, namely: hotels, carparks, restaurants, chemists, service stations, hospitals, authorized workshops, railway stations, airports, etc. The navigation system uses GPS (Global Positioning System) satellite technology consisting of an aerial that allows the GPS satellite location of the vehicle: the aerial is connected to a receiver located in the integrated unit by means of a special shielded cable. The aerial is fitted at the rear of the roof: it has two functions (GSM/GPS) because it also incorporates the GSM aerial for the CONNECT system Vehicle position is identified by analysing GPS data together with speedometer and reverse gear signals received from the vehicle. The navigation CD-ROM drive is located in the radio assembly. the navigation system only works with the CD-ROM inserted in the special drive; it is therefore possible to listen to a music CD during navigation. In this case, the navigation function requires the map CD to be inserted whilst carrying out the route calculation procedures. The main radio controls are duplicated on the steering wheel allowing the driver to operate the radio without taking their hands off the steering wheel. The special controls for the Connect function are on a special control knob located in the centre of the dashboard next to the climate control system controls. A cooling fan ensures the necessary exchange of air in the area of the radio, preventing it from overheating. On this versions the multifunction screen has a 7" 16/9 DT colour monitor. The Connect radio system is, to all intents and purposes, a CAN node and is connected to the body computer, the instrument panel and the multifunction screen where information relating to the radio is displayed. A special CD cartridge allows up to 6 CDs to be loaded which are then selected through the radio controls. The CD changer is located in the dashboard console On this version there is also an audio-video socket, located inside the glove compartment, which can be used for connecting an outside television camera to the Connect system in order to be able to show immages on the actual system monitor. The following is also available, depending on the trim level: RADIO with CD player, See E3510 RADIO "CONNECT Nav" device (with navigator with pictograms) See E4091 CONNECT "CONNECT Nav +" device (with navigator with maps) described in this section All the details of the specifications and operations of these radio systems are given in the "OWNER'S HANDBOOK".

Operational Description The body computer node M001 provides a direct supply, from pin 1 connector D, to the radio Connect P020, pin 4 connector D, via the line protected by fuse F11 of the body computer. It converses, from pins 5 and 2 of connector D, via the CAN, with the milometer and warning lights control unit node M140, at pins 6 and 3 and with the instrument panel E050. A power supply for the CAN is received at pin 6 connector D from the body computer node M001 from pin 3 connector D from the line protected by fuse F20 of the control unit. The radio P020 is connected (switched power supply) to the aerial P025 from pin 3 connector D and to earth at pin 8. The Connect radio P020 is connected, via connector C, to the various speakers located inside the vehicle: from pins 1, 5 it is connected to the speakers P048 (right rear tweeter) and P121 (right rear speaker); it is connected, from pins 2, 6, to the speakers P036 (speaker in right front door) and P046 (right front tweeter); it is connected, from pins 3, 7, to the speakers P035 (speaker in left front door) and P045 (left front tweeter); from pins 4, 8 it is connected to the speakers P047 (left rear tweeter) and P120 (left rear speaker); Pins 2 and 8 of connector A are connected to speaker P035 also used for the hands-free function in the telephone mode. The Connect P020 is connected, from pins 3, 9 connector A, to the microphone P027; pin 3 is the reference earth, whilst pin 9 is the audio signal input. Pins 1, 7 supply the outside fan N160. The multifunction colour screen M172 displays the information supplied by the Connect in a graphic format. Pin 2 of the screen is connected to pin 6 connector A of the Connect P020 (stand-by signal); pins 1,7, on the other hand, are connected to pins 7, 1 connector D of the Connect P020 and receive the power supply and reference earth, respectively. The audio-video socket coupling D055 is connected to pins 4, 10 and 11 of connector A of P020 (right, left audio signals and earth) and to pins 5 and 11 of the screen M172 (video signals). The radio P020 is connected, via connector B, to the CD changer P075. Pins 7, 2 and 9 are used for the exchange of data via the CAN. From pins 1, 3 the radio P020 provides the CD changer with a reference earth and direct battery supply, respectively. Pins 4 and 10 are the left and right audio inputs, respectively. Pin 8 is the reference earth for the audio channel. The control panel M160 is connected to the Connect P020 at pins 12, 11, 6 of connector B via the CAN. The radio/GSM aerial P111 is connected to connector E of P020. It is possible, via the steering wheel node M093, to control several of the radio functions using the radio controls on the steering wheel; this information is sent by the steering wheel node control unit M093 to the body computer node M001, via the CAN which connects the two control units. The vehicle is prepared for the installation of a "CONNECT NAV" system: it involves a radio built into the CONNECT device and a navigator with maps. The telephone system includes: - GSM module and SIM CARD reader built into the radio; - navigator module with maps incorporated in the radio; - hands free function via the radio speakers; - microphone located in the front courtesy light; - GSM/GPS exterior aerial. The navigation system makes it possible to know the position of the vehicle in the road network, at any time. In this way the driver is guided to the required destination step by step by means of voice messages and visual information. The system also provides additional information for reaching general services, namely: hotels, carparks, restaurants, chemists, service stations, hospitals, authorized workshops, railway stations, airports, etc. The navigation system uses GPS (Global Positioning System) satellite technology consisting of an aerial that allows the GPS satellite location of the vehicle: The aerial is connected to a receiver located in the integrated unit by means of a special shielded cable. The aerial is fitted at the rear of the roof and has two functions (GSM/GPS): it incorporates a GSM aerial when the CONNECT system is also required. Vehicle position is identified by analysing GPS data together with speedometer and reverse gear signals received from the vehicle. The navigation CD-ROM drive is located in the radio assembly. the navigation system only works with the CD-ROM inserted in the special drive; it is therefore possible to listen to a music CD during navigation. In this case, the navigation function requires the map CD to be inserted whilst carrying out the route calculation procedures. The main radio controls are duplicated on the steering wheel allowing the driver to operate the radio without taking their hands off the steering wheel. The special controls for the Connect function are on a special control knob located in the centre of the dashboard next to the climate control system controls. A cooling fan ensures the necessary exchange of air in the area of the radio, preventing it from overheating. On this versions the multifunction screen has a 7" 16/9 DT colour monitor. The Connect radio system is, to all intents and purposes, a CAN node and is connected to the body computer, the instrument panel and the multifunction screen where information relating to the radio is displayed. A special CD cartridge allows up to 6 CDs to be loaded which are then selected through the radio controls. The CD changer is located in the dashboard console. On this version there is also an audio-video socket, located inside the glove compartment, which can be used for connecting an outside television camera to the Connect system in order to be able to show images on the actual system monitor. The following is also available, depending on the trim level: - radio with CD player; See E3510 RADIO - "CONNECT Nav" device (with navigator with pictograms); See E4091 CONNECT - "CONNECT Nav +" device (with navigator with maps) described in this section. All the details of the specifications and operations of these radio systems are given in the "OWNER'S HANDBOOK".

Operational Description The body computer node M001 provides a direct supply, from pin 1 connector D, to the radio Connect P020, pin 4 connector D, via the line protected by fuse F11 of the body computer. It converses, from pins 5 and 2 of connector D, via the CAN, with the milometer and warning lights control unit node M140, at pins 6 and 3 and with the instrument panel E050. A power supply for the CAN is received at pin 6 connector D from the body computer node M001 from pin 3 connector D from the line protected by fuse F20 of the control unit. The radio P020 is connected (switched power supply) to the aerial P025 from pin 3 connector D and to earth at pin 8. The Connect radio P020 is connected, via connector C, to the various speakers located inside the vehicle: from pins 1, 5 it is connected to the speakers P048 (right rear tweeter) and P121 (right rear speaker); it is connected, from pins 2, 6, to the speakers P036 (speaker in right front door) and P046 (right front tweeter); it is connected, from pins 3, 7, to the speakers P035 (speaker in left front door) and P045 (left front tweeter); from pins 4, 8 it is connected to the speakers P047 (left rear tweeter) and P120 (left rear speaker); Pins 2 and 8 of connector A are connected to speaker P035 also used for the hands-free function in the telephone mode. The Connect P020 is connected, from pins 3, 9 connector A, to the microphone P027; pin 3 is the reference earth, whilst pin 9 is the audio signal input. Pins 1, 7 supply the outside fan N160. The multifunction screen M172 displays the information supplied by the Connect in a graphic format. Pins 6 and 4 of the screen are connected at pins 5 and 12 connector A of the Connect P025 and form a CAN connection; pin 3 of M172 is connected to pin 6 connector A of the Connect P020 (stand-by signal). Pins 1, 2 are connected to pins 1, 7 connector D of the Connect P020 and receive the power supply and the reference earth, respectively. The radio P020 is connected, via connector B, to the CD changer P075. Pins 7, 2 and 9 are used for the exchange of data via the CAN. From pins 1, 3 the radio P020 provides the CD changer with a reference earth and direct battery supply, respectively. Pins 4 and 10 are the left and right audio inputs, respectively. Pin 8 is the earth reference of the audio channel. The control panel M160 is connected to the Connect P020 at pins 12, 11, 6 of connector B via the CAN. The radio/GSM aerial P111 is connected to connector E of P020. It is possible, via the steering wheel node M093, to control several of the radio functions using the radio controls on the steering wheel; this information is sent by the steering wheel node control unit M093 to the body computer node M001, via the CAN which connects the two control units. Description The ignition and recharging circuit comprises the battery, starter motor and alternator. The battery (12V) is the lead, low maintenance type. The starter motor consists of a d.c. motor supplied by the battery and an excitation electromagnet. When the ignition key is turned as far as it will go (D), the motor windings are supplied to generate the electromagnetic forces that are used to turn the starter motor pinion. This simultaneously activates the electromagnet that operates the mechanism that causes the pinion to mesh with the flywheel ring gear and thus turn the crankshaft. The alternator recharges the battery during normal engine rotation. The alternator shaft (rotor) is turned by the crankshaft via a belt. When supplied by an excitation current, the rotor generates a magnetic field that sets up an alternating current in the fixed winding (stator). A rectifying diode bridge on the back of the alternator allows the alternating current to be rectified to a direct current that is sent to recharge the battery. A voltage governor, also built into the alternator, maintains the power supply at a constant voltage (14 V) throughout the load variation and engine speed ranges.

Operational Description The battery A001, supplies the ignition switch H001, through the line protected by fuse MF7 of the engine compartment junction unit B001, at pin 1 connector A. When the ignition is turned to position M, the alternator A010 informs the body computer node M001, from pin D+, at pin 11 connector M of the battery charge state. The "battery recharging" warning light is switched on by the milometer warning lights node M140 which communicates with the instrument panel E050 and the body computer node M001 via the CAN. The ignition switch also provides the junction unit B001 with an igition-controlled supply (from pin 2 connector A at pin 9 connector C) and the body computer node M001 (from pin 1 connector B at pin 1 connector C). When the ignition key is turned to position D, the supply, from pin 3 connector A of H001, reaches the starter motor A020 at pin 50. The internal contact is closed, providing the internal motor with a direct battery supply at pin 30 of the starter motor. When the ignition key is turned back to position M, the starter motor A020 internal contact opens, interrupting the direct battery supply. The alternator A010 recharges the battery A001 from pin B+. < B > 2.0 16V < /B > When the ignition key is turned back to position M, the starter motor A020 internal contact opens, interrupting the direct battery supply. The alternator A010 recharges the battery A001 from pin B+. < B > 2.0 16V 2.2 16V < /B > The alternator communicates the battery charge from pin D+ to the heater plugs control unit M015.

The internal contact is closed, providing the direct supply from the battery for the starter motor entering at pin 30. The ignition and recharging circuit comprises the battery, starter motor and alternator. A low-maintenance lead battery (12V) is required. When the ignition key is turned as far as it will go (D), the motor windings are supplied to generate the electromagnetic forces that are used to turn the starter motor pinion. This simultaneously activates the electromagnet that operates the mechanism that causes the pinion to mesh with the flywheel ring gear and thus turn the crankshaft. The alternator recharges the battery during normal engine rotation. The alternator shaft (rotor) is turned by the crankshaft via a belt: an induced magnetic field is generated in the fixed winding (stator) that gives rise to an alternating current. A diode rectifier bridge on the back of the alternator allows the alternating current to be converted to a direct current that is sent to recharge the battery. A voltage governor, also built into the alternator, maintains the power supply at a constant voltage (14 V) throughout the load variation and engine speed ranges.

Ignition switch H001 (pins 1, 2 and 3) is connected to body computer node M001 (pin 4 connector G, pin 5 connector D and pin 6 connector G respectively). Description The engine radiator and air conditioner condenser cooling system consists of two fans operated at three different speeds achieved by means of an additional resistance: the first speed is activated at an initial engine coolant temperature level or a certain air conditioning refrigerant fluid pressure; the second speed is engaged at a higher temperature or pressure; the third speed is engaged at even greater temperature or pressure values. The fans are operated by means of three specific relays located near the radiator.

Operational Description Engine control unit M010 controls the operation of the engine cooling fan according to data supplied by linear sensor K120 and engine coolant sensor K036. Both sensors are connected directly to the engine control unit; K036 to pins E4, D4 (or D2, D3), while K120 is connected to pins H4, H2 and F2 of connector A. Depending on the data supplied by the two sensors, the control unit M010 and the body computer node M001, either activate the fan N011 at three different speeds or do not. Operation at first speed: The engine management control unit energizes relay J030, pin 2 from pin D4 connector A; the relay coil is supplied by the engine compartment junction unit B001, from pin 14 connector C, by the line protected by fuse F08 and operated by a specific relay. When the relay is energized, it supplies the fan N011, by means of the two resistances O010 and O012 through the line coming from the junction unit B001, pin 6 connector G protected by fuse FM6: it therefore turns at the first speed. Operation at second speed: The body computer node M001 energizes relay J031, pin 2 from pin 30 connector M; the relay coil is supplied by the engine compartment junction unit B001, from pin 10 connector C, by the line protected by fuse F01. When the relay J031 is energized, it supplies the fan N011, by means of the single resistance O012 through the line coming from the junction unit B001, pin 6 connector G protected by fuse MF6: it therefore turns at the second speed. Operation at third speed: The engine management control unit energizes relay J032, pin 2 from pin B2 connector A; the relay coil is supplied by the engine compartment junction unit B001, from pin 14 connector C, by the line protected by fuse F08 and operated by a specific relay. When the relay J032 is energized, it supplies the fan N011 directly without passing through the resistances, through the line coming from the junction unit B001, pin 1 connector G protected by fuse MF1: it therefore turns at the third speed.

Description The cooling system for the engine radiator and air conditioning condenser consists of two fans operated at different speeds by means of a connection between them either in series or parallel. the first speed is activated at an initial engine coolant temperature level or a certain air conditioning refrigerant fluid pressure; the second speed is engaged at a higher temperature or pressure. The fans are operated by means of three specific relays located near the radiator.

Operational Description Engine control unit M010 controls the operation of the engine cooling fan according to data supplied by linear sensor K120 and engine coolant sensor K036. Both sensors are connected directly to the engine control unit; K036 to pins E1, D1 connector B, while K120 is connected to pins H4, H2 and F2 of connector A. Control unit M010 operates fans N011 and N012 on the basis of data supplied by both sensors. Operation at first speed: fans in series: The engine management control unit energizes relay J030, pin 2 from pin D4 connector A; the relay coil is supplied by the engine compartment junction unit B001, from pin 14 connector C, by the line protected by fuse F08 and operated by a specific relay. When the relay is energized, it supplies the fans N012 and N011, connected in series, through the line coming from junction unit B001, pin 6 connector G protected by fuse MF6 (relay J031 is not energized and connects the two fans in this way). Operation at second speed: fans in parallel: The engine management control unit energizes relays J030 and J032, pin 2 from pin B2 connector A; the relay coil is supplied by the engine compartment junction unit B001, from pin 10 connector C, by the line protected by fuse F01. When the relay J032 is energized, it supplies the fans N012 and N011, connected in parallel, through the line coming from junction unit B001, pin 1 connector G protected by fuse MF1 (relay J031 is energized and connects the two fans in this way).

The radiator and air conditioner condenser cooling system consists of two electric fans: there are two different speeds depending on the temperature of the engine coolant or the pressure of the air conditioning refrigerant. The fans are activated by three relays connected to one another: depending on the temperature and pressure sensor signals, the connections are series or parallel and produce the speed levels mentioned above

Engine control unit M010 controls the operation of the engine cooling fans according to data supplied by linear sensor K120 and engine coolant sensor K036. The two sensors are connected directly to the engine management control unit M010: - pins 1, 2, 3 of K120 at pins F2, H2, F4 connector A; - pins 1, 2 of K036 at pin E1 and D1 connector B. Control unit M010 operates fans N011 and N012 on the basis of the signals supplied by both sensors. First speed operation (fans in series): The engine management control unit M010 energizes relay J030 (pin 2) from pin D4 of connector A. The relay coil is supplied (pin 1) by the engine compartment junction unit B001 (pin 2 connector F) through a line protected by fuse F01 and operated by a specific relay. When the relay J030 is energized, pin 3 (connected to pin 2 connector C of the MAXI FUSE box 2 B006) is short circuited at pin 5. This pin is connected to pin 1 of fan N012 which, in turn, has pin 2 connected with pin 3 of relay J031. This relay is not energized in this operating condition, therefore pin 3 is short circuited with pin 4. The latter is connected with pin 1 of fan N011 which, in turn, has pin 2 connected with earth C011. The fans are thereby connected in series. Second speed operation (fans in parallel): The engine management control unit M010 energizes relays J031 and J032 (pin 2) from pin B2 of connector A. The relay coils are supplied (pin 1) by the engine compartment junction unit B001 (pin 4 connector F) through a line protected by fuse F06 and operated by a specific relay. The engine management control unit M010 energizes relay J030 (pin 2) from pin D4 of connector A. The relay coil is supplied (pin 1) by the engine compartment junction unit B001 (pin 2 connector F) through a line protected by fuse F01 and operated by a specific relay. When the relay J032 is energized, pin 5 (connected to pin 1 connector B of the MAXI FUSE box 2 B006) is short circuited at pin 3. This pin is connected to pin 1 of fan N011 which, in turn, has pin 2 connected with earth C011. Relay J031 is also energized: pin 5 (connected with earth C011) is short circuited at pin 3 which, in turn, is connected with pin 2 of fan N012. As relay J030 is also energized (pins 3 and 5 short circuited), pin 1 of N012 is connected with pin 2 of connector C of B006. The fans are thereby connected in parallel.

An electronic control system supervises and governs all engine parameters to optimise performance and fuel consumption by means of a real-time response to different service conditions. Diesel engines are equipped with a COMMON RAIL type injection system. This features the use of an electronically controlled high injection pressure. The supply of fuel, known as the pilot injection, is optimized by the electronic control unit by means of the injector rather than managed by the pump. Depending on the signals received from numerous sensors, the control unit controls the injectors connected to it managing the following systems: fuel supply; air supply; heater plugs; accelerator pedal; engine cooling; fuel pre-heating; operation of the particle filter (FAP). See E5070 FAP PARTICLE FILTER SYSTEM The rail is connected to the various injectors by means of pipes. The injector opening is implemented by a solenoid valve controlled by the engine management node. Depending on the engine operating conditions, the NCM manages: the pressure in the rail, the high pressure pump flow rate, the moment and opening time for each injector. The common rail system manages different fuel injectors for each injector cycle for each engine cycle: the moment and opening time for each injector. pilot injection, main injection, post-injection (when needed).

Engine management control unit M010 controls and governs the entire electronic ignition and injection system. Control unit M010 is supplied directly by the battery (pins L2 and M1 of connector B) via a line protected by fuse F01 located inside engine compartment junction unit B001 (pin 5 connector B) and is controlled by a relay, excited (pin 9 connector B of B001) by a control signal from M010 (pin A2 connector B). The same supply also reaches the fuel pressure regulator N077 (pin 2) and the throttle adjustment solenoid valve L036 (pin 1). The ignition-operated supply reaches pin C3 of connector A of M010 through the line protected by fuse F09 located inside B001 (pin 19 connector G). The main injection relay for the engine compartment junction unit B001 controls the entire system: it is excited (pin 8 connector B) by a control signal (earth) from control unit M010 (pin C3 connector B) that in turn supplies: - fuel pump N040 (pin 3) from pin 5 of connector F via a line protectged by fuse F05; - EGR solenoid L030 (pin 1) and wastegate solenoid L037 (pin 1) from pin 22 of connector F, via the same line; - intake variable geometry control solenoid (pin 1) and part of the FAP system from pin24 of connector B via a line protected by fuse F10; See E5070 FAP PARTICLE FILTER SYSTEM - diesel preheating coil O020 (pin 1) from pin 2 of connector B, again via the same line; Fuel pump N040 (pins 5 and 6) is connected to the on-board instruments. See E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL The ignition-operated power suppoly is sent to air flow meter K041 (pin 2), glow plug preheating control unit M015 (pin 3 connector B) and safety switch on the brake pedal for cruise control I035 (pin 1) of control unit B001 (pin 20 connector F) with a line protected by fuse F06. Glow plug preheating control unit M015 (pins 4 and 5 connector B) are connected to pins B1 and F1 of connector C of M010. Control unit M010 receives signals from the various sensors in order to monitor all engine service parameters. RPM sensor K046 (pins 1 and 2) provides information on engine rpm (pins J1 and K1 connector B of M010 respectively). Engine temperature sensor K036 (pins 1and 2) receives a reference earth and supplies a signal proportional to the engine coolant temperature (pins E1 and D1 connector B of M010 respectively). Supply air pressure sensor K082 (pins 1, 2, 3) is connected to pins B2, C4, D4 of connector B of M010. Fuel pressure sensor K083 (pins 1, 2, 3) is connected to pins F1, G1, H1 of connector B of M010. Fuel temperature sensor K081 (pins 1, 2) supplies a signal proportional to temperature (pins D2 and E2 connector B of M010). Throttle adjustment solenoid L036 (pin 2) is connected to pin A4 of connector C of M010. Cylinder reference sensor K170 (pins 1, 2, 3) is connected to pins H2 G2, F2, of connector B of M010. Air flow meter K041 (pins 1, 6, 5) is connected to pins J3, G3, H3 of connector B of M010. The accelerator pedal K055 (pins 1, 2, 3, 4) has two built-in potentiometers (one main one and one safety one) and is connected to pins G3, H3, C2, G2 of connector A of M010. Clutch pedal switch I031 (pin 2) and the safety switch on the brake pedal I035 (pin 2) are connected to pins E3 and E4 (respectively) of connector A of M010. Switch I031 (pin 1) is supplied by body computer node M001 (pin 9 connector B). The "redundant" switch I035 is the "normally closed" type (when the pedal is pressed, the switch contact opens): the system checks the consistency of the "pedal pressed" information in this way. Control unit M010 (pins G1-H2, H4-H3, G4-G3, H1-G2 connector C) controls the opening of injectors N070 (pins 1 and 2). Fuel pressure regulator N077 (pin 1) keeps the fuel pressure in the rail constant and is connected to pin L2 and connector B of M010. EGR solenoid L030 (pin 2) controls exhaust gas recirculation and is connected to pin A3 of connector B di M010. Turbo pressure valve L037 (pin 2) controls the outlet pressure from the turbocharger and is connected to pin B4 of connector C of M010. Intake variable geometry control solenoid L015 (pin 2) regulates the engine air intake ports and is connected to pin B4 of connector B of M010. Control unit M010 is connected (pins A3 and A4 connector A) via the CAN line to body computer node M001 (pins 8 and 10 connector D) to instrument panel E050 (pins 6 and 12) and to warning light and odometer control unit M140 (pins 2 and 5) and engine compartment junction unit B001 (pins 11 and 12 connector F). See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES The autodiagnostic data for the control unit M010 (pin B4 connector A) is read by connecting to connector R010 (pin 7). Control unit M010 (pins F2, H2, F4 connector A) is connected to the air conditioning system: in this way, compressor activation or deactivation is adjustd on the basis of engine speed. See E6021 COMPRESSOR ENGAGEMENT - to pins B2, C4, D4 of connector A, the engine cooling system; See E5020 ENGINE COOLING - to pins H2, E3, D3, F3, M3, B3, A4, C2 of connector B, the FAP system; See E5070 FAP PARTICLE FILTER SYSTEM - to pins K3, F4, E4, H4 of connector B, the cruise control system; See E5060 CRUISE CONTROL

Description An electronic control system supervises and governs all engine parameters to optimise performance and fuel consumption by means of a real-time response to different service conditions. Diesel engines are equipped with a COMMON RAIL type injection system. This features the use of an electronically controlled high injection pressure. The supply of fuel, known as the pilot injection, is optimized by the electronic control unit by means of the injector rather than managed by the pump. Depending on the signals received from numerous sensors, the control unit controls the injectors connected to it managing the following systems: fuel supply; air supply; heater plugs; accelerator pedal; engine cooling; fuel pre-heating; operation of the particle filter (FAP). (Wiring Diagram ) E5070 FAP PARTICLE FILTER SYSTEM The rail is connected to the various injectors by means of pipes. The injector opening is implemented by a solenoid valve controlled by the engine management node. Depending on the engine operating conditions, the NCM manages: the pressure in the rail, the high pressure pump flow rate, the moment and opening time for each injector. The common rail system manages different fuel injectors for each injector cycle for each engine cycle: the moment and opening time for each injector. pilot injection, main injection, post-injection (when needed).

Operational Description Engine management control unit M010 controls and governs the entire electronic ignition and injection system. The control unit M010 receives a direct battery supply at pin L1 and M1 of connector B, via the line protected by fuse F08 and operated by a relay in the engine compartment control unit B001, energized by a control (earth) signal coming from pin A2 of connector B of the control unit M010. The same supply also reaches the fuel pressure regulator N077 and the throttle adjustment solenoid valve L036. The ignition-controlled supply arrives via the line protected by fuse F04 of B001 which protects the supply line for pin C3 of connector A of M010. The main injection relay for the engine compartment junction unit B001 controls the entire system: t is energized by an earth signal from pin A4 of connector B of control unit M010 and then forwards a power supply to: the fuel pump N040 from pin 11 of connector C and the EGR solenoid valves L030 and supercharging pressure solenoid valves L037 from pin 12 of connector C, via the line protected by fuse F02; the swirl solenoid valve L015 from pin 1 connector B and the diesel preheating resistance O020 from pin 16 of connector B, all via the line protected by fuse F15 of B001. The ignition-controlled supply is also sent to the air flow meter K041 and to the heater plugs control unit M015 from pin 2 connector B via the line protected by fuse F01 of B001. Control unit M010 is earthed from pin H1 and G1 of connector A, M4 and L4 of connector B. Control unit M010 receives signals from the various sensors in order to control all engine service parameters. The rpm sensor K046 provides engine rpm information via a frequency signal sent to pins D1 E1 of connector B of control unit M010: The engine temperature sensor K036 receives a reference earth and provides a signal proportional to the temperature of the engine coolant to pins J1 and K1 of connector B of control unit M010. The air pressure sensor K082 receives a supply from the control unit at pin B2 of connector B of control unit M010; it receives a reference earth from pin C4 of connector B and sends a signal to pin D42 of connector B of the control unit. The fuel pressure sensor K083 receives a supply from the control unit at pin H1 of connector B of control unit M010; it receives a reference earth from pin F1 of connector B and sends a signal to pin G1 of connector B of the control unit. The fuel temperature sensor K082 receives a reference earth and provides a signal proportional to the temperature for pins D2 and E2 of connector B of control unit M010. The cylinder reference sensor K070 receives a supply from the control unit at pin H2 of connector B of control unit M010; it receives a reference earth from pin F2 of connector B and sends a signal to pin G2 of connector B of the control unit. The air flow meter K041, supplied by the main relay, pin 2, is earthed at pin 3 and is connected to the control unit M010 from pins 5, 6 and 1 to pins H3, G3 and J3 of M010. The accelerator pedal K055 has two built-in potentiometers (one main one and one safety one) and is connected to pins G3, C2, G2 and H3 of connector A of M010. Clutch pedal switch I031 and the safety switch on the brake pedal for cruise control I035 supply a signal to indicate engagement has taken place to pins E3 and E4 of connector B of M010. The two switches receive a supply from the ignition-controlled line protected by fuse F18 of the body computer M001. The "redundant" switch I035 is the "normally closed" type (when the pedal is pressed, the switch contact opens): the system checks the consistency of the "pedal pressed" information in this way. The control unit M010 controls the opening of the injectors N070 by means of special signals sent from pins H2-G1, H3-H4, G4-G3 and G2-H1 of connector C of M010. The fuel pressure regulator N077 has the task of keeping the fuel pressure value in the RAIL constant; supplied by the main relay, it receives a control signal from pin L2 of connector B of M010. The EGR solenoid valve L30 controls the recirculation of the exhaust gases; it is supplied by the main relay and controlled by a signal for pin A3 of connector B of M010. The supercharging pressure solenoid valve L037 controls the turbocharger output pressure; it is supplied by the main relay and controlled by a signal for pin B4 of connector C of M010. The swirl solenoid valve (movement of air in the combustion chamber) L015 regulates the engine air intake ducts; it is supplied by the main relay and controlled by a signal for pin C3 of connector B of M010. The control unit M010 is then connected via the CAN, pins A3 and A4, to the Body Computer M001 and to the other network nodes. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES The autodiagnostic data for the control unit M010 is read by connecting to connector R010 - pin 7: it receives signals from pin B4 connector A of M010 via the special diagnostic line. The control unit M010 is connected to the air conditioning system through pins F2, H2 and F4 of connector A. This allows the engine idle speed to be adjusted as the load conditions increase each time the compressor is switched on or to switch it off in the case of high engine speed or load conditions. See E6021 COMPRESSOR ENGAGEMENT It is also connected to the additional heating device, pin C1 of connector A of M010. See E6015 ADDITIONAL HEATER The control unit also controls the engine cooling system: pins B2, D4 and C4 of connector A control the engagement of the fan. See E5020 ENGINE COOLING Control signals for the operation of the particle filter (FAP) leave from pins D3, F3, M3, C3 and B3 of connector A of M010. See E5070 FAP PARTICLE FILTER SYSTEM

Engine management control unit M010 controls and governs the entire electronic ignition and injection system. Control unit M010 is supplied directly by the battery (pins L2 and M1 of connector B) via a line protected by fuse F01 located inside engine compartment junction unit B001 (pin 5 connector B) and is controlled by a relay, excited (pin 9 connector B of B001) by a control signal from M010 (pin A2 connector B). The same supply also reaches the fuel pressure regulator N077 (pin 2) and the throttle adjustment solenoid valve L036 (pin 1). The ignition-operated supply reaches pin C3 of connector A of M010 through the line protected by fuse F09 located inside B001 (pin 19 connector G). The main injection relay for the engine compartment junction unit B001 controls the entire system: it is excited (pin 8 connector B) by a control signal (earth) from control unit M010 (pin C3 connector B) that in turn supplies: - fuel pump N040 (pin 3) from pin 5 of connector F via a line protectged by fuse F05; - EGR solenoid L030 (pin 1) and wastegate solenoid L037 (pin 1) from pin 22 of connector F, via the same line; - intake variable geometry control solenoid (pin 1) and part of the FAP system from pin24 of connector B via a line protected by fuse F10; See E5070 FAP PARTICLE FILTER SYSTEM - diesel preheating coil O020 (pin 1) from pin 2 of connector B, again via the same line; Fuel pump N040 (pins 5 and 6) is connected to the on-board instruments. See E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL The ignition-operated power suppoly is sent to air flow meter K041 (pin 2), glow plug preheating control unit M015 (pin 3 connector B) and safety switch on the brake pedal for cruise control I035 (pin 1) of control unit B001 (pin 20 connector F) with a line protected by fuse F06. Glow plug preheating control unit M015 (pins 4 and 5 connector B) are connected to pins B1 and F1 of connector C of M010. Control unit M010 receives signals from the various sensors in order to monitor all engine service parameters. RPM sensor K046 (pins 1 and 2) provides information on engine rpm (pins J1 and K1 connector B of M010 respectively). Engine temperature sensor K036 (pins 1and 2) receives a reference earth and supplies a signal proportional to the engine coolant temperature (pins E1 and D1 connector B of M010 respectively). Supply air pressure sensor K082 (pins 1, 2, 3) is connected to pins B2, C4, D4 of connector B of M010. Fuel pressure sensor K083 (pins 1, 2, 3) is connected to pins F1, G1, H1 of connector B of M010. Fuel temperature sensor K081 (pins 1, 2) supplies a signal proportional to temperature (pins D2 and E2 connector B of M010). Throttle adjustment solenoid L036 (pin 2) is connected to pin A4 of connector C of M010. Cylinder reference sensor K170 (pins 1, 2, 3) is connected to pins H2 G2, F2, of connector B of M010. Air flow meter K041 (pins 1, 6, 5) is connected to pins J3, G3, H3 of connector B of M010. The accelerator pedal K055 (pins 1, 2, 3, 4) has two built-in potentiometers (one main one and one safety one) and is connected to pins G3, H3, C2, G2 of connector A of M010. Clutch pedal switch I031 (pin 2) and the safety switch on the brake pedal I035 (pin 2) are connected to pins E3 and E4 (respectively) of connector A of M010. Switch I031 (pin 1) is supplied by body computer node M001 (pin 9 connector B). The "redundant" switch I035 is the "normally closed" type (when the pedal is pressed, the switch contact opens): the system checks the consistency of the "pedal pressed" information in this way. Control unit M010 (pins G1-H2, H4-H3, G4-G3, H1-G2 connector C) controls the opening of injectors N070 (pins 1 and 2). Fuel pressure regulator N077 (pin 1) keeps the fuel pressure in the rail constant and is connected to pin L2 and connector B of M010. EGR solenoid L030 (pin 2) controls exhaust gas recirculation and is connected to pin A3 of connector B di M010. Turbo pressure valve L037 (pin 2) controls the outlet pressure from the turbocharger and is connected to pin B4 of connector C of M010. Intake variable geometry control solenoid L015 (pin 2) regulates the engine air intake ports and is connected to pin B4 of connector B of M010. Control unit M010 is connected (pins A3 and A4 connector A) via the CAN line to body computer node M001 (pins 8 and 10 connector D) to instrument panel E050 (pins 6 and 12) and to warning light and odometer control unit M140 (pins 2 and 5) and engine compartment junction unit B001 (pins 11 and 12 connector F). See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES The autodiagnostic data for the control unit M010 (pin B4 connector A) is read by connecting to connector R010 (pin 7). Control unit M010 (pins F2, H2, F4 connector A) is connected to the air conditioning system: in this way, compressor activation or deactivation is adjustd on the basis of engine speed. An electronic control system supervises and governs all engine parameters to optimise performance and fuel consumption by means of a real-time response to different service conditions. Diesel engines are equipped with a COMMON RAIL type injection system. This features the use of an electronically controlled high injection pressure. The supply of fuel, known as the pilot injection, is optimized by the electronic control unit by means of the injector rather than managed by the pump. Depending on the signals received from numerous sensors, the control unit controls the injectors connected to it managing the following systems: fuel supply; air supply; heater plugs; accelerator pedal; engine cooling; fuel pre-heating; The rail is connected to the various injectors by means of pipes. The injector opening is implemented by a solenoid valve controlled by the engine management node. Depending on the engine operating conditions, the NCM manages: the pressure in the rail, the high pressure pump flow rate, the moment and opening time for each injector. The common rail system manages different fuel injectors for each injector cycle for each engine cycle: the moment and opening time for each injector. pilot injection, main injection, post-injection (when needed).

Engine management control unit M010 controls and governs the entire electronic ignition and injection system. Control unit M010 is supplied directly by the battery (pins L2 and M1 of connector B) via a line protected by fuse F01 located inside engine compartment junction unit B001 (pin 5 connector B) and is controlled by a relay, excited (pin 9 connector B of B001) by a control signal from M010 (pin A2 connector B). The same supply also reaches the fuel pressure regulator N077 (pin 2) and the throttle adjustment solenoid valve L036 (pin 1). The ignition-operated supply reaches pin C3 of connector A of M010 through the line protected by fuse F09 located inside B001 (pin 19 connector G). The main injection relay for the engine compartment junction unit B001 controls the entire system: it is excited (pin 8 connector B) by a control signal (earth) from control unit M010 (pin C3 connector B) that in turn supplies: - fuel pump N040 (pin 3) from pin 5 of connector F via a line protectged by fuse F05; - EGR solenoid L030 (pin 1) and wastegate solenoid L037 (pin 1) from pin 22 of connector F, via the same line; - intake variable geometry control solenoid L015 (pin 1) and injection pump piston third deactivation solenoid L005 (pin 2) from pin24 of connector B via a line protected by fuse F10; - diesel preheating coil O020 (pin 1) from pin 2 of connector B, again via the same line; Fuel pump N040 (pins 5 and 6) is connected to the on-board instruments. See E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL The ignition-operated power suppoly is sent to air flow meter K041 (pin 2), glow plug preheating control unit M015 (pin 3 connector B) and safety switch on the brake pedal for cruise control I035 (pin 1) of control unit B001 (pin 20 connector F) with a line protected by fuse F06. Glow plug preheating control unit M015 (pins 4 and 5 connector B) are connected to pins B1 and F1 of connector C of M010. Control unit M010 receives signals from the various sensors in order to monitor all engine service parameters. RPM sensor K046 (pins 1 and 2) provides information on engine rpm (pins J1 and K1 connector B of M010 respectively). Engine temperature sensor K036 (pins 1and 2) receives a reference earth and supplies a signal proportional to the engine coolant temperature (pins E1 and D1 connector B of M010 respectively). Supply air pressure sensor K082 (pins 1, 2, 3) is connected to pins B2, C4, D4 of connector B of M010. Fuel pressure sensor K083 (pins 1, 2, 3) is connected to pins F1, G1, H1 of connector B of M010. Fuel temperature sensor K081 (pins 1, 2) supplies a signal proportional to temperature (pins D2 and E2 connector B of M010). Throttle adjustment solenoid L036 (pin 2) is connected to pin A4 of connector C of M010. Cylinder reference sensor K170 (pins 1, 2, 3) is connected to pins H2 G2, F2, of connector B of M010. Air flow meter K041 (pins 1, 6, 5) is connected to pins J3, G3, H3 of connector B of M010. The accelerator pedal K055 (pins 1, 2, 3, 4) has two built-in potentiometers (one main one and one safety one) and is connected to pins G3, H3, C2, G2 of connector A of M010. Clutch pedal switch I031 (pin 2) and the safety switch on the brake pedal I035 (pin 2) are connected to pins E3 and E4 (respectively) of connector A of M010. Switch I031 (pin 1) is supplied by body computer node M001 (pin 9 connector B). The "redundant" switch I035 is the "normally closed" type (when the pedal is pressed, the switch contact opens): the system checks the consistency of the "pedal pressed" information in this way. Control unit M010 (pins G1-H2, H4-H3, G4-G3, H1-G2 connector C) controls the opening of injectors N070 (pins 1 and 2). Fuel pressure regulator N077 (pin 1) keeps the fuel pressure in the rail constant and is connected to pin L2 and connector B of M010. EGR solenoid L030 (pin 2) controls exhaust gas recirculation and is connected to pin A3 of connector B di M010. Turbo pressure valve L037 (pin 2) controls the outlet pressure from the turbocharger and is connected to pin B4 of connector C of M010. Intake variable geometry control solenoid L015 (pin 2) regulates the engine air intake ports and is connected to pin B4 of connector B of M010. Injection pump piston third deactivation solenoid L005 (pin 1) is connected to pin A4 of connector B of M010. Control unit M010 is connected (pins A3 and A4 connector A) via the CAN line to body computer node M001 (pins 8 and 10 connector D) to instrument panel E050 (pins 6 and 12) and to warning light and odometer control unit M140 (pins 2 and 5) and engine compartment junction unit B001 (pins 11 and 12 connector F). See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES The autodiagnostic data for the control unit M010 (pin B4 connector A) is read by connecting to connector R010 (pin 7). Control unit M010 (pins F2, H2, F4 connector A) is connected to the air conditioning system: in this way, compressor activation or deactivation is adjustd on the basis of engine speed. See E6021 COMPRESSOR ENGAGEMENT - to pins B2, C4, D4 of connector A, the engine cooling system; See E5020 ENGINE COOLING - to pins K3, F4, E4, H4 of connector B, the cruise control system; See E5060 CRUISE CONTROL
