Description The electronically controlled Cruise Control system makes it possible to drive the vehicle at the desired speed without pressing the accelerator pedal. This makes driving on motorways less tiring, especially on long journies, because the speed memorized is maintained automatically. The device can only be switched on at speeds above 40 km/h or in 4th or 5th gear. The function is managed by the engine control unit. This receives commands from a Cruise Control lever on the left of the steering wheel. The function is engaged by turning the wheel (ON). When a speed is set ( SET + , SET - ), the setting is saved and may be called up at any time ( RCL ). The function is automatically deactivated: by pressing the brake pedal; by pressing the clutch pedal; by turning the wheel to OFF; by switching off the engine; In such cases, the last speed achieved is stored and can be recalled by pressing the RCL button. The system also deactivates at speeds below the minimum permitted speed (about 30 km/h). The Cruise Control lever is incorporated in the steering column switch unit (steering wheel node); the activation, deactivation information, etc. is sent via the CAN to the Body Computer. With the system activated, the milometer warning lights node warning light is lit up. there is a second "redundant" switch located on the brake pedal, used by the engine management control unit, in particular, for the Cruise Control function The "basic" switch (I030) is the "normally open" type (when the pedal is pressed, the switch closes), whilst the "redundant" switch (I035) is the "normally closed" type (when the pedal is pressed, the switch contact opens): the system checks the consistency of the "pedal pressed" information in this way.

Operational Description The Cruise Control function is managed by the engine control unit M010. All the Cruise Control function commands are supplied by the steering wheel node control unit M093 to the Body computer node M001. The signal travels via the CAN which connects the two control units. The steering wheel node control unit M093 receives a supply (pin 5 connector A) through the line protected by fuse F11, located in the body computer node M001; it receives a supply via the CAN (pin 6 connector A) from the line protected by fuse F16, located in the body computer node M001. The commands are sent, from the latter, via the CAN, to the ABS control unit M050 and from there to the engine management control unit M010 (pins E3, E4 connector B). The command from the steering wheel node control unit activates the system and communicates the constant speed to be maintained. The system is disengaged as soon as brake pedal I030 or clutch pedal I031 are pressed. If the accelerator pedal is pressed, the system is disengaged temporarily and reset when the pedal is released. The accelerator pedal K055 has two built-in potentiometers (one main one and one safety one) and is connected to pins G3, C2, G2 and H3 of connector A of M010. Clutch pedal switch I031 and the safety switch on the brake pedal for cruise control I035 supply a signal to indicate engagement has taken place to pins E3 and E4 of connector B of M010. The two switches receive a supply from the ignition-controlled line protected by fuse F18 of the body computer M001. The "redundant" switch I035 is the "normally closed" type (when the pedal is pressed, the switch contact opens): the system checks the consistency of the "pedal pressed" information in this way. The warning light is switched on by the milometer warning lights node M140 which communicates with the instrument panel E050 and the body computer node M001 via the CAN. The instrument panel E050 and the milometer warning lights node M140 receive a supply via the CAN (pin 13 of E50 and pin 4 of M140) through the line protected by fuse F24 of the body computer M001.

The electronically controlled Cruise Control system makes it possible to drive the vehicle at the desired speed without pressing the accelerator pedal. This makes driving on motorways less tiring, especially on long journies, because the speed memorized is maintained automatically. The device can only be switched on at speeds above 40 km/h or in 4th or 5th gear. The speed regulator should only be activated when traffic and route conditions allow a constant speed to be safely maintained for a sufficiently long stretch. The function is managed by the engine control unit. This receives commands from a Cruise Control lever on the left of the steering wheel. The function is engaged by turning the wheel (ON). When a speed is set ( SET + , SET - ), the setting is saved and may be called up at any time ( RCL ). If necessary, the speed setting may be over-ruled by pressing the accelerator pedal (e.g. when overtaking); the system returns to the stored speed when the pedal is released. The function deactivates automatically: - by pressing the brake pedal; - by pressing the clutch pedal; - by turning the wheel to OFF; - by turning off the engine. In such cases, the last speed achieved is stored and can be recalled by pressing the RCL button. The system also deactivates at speeds below the minimum permitted speed (about 30 km/h). The Cruise Control system control lever is incorporated in the steering column switch unit (Steering wheel node): the activation, deactivation, etc. information is sent to the Body Computer via the CAN. With the system activated, the milometer warning lights node warning light is lit up. There is a second "redundant" switch located on the brake pedal, used by the engine management control unit, in particular, for the Cruise Control function. The "basic" switch (I030) is the "normally open" type (when the pedal is pressed, the switch closes), whilst the "redundant" switch (I035) is the "normally closed" type (when the pedal is pressed, the switch contact opens): the system checks the consistency of the "pedal pressed" information in this way.

The Cruise Control function is managed by the engine control unit M010. All cruise control function controls are supplied by steering wheel node control unit M093 (pins 1, 3 connector A) to body computer node M001 (pins 5, 3 connector G respectively) and then from this node (pins 8 and 10 connector D) to engine control unit M010 (pins A3 and A4 connector A). The signal is sent via the CAN network. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES Body computer M001 (pin 11 connector B and pin 1 connector G) supplies steering wheel node control unit M093 (pin 5 connector A and pin 4 connector D respectively) via two lines, of which only the second is protected by fuse F04. The command from the steering wheel node control unit M093 activates the system and communicates the constant speed to be maintained. The system is disengaged as soon as brake pedal I030 or clutch pedal I031 is pressed (on versions with a manual gearbox only); if the accelerator pedal K055 is pressed, the system is disengaged temporarily and reset when the pedal is released. Brake pedal I030 is connected (pin 2) to body computer node M001 (pin 4 connector B) and supplementary fuse box B098 (pin G31 connector B). This latter conection is made via a line protected by fuse F31 located inside the control unit. Accelerator pedal K055 (pins 1, 2, 3, 4) is connected to engine control unit M010 (pin G3, H3, C2, G2 connector A respectively) and is equipped with two built-in potentiometers: a main one and one safety one. Clutch pedal switch I031 is interfaced on one side (pin 2) with engine control unit M010 (pin E3 connector A) and on the other (pin 1) with body computer node M001 (pin 9 connector B). The safety switch on brake pedal I035 is also connected (pin 2) to control unit M010 (pin E4 connector A) and receives power at pin 1. See E5050 DIESEL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT Switches I031 and I035 supply the cruise control activation signal to control unit M010. The "redundant" switch I035 is the "normally closed" type (when the pedal is pressed, the switch contact opens): the system checks the consistency of the "pedal pressed" information in this way. Warning light activation is controlled by odometer warning light node M140, which communicates via CAN line (pins 2 and 5) with instrument panel E050 (pins 6 and 12) and body computer node M001 (pins 8 and 10 connector D). The latter (M001 pin 6 connector D) supplies power to both components E050 (pin 13) and M140 (pin 4).

Description The F.A.P. system (Anti-Particle Filter) is fitted on vehicles equipped with Diesel engines in order to reduce the particles present in the exhaust gases by more than 95%. Particles cannot be eliminated through the use of normal catalyzers, but require the use of special filters known precisely as "anti-particle", which become prematurely unusable, especially if used for town driving. The F.A.P. system allows the automatic regeneration of the anti-particle filter during the operation of the vehicle so that it remains efficient in all operating conditions for around 80,000 km after which the anti-particle filter should be replaced. The FAP system consists of: a silicon carbide anti-particle filter in conjunction with a catalyzer (located upstream of the filter) and sensors for checking the temperature and pressure; an additive system which injects an appropriate amount of cerium oxide based additive into the fuel tank each time it is refilled. A control logic incorporated in the engine management node, operates the artificial regeneration of the filter. There is also a specific control unit ("additive control node") which regulates the injection of additive into the fuel tank; it uses the fuel level, engine speed and vehicle speed signals for the management of this function. On the basis of the signals received, the additive control node: determines the amount of additive to be injected, activates the additive injeciton pump, operates the additive injector. The additive control node also receives a signal from the exhaust gas temperature sensor (downstream of the filter) and sends it to the engine management control unit via the body computer. The additive reservoir is located under the vehicle near the fuel tank; it has a capacity of 5 litres (an amount which allows it to run for about 80,000 km). The additive injection pump, submerged in the tank, has the task of providing the pressure (3 bar) and the flow rate (80 l/h) required for the correct operation of the additive circuit. This sensor is incorporated in the pump assembly and is designed to notify the additive control node that the minimum level has been reached. The additive injector, located on the main reservoir, allows a pre-set amount of additive to be atomized in the fuel tank; it is operated by the additive node and is an electromagnetic type injector similar to the type of injector used in petrol engines. The temperature sensor downstream of the catalyzer, located between the catalyzer and the particle filter, allows the engine management node to monitor the temperature of the exhaust gases downstream of the catalyzer and consequently an increase in temperature caused by catalytic combustion. The differential pressure sensor constantly measures the difference in pressure between the inlet and outlet of the catalytic converter/anti-particle filter assembly. This measurement makes it possible to determine the filter blockage level. The intake air heating circuit is connected to the FAP system: it is a device is designed to increase the temperature of the exhaust gases by increasing the temperature of the intake air, in order to facilitate the regeneration of the particle filter (specific to the FAP device) and is only activated during the filter regeneration phase. The F.A.P. system (Anti-Particle Filter) is fitted on vehicles equipped with Diesel engines in order to reduce the particles present in the exhaust gases by more than 95%. The particulate cannot be eliminated through the use of normal catalytic converters, for this reason special (particle) filters are used which, however, suffer from the following defect: their performance deteriorates rapidly especially if used for town driving. The F.A.P. system allows the automatic regeneration of the particle filter during the operation of the vehicle, keeping it working efficiently in all usage conditions for about 80,0000 [km] after which it should be replaced. The FAP system consists of: The F.A.P. system consists of: - a silicon carbide anti-particle filter in conjunction with a catalyzer (located upstream of the filter) and sensors for checking the temperature and pressure; - an additive system which injects an appropriate amount of cerium oxide based additive into the fuel tank each time it is refilled. The control logic incorporated in the engine management control unit operates the artificial regeneration of the filter. There is a diesel additive control unit that regulates the addition of additive into the fuel tank. The fuel level, engine speed and vehicle speed signals are used to carry out this operation. Depending on the signals received, the above mentioned control unit determines the amount of additive to be injected and activates the additive injection pump. The additive reservoir is located under the vehicle near the fuel tank: it has a capacity of 5 [l]: this quantity lasts for about 80,000 [km]. The additive injection pump, submerged in the tank, has the task of providing the pressure (3 bar) and the flow rate (80 l/h) required for the correct operation of the additive circuit. The diesel additive level sensor has the task of notifying the control unit that the minimum level has been reached. The temperature sensor downstream of the catalyzer (located between the catalyzer and the particle filter) allows the engine management control unit to monitor the increase in the temperature of the exhaust gases due to catalytic combustion. The differential pressure sensor constantly measures the difference in pressure between the inlet and outlet of the catalytic converter/particle filter assembly. This measurement makes it possible to determine the filter blockage level. The intake air heating circuit is connected to the FAP system: it involves a device designed to increase the temperature of the exhaust gases raising the temperature of the intake air. This function is only activated during the filter regeneration stage. See E5050 DIESEL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT

Description An electronic control system supervises and governs all engine parameters to optimise performance and fuel consumption by means of a real-time response to different service conditions. The system is managed by a single control unit which controls both the ignition and the sequential, phased injection. Depending on the signals received from numerous sensors, the control unit controls the injectors connected to it managing the following systems: fuel supply; air supply; accelerator pedal; engine cooling; exhaust with catalytic converters controlled by two lambda sensors; fuel vapour recirculation. The throttle body is also controlled electronically by the control unit: throttle opening is calculated in accordance with specific software mapped inside the engine control unit. This system does away with the need for a mechanical link between accelerator pedal and throttle body. The control unit als controls the air intake pump on the exhaust manifold and the EGR valve; when the engine is cold it also heats the oil vapours and the throttle casing. The electronic management system described above ensures that this engine meets the very latest EOBD (European On Board Diagnogis) system emission control and monitoring requirements. This system allows continous diagnosis of emission-related car components and notifies the driver if any of the components should deteriorate by turning on a warning light in the instrument panel.

Operational Description Engine management control unit M010 controls and governs the entire electronic ignition and injection system. The control unit M010 receives a direct battery supply at pin H4 of connector C, via the line protected by fuse F08 and operated by a relay in the engine compartment control unit B001, energized by a control (earth) signal coming from pin F2 of connector B of the control unit M010. The ignition-operated supply reaches pin C3 of connector A of M010 through the line protected by fuse F04 of B001. The main injection relay for the engine compartment junction unit B001 controls the entire system: t is energized by an earth signal from pin F3 of connector A of control unit M010 and then forwards a power supply to: the fuel pump N040 from pin 11 of connector C, via the line protected by fuse F02; the air intake pump on exhaust manifold N145 from pin 16 of connector C via the line protected by fuse F16 of B001 and governed by the relay housed in the junction unit; the Lambda sensors K017 and K018 from pin 1 connector B, the injectors N070 from pin 10 connector B; the ignition coil A030 and the throttle casing heating resistance O015 from pin 9 connector B; the EGR solenoid valve L030 and the fuel vapour recovery solenoid valve L010 from pin 16 of connector B, all via the line protected by fuse F15 of B001. The ignition-controlled supply is also sent to the oil vapour heating resistance O007 from pin 2 connector B via the line protected by fuse F01 of B001. The control unit M010 is earthed from pin H1 of connector C, M4 of connector B, G4 and H4 of connector A. Control unit M010 receives signals from the various sensors in order to control all engine service parameters. The rpm sensor K046 provides engine rpm information via a frequency signal sent to pins B1 and B2 of connector C of control unit M010: these two signals are very low intensity and are thus appropriately shielded. The engine temperature sensor K036 receives a reference earth and provides a signal proportional to the temperature of the engine coolant to pins E4 and D4 of connector B of control unit M010. The cylinder reference sensor K170 receives a supply from the control unit M010, pin C3 of connector, a reference earth from pin A3 of connector B and sends a frequency signal to pin F3 of connector B of the control unit. The air temperature sensor K042 receives a reference earth from pin A3 of connector B of M010 and sends a signal to pin A2 of connector B of the control unit. The absolute pressure sensor K082 receives a supply from the control unit M010 (pin C3 of connector C), it receives a reference earth from pin C1 of connector C and sends a signal to pin C2 of connector C of the control unit. The detonation sensor K050 provides information, by means of frequency signals, concerning the onset of detonation in the combustion chamber: it sends two signals to pins B3 and C3 of connector B of M010. The Lambda sensor upstream of the catalyzer K017 and the one downstream K018 provide the control unit M010 with information concerning the correct composition of the air/fuel mixture. Sensor K017 is connected to pins A3 and B3 of connector C of M010: these two signals are very low intensity and are thus appropriately shielded. Sensor K017 is heated by a resistance to ensure it works efficiently even when cold. the resistance is supplied by the main relay. Pin E2 of connector B of M010 provides the reference earth. Sensor K018 is connected to pins D3 and E3 of connector B of M010: these two signals are very low intensity and are thus appropriately shielded. Sensor K018 is heated by a resistance to ensure it works efficiently even when cold: the resistance is supplied by the main relay. Pin D2 of connector B of M010 provides the reference earth. The accelerator pedal K055 has two built-in potentiometers (one main one and one safety one) and is connected to pins G3, C2, G2 and H3 of connector A of M010. The steering pressure sensor K058 is connected to the control unit M010 at pin G1 connector B. Clutch pedal switch I031 and the safety switch on the brake pedal for cruise control I035 supply a signal to indicate engagement has taken place to pins E3 and E4 of connector B of M010. The two switches receive a supply from the ignition-controlled line protected by fuse F18 of the body computer M001. The "redundant" switch I035 is the "normally closed" type (when the pedal is pressed, the switch contact opens): the system checks the consistency of the "pedal pressed" information in this way. The control unit M010 controls the opening of the injectors N070 by means of special signals sent from pins H2, G3, G2, G3 of connector C of M010. The injectors N70 receive a power supply to enable opening from the main relay. The control unit M010 also controls the coil A030 through the control signals for the coil main winding, pins L3 and M3 of connector B of M010, whilst the secondary coil winding sends the impulse to the plugs. The primary windings of coils A030 receive a supply to enable the opening of main relay . Throttle body actuator N075 is equipped with two integral potentiometers connected in parallel: this controls throttle opening by means of a stepping motor. The motor receives a supply from pins M1 and L1 of connector B of M010. Pin C1 of connector B sends power to both potentiometers, while pin B1 sends an earth signal; pins B4 and A1 of the same connector receive signals that reach throttle body actuator N075. Fuel vapour recovery solenoid L010 allows fuel vapours to flow through toward the engine intake, where they join the mixture that is entering the combustion chamber. Valve L010, supplied by the main relay, is opened by the control unit when the engine is operating in load conditions by means of a signal from pin F2 of connector C of M010. The EGR solenoid valve L030 receives a supply from pin E1 connector C of M010 and receives a reference earth from pin A2 connector C and is connected to the control unit at pin D1 connector C and G4 connector B. The control unit M010 is then connected via the CAN, pins A3 and A4 connector A , to the Body Computer M001 and to the other network nodes. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES The autodiagnostic data for the control unit M010 is read by connecting to connector R010 - pin 7: it receives signals from pin B4 connector A of M010 via the special diagnostic line. The control unit M010 is connected to the air conditioning system through pins F2, H2 and F4 of connector A. This allows the engine idle speed to be adjusted as the load conditions increase each time the compressor is switched on or to switch it off in the case of high engine speed or load conditions. See E6021 COMPRESSOR ENGAGEMENT The control unit also controls the engine cooling system: pins B2, D4 and C4 of connector A control the engagement of the fan. See E5020 ENGINE COOLING

The "redundant" switch I035 is the "normally closed" type (when the pedal is pressed, the switch contact opens): the system checks the consistency of the "pedal pressed" information in this way. The control unit M010 controls the opening of the injectors N070 by means of special signals sent from pins K2, K4, J4, K3, J3 and K1 of connector C of M010. The injectors N70 receive a power supply to enable opening from the main relay. The control unit M010 also controls the coils A030 through the control signals for the coil main winding, pins H2, H4, H3, G4, G3 and G2 of connector B of M010, whilst the secondary coil winding sends the impulse to the plugs. The primary windings of coils A030 receive a supply to enable the opening of main relay . The steering pressure sensor K058 is connected to the control unit M010 at pin E3 connector A. Throttle body actuator N075 is equipped with two integral potentiometers connected in parallel: this controls throttle opening by means of a stepping motor. The motor receives a supply from pins B4 and C3 of connector B of M010. Pin L4 of connector B sends power to both potentiometers, while pin C4 sends an earth signal; pins B3 and M3 of the same connector receive signals that reach throttle body actuator N075. Fuel vapour recovery solenoid L010 allows fuel vapours to flow through toward the engine intake, where they join the mixture that is entering the combustion chamber. Valve L010, supplied by the main relay, is opened by the control unit when the engine is operating in load conditions by means of a signal from pin F4 of connector B of M010. The variable geometry solenoid valve L015 regulates the geometry of the intake chamber; it is supplied by the main relay and opened by the control unit by means of a signal from pin F1 of connector B of M010. The phase transformer actuator N076 receives a supply from the main relay and is regulated by the control unit by means of a signal from pin G1 of connector B of M010. The control unit M010 is then connected via the CAN, pins H3 and H4 connector A , to the Body Computer M001 and to the other network nodes. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES The autodiagnostic data for the control unit M010 is read by connecting to connector R010 - pin 7: it receives signals from pin H2 connector A of M010 via the special diagnostic line. The control unit M010 is connected to the air conditioning system through pins A3, D4 and E4 of connector A. This allows the engine idle speed to be adjusted as the load conditions increase each time the compressor is switched on or to switch it off in the case of high engine speed or load conditions. See E6021 COMPRESSOR ENGAGEMENT The control unit also controls the engine cooling system: pins F2, J4 and K4 of connector A control the engagement of the fans. See E5020 ENGINE COOLING

Description The vehicle is equipped with a climate control system for managing the temperature, air flow rate, distribution and recirculation. The control unit manages the operation of the system by controlling: air temperature at the vents; air distribution at the vents; fan speed (continuous variation); compressor engagement (air refrigeration circuit); air recirculation engagement. The system controls are located on the outside of the container which houses the control unit: the following parameters/functions can be controlled manually: fan speed; distribution arrangement; compressor enablement; defrosting/demisting: recirculation.

Operational Description Climate control unit M070 receives a supply direct from the battery at pin 11, connector A from body computer node M001, pin 7 connector D from the line protected by fuse F12 and managed by a specific relay, contained inside the control unit. It receives an ingition-operated power supply at pin 12 connector A, from the body computer node M001, from pin 6 connector F, from a line protected by fuse F18. Pin 16 of connector A is earthed Control unit M070 communicates from pins 8, 14, 15 via the CAN with the body computer node M001 at pins 6, 8, 10 connector D and with instrument panel E050 at pins 23, 17, 13 (for more details. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES Passenger compartment air fan N085 is controlled by selector unit H081. The unit contains an internal control unit that controls passenger compartment speeds according to the speed set on the appropriate selector. The relay J035 supplies the selector unit H081, at pin B connector A, on the go ahead of the body computer node M001, from pin 40 connector M, providing a direct battery supply at the selector H091, via the line protected by fuse MF08 for the engine compartment junction unit B001 (pin 8 connector G). The selector H081, connector B, is then operated by the control unit M070, from pin 2 of connector B, according to the strategy for implementing the management of the internal ventilation. Pins 6, 5, and 4 connector B of electronic control unit M070 supply the electric motors for recirculation N082, mixing N081, distribution N080 at pins 1. Pins 3, 4, 5, 6 connector C of control unit M070 receive the anglar opening position of the internal air intake flaps. Control unit M070 also communicates certain information (heated rear windscreen on, air conditioning on) from pins 1, 2, 3 to the instrument panel E050 to pins 5, 9 and 2 and from there to the various displays [EL4010]. The diesel version signal reaches pin 10 of the instrument panel E050 from pin 18 connector A of M070.

Description The vehicle is equipped with an automatically operated climate control system for managing the temperature, air flow rate, distribution and recirculation which is available in two versions: automatic system known as dual zone, with left/right different temperatures for the first and second rows of seats; automatic system known as multi zone with additional rear fans which can be operated from the second row to alter the air flow rate to the front vents in the second and third rows. The control unit manages the operation of the system by controlling: air temperature at the vents; air distribution at the vents; fan speed (continuous variation); compressor engagement (air refrigeration circuit); air recirculation engagement; the MAX-DEF rapid defrosting function (which consists of a collection of measures which make it possible to demist both the windscreen and the rearscreen quickly); The control unit sets the above parameters so that temperature of the passenger compartment is adjusted to the desired temperature. The system controls are located on the outside of the container which houses the control unit. The following parameters/functions can be altered manually: fan speed; distribution arrangement; compressor disabling; defrosting/demisting: recirculation. The control unit acquires information on the temperature and climate conditions both inside and outside the vehicle by means of special sensors: outside temperature sensor, located on the passenger door mirror: the sensor value is acquired by the controls on the door and is suitably "filtered"; it is then sent, via the CAN, to the climate control system control unit; lower mixed air temperature sensor; upper mixed air sensor; inside temperature sensors; solar sensor, which measures the sun rays on the windscreen; According to the calculations made, it sets the passenger compartment air intake speed through the fan motor and the temperature by means of two mixture actuators (one for the right side of the passenger compartment and one for the left side); it also sets the distributions of the flows through another actuator and, lastly, another actuator is responsible for the inside/outside air recirculation function.

Description The special button on the climate control system in the centre of the dashboard switches on the air cooling and dehumidification circuit, activating the air conditioning compressor. The above button enables operation of the air cooling circuit, but actual compressor activation is also dependent upon activation of: the frost thermostat sensor, located near the evaporator, which stops the engagement of the air conditioning if the temperature of the evaporator is too low; the fan linear sensor, located on the coolant circuit that locks air conditioner activation if coolant pressure is too low or high; the engine control unit that excludes compressor operation in accordance with engine management mode; e.g. in the case of high engine temperatures or high engine load (sudden acceleration). Operational Description The compressor activation control is given by pressing the key housed on the climate control unit M070. The request is forwarded via CAN from pins 8, 14 connector A of control unit M070 to body computer node M001 at pins 8, 10 connector D. The control unit M070 communicates compressor engagement information to the instrument panel E050 at pins 2 and from there to the various displays. See E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL The diesel version signal is sent to pin 10 of the instrument panel E050. The command is also sent, from the body computer M001, pin 2, 4 connector M, via the CAN, to the engine management control unit M010, to pins A3, A4 connector A. Engine control unit M010 determines compressor activation or deactivation according to data supplied by linear sensor K120 connected at pins F2, H2 and F4 connector B. Compressor L020 is engaged by body computer node M001 from pin 7 connector B via junction unit B001 from pin 13 connector C at pin 7 connector B. The frost sensor K086 is connected to pins 17 and 18 of connector M from the body computer node M001, informing whether the evaporator temperature is too low; the information reaches the control unit M070 from M001 via the CAN.

Description To increase protection against theft attempts, an engine immobilizer system known as the CODE is used. Each time the ignition key is turned to position S, the CODE system deactivates the engine management electronic control unit functions. Each time the key is turned to position M, the CODE system sends the engine management control unit a recognition code to deactivate the immobilizing function. The keys are equipped with an electronic Transponder device that sends a coded signal to a special control unit (incorporated in the Body Computer): if it recognizes the code sent, it allows the engine to be started. The code used in the dialogue, that takes place via an aerial coaxial to the ignition switch, varies each time the engine is started (rolling code): therefore the code cannot be reproduced even using electronic scanners. The main function of the Code control unit is to recognize the key inserted in the ignition switch: it contains the secret code used in the dialogue with the key transponder. All the codes for the enabled keys and the code used in the dialogue with the engine management control unit are contained in the unit: when the key is turned to the ON position for the first time, if the key is correctly recognized, this code is transferred to the engine management control unit which remains indelibly linked to the Code unit and therefore to the Body Computer. The dialogue between the two units takes place via the two-way serial line. The function also includes the display of the status by means of the CODE warning light in the instrument panel, connected via the CAN, coming on. The special button on the climate control system in the centre of the dashboard switches on the air cooling and dehumidification circuit, activating the air conditioning compressor. The above button enables operation of the air cooling circuit, but actual compressor activation is also dependent upon activation of: the frost thermostat sensor, located near the evaporator, which stops the engagement of the air conditioning if the temperature of the evaporator is too low; the fan linear sensor, located on the coolant circuit that locks air conditioner activation if coolant pressure is too low or high; the engine control unit that excludes compressor operation in accordance with engine management mode; e.g. in the case of high engine temperatures or high engine load (sudden acceleration).

The compressor activation control is given by pressing the key housed on the climate control unit M070. Control unit M070 (pin 10 connector A) receives power via a line protected by fuse F14 leaving body computer node M001 (pin 6 connector D) and communicates via the CAN line (pins 14 and 15 connector A) with instrument panel E050 (pins 6 and 12) and with body computer node M001 (pins 8 and 10 connector D). See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES Body computer M001, again via the CAN line, forwards the command to engine control unit M010 (pins A3 and A4 connector A), enables or disables compressor activation (pins F2, H2 and F4 connector A) from linear sensor K120 (pin 1, 2 and 3). Compressor L020 is supplied (pins 1 and 2) from engine compartment junction unit B001 (pins 1 and 5 connector C), which is connected in turn (pins 12 and 11 connector F) via the CAN line to body computer node M001 (pins 25 and 27 connector C). Demister sensor K086 is also connected (pins 1 and 2) to body computer node M001) (pins 17 and 16 connector E respectively): the signal contains information on the evaporator temperature, which is also sent to control unit M070.

Description The vehicle climate control system is insufficient via the heater unit when the engine is cold, especially for diesel engines which take longer to warm up. On these versions there is also an additional heating system which is activated when the engine is first running, depending on the temperature of the engine coolant. The system consists of an additional heating device, located inside the heater unit: this device contains three resistances (PTC). The operation of the resistances is controlled by a specific control unit, connected to the engine management control unit, which operates either just one, or two or three, thereby providing gradual heating. This control logic depends on: the temperature of the engine coolant; the electrical power level available (the battery voltage is controlled); the engine speed (which should be above a preset value).

Operational Description On the de-luxe version that includes ABS/ESP, the additional heater electronic control unit M075 receives a supply, at pin 3, from the maxi fuse box B005, via the line protected by fuse MF3. On the basic version, on the other hand, the control unit M075 receives a power supply from the engine compartment junction unit B001, via the line protected by maxifuse MF3. On the basic version, on the other hand, the control unit M075 receives a power supply from the engine compartment junction unit B001, via the line protected by maxifuse MF3. The control unit is earthed at pin 4. Information on engine coolant temperature and engine speed is supplied by engine management control unit M010 from pin C1 connector A, to pin 2 of M075. The engine management control unit M010 receives this information from the engine coolant temperature sensor K036 and from the rpm sensor K046 connected to it at pins D1, E1 and J1, K1, respectively of connector B. On the basis of these data, additional heater control unit M075 activates/deactivates system operation according to commands set by the user. The control unit M075 has an autodiagnostic function. The control unit autodiagnostic data can be read by connecting to connector R010, pin 7: it receives signals from pin 1 of M075 via the special diagnostic line.

Description The vehicle is equipped with an electronic alarm with perimeter (exterior) and volumetric (interior) protection. The alarm is switched on/off using the remote control incorporated in the key. It has 4 buttons: one for activating the central locking < R1 > and for switching the alarm on See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING one for activating the release of the central locking < R1 > and switching off the alarm. See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING On versions with electrically operated sliding doors, the remote control has other buttons: one for opening/closing the right sliding side door (Wiring Diagram ) E3095 SLIDING SIDE DOORS one for opening/closing the left sliding side door (Wiring Diagram ) E3095 SLIDING SIDE DOORS A dedicated control unit monitors the following: the state of the doors and lids, via switches in the catches (perimeter control) the presence of a moving object inside the passenger compartment, by means of volumetric sensors. (volumetric control); the condition of the system supply leads; operation of the ignition switch. The control unit is equipped with a self-diagnostic function which detects and memorises faults and problems in the control unit and system components; in addition, it checks the condition of the connecting cables and saves the number of activations and times the alarm has been operated. The control unit operating logic can be modified in order to satisfy the legal requirements which govern the use of alarm systems in the various markets. All the outside components are connected by means of a dedicated serial line. The alarm siren is located at the front, on the left of the engine compartment. The deterrent LED is located on the right side of the dashboard: with the alarm on the LED flashes at 0.8 Hz to indicate that the vehicle is locked. The door lock system switches are used to monitor the doors and boot. A special separate switch detects bonnet closure. The volumetric sensors check that there are no intrustions in the vehicle. They are located in the front courtesy light: they consist of a transmitter and a receiver: the wave transmitted by one transmitter must reach the receiver of the other sensor and viceversa: otherwise an alarm signal is sent to the control unit. the volumetric function can be switched off, using the special button (which can be reached with the driver's door open); an LED located in the dashboard lights up constantly. In this case, when the anti-theft device is switched on, there is perimeter (external) protection only. Description The vehicle is fitted with an ABS braking system which prevents the wheels from locking during braking, makes the best possible use of the grip conditions available and keeps the vehicle as easy as possible to control during emergency braking. The ABS is an additional section of the basic braking system; it is disabled if there is a problem, with the braking system working the same way as for a vehicle without ABS. The advantage of ABS over conventional systems is that it makes it possible to maintain maximum manoeuvrability even when braking hard in poor grip conditions, preventing the wheels from locking. The system is completed by the EBD system (Electronic Brake Distributor) which distributes the brake force by means of the ABS sensors and control unit. The "ABS failure" warning light and the "minimum brake fluid level" warning light coming on simultaneously with the engine running means that there is a problem with the EBD system; in this case, the wheels could lock during sharp braking. The "ABS failure" warning light coming on by itself with the engine running usually means that there is a problem with the ABS only. In this case, the braking system will work properly, just without the anti-lock function. The operation of the EBD system may also be affected under these circumstances. If the "minimum brake fluid level" warning light only comes on, this means that the hydraulic system fluid level is too low. On this version, the system is only available in the basic configuration. The vehicle is equipped with an electronic alarm with perimeter (exterior) and volumetric (interior) protection. The alarm is switched on/off using the remote control incorporated in the key. The remote control incorporated in the key has 4 buttons: - one for activating the central locking (locking) command, switching on the alarm and the location function; - one for activating the release of the central locking and switching off the alarm. - one for opening/closing the right sliding side door; - one for opening/closing the left sliding side door. See E3095 SLIDING SIDE DOORS A dedicated control unit monitors the following: - the state of the doors and lids, via switches in the catches (perimeter control) - the presence of a moving object inside the passenger compartment, by means of volume-sensing sensor (volumetric control) - the condition of the system supply leads; - operation of the ignition switch. The control unit is equipped with an autodiagnostic function which detects and memorizes faults and problems in the actual control and the system components; in addition, it checks the condition of the connecting cables and memorizes the number of activations and times the alarm has been operated. The control unit operating logic can be modified in order to satisfy the legal requirements which govern the use of alarm systems in the various markets. All the outside components are connected by means of a dedicated serial line. The alarm siren is located at the front, on the left of the engine compartment. The deterrent LED is located on the right side of the dashboard: with the alarm on the LED flashes at 0.8 [Hz] to indicate that the vehicle is locked (dissuasion function). The door lock system switches are used to monitor the doors and boot. A special separate switch detects bonnet closure. The volumetric sensors check that there are no intrustions in the vehicle. Located in the front courtesy light, they consist of a transmitter and a receiver: the wave transmitted by one transmitter must reach the receiver of the other sensor and viceversa: otherwise an alarm signal is sent to the control unit. The volume-sensing function may be deactivated by pressing a special button that is accessible only with the driver's door open: a led on the instrument panel comes on with a fixed light. In this case, when the anti-theft device is switched on, there is perimeter (external) protection only.

Alarm control unit M030 is supplied (pins 4 and 7 of connector A) from body computer M001 (pins 2 and 1 connector C respectively) which which it communicates (pins 10 and 12 connector A) via the CAN line (pins 4 and 6 connector C respectively). The siren is activated even if it is not supplied with power via an internal buffer battery. Alarm system activation is indicated by activation of the turn signals (pin 11 connector B, pins 3, 5 connector G of M001). See E2020 DIRECTION INDICATORS / HAZARD WARNING LIGHTS

Description The vehicle is fitted with an ABS braking system which prevents the wheels from locking during braking, makes the best possible use of the grip conditions available and keeps the vehicle as easy as possible to control during emergency braking. The ABS is an additional section of the basic braking system; it is disabled if there is a problem, with the braking system working the same way as for a vehicle without ABS. The advantage of ABS over conventional systems is that it makes it possible to maintain maximum manoeuvrability even when braking hard in poor grip conditions, preventing the wheels from locking. The system is completed by the EBD system (Electronic Brake Distributor) which distributes the brake force by means of the ABS sensors and control unit. The "ABS failure" warning light and the "minimum brake fluid level" warning light coming on simultaneously with the engine running means that there is a problem with the EBD system; in this case, the wheels could lock during sharp braking. The "ABS failure" warning light coming on by itself with the engine running usually means that there is a problem with the ABS only. In this case, the braking system will work properly, just without the anti-lock function. The operation of the EBD system may also be affected under these circumstances. If the "minimum brake fluid level" warning light only comes on, this means that the hydraulic system fluid level is too low. On this version, the system also includes the ESP function ESP (Electronic Stability Program) is an electronic system that controls the stability of the vehicle, intervening on the engine torque and introducing differentiated braking for the wheels in the case of a loss of grip restoring the vehicle to the correct path. Whilst driving the vehicle is subject to lateral and longitudinal forces which can be controlled by the driver as long as the tyres hold the road sufficiently well; when this is no longer the case, the vehicle starts to drift from the desired path. Especially when driving on uneve road surfaces (such as cobblestones or where there is water, ice or soil), changes in speed (during acceleration or braking) and/or trajectory (bends or the need to avoid obstacles) can cause a loss in grip for the tyres. When the sensors detect conditions that could lead to the vehicle slipping, the ESP system intervenes on the engine and the brakes producing a stabilizing torque. The ESP system switches on automatically each time the engine is started up; it can be switched off and switched back on again manually by pressing the button on the left side of the dashboard. The basic ESP system components are: the control unit the angular sensor detecting the position of the steering; four sensors which detect the rotation speed of each wheel (ABS sensors); the braking system pressure sensor; the slewing sensor which detects the rotation of the vehicle around the vertical axis; the sensor which detects lateral acceleration (centrifugal force). Depending on the version, the system also includes other auxiliary functions: TC (Traction Control) and ASR (Anti Slip Regulation) incorporated in the ESP system, control the vehicle traction and intervene automatically each time either one or both of the drive wheels are slipping, respectively. Depending on the slipping conditions, two different control systems can be activated: if the slipping involves both drive wheels, caused by the excessive force transmitted, the ASR function intervenes, reducing the power transmitted by the engine; if the slipping only involves one of the drive wheels, the TC function intervenes, automatically braking the wheel that is slipping, with a similar effect to that of a self-locking (limited-slip) differential. The MBA (Mechanic Brake Assistance) and HBA (Hydraulic Brake Assistance) functions are systems that provide an automatic increase in the braking pressure in emergency braking conditions. In effect, in critical situations, when the driver operates the brake pedal decisively, the system intervenes on the braking circuit, increasing braking pressure to ensure that the vehicle stops as quickly as possbile. The two systems behave in the same way, the only difference being that the pressure increase setting in one case is regulated by the ABS - ESP system control unit and in the other case in a mechanical fashion. The MSR function (Motor Schleppmoment Regelung) completes the system. This function automatically regulates the engine braking torque whilst changing down; if there is a sudden gear change down, it intervenes, supplying torque to the engine to prevent excessive drive at the drive wheels which, especially in poor grip conditions, could lead to a loss in stability of the vehicle. Description The vehicle is equipped with an electronically controlled safety system which, in the case of a frontal impact of a certain severity, activates the front seat belt pretensioners and the front Air Bags protecting the driver and the passenger. In the case of a fairly serious side impact, the side Air Bags (Side Bags) and the corresponding front Window Bags (only on the side where the impact took place) are activated. An electronic control unit manages the entire system controlling all the components and activating the retention systems (pretensioners and Air Bags), when necessary. The control unit is located under the centre console and is securely fastened to the bodyshell: in this way the deceleration sensors located inside the unit are near the centre of gravity and detect the deceleration for the entire vehicle accurately. An accelerometric sensor on the pillar of both front doors transmits a signal to the control unit in the case of a side impact. When, according to the control logic, the two sensors detect a slight frontal impact, the control unit sends signals for the intervention of the front modules in the first stage and both the front and rear pretensioners. If a more serious frontal impact is detected, the control unit sends signals for the intervention of the front modules in the second stage. In the case of a fairly serious side impact, the front and rear side Air Bags (Side Bags) and the corresponding Head Bag (only on the side where the impact took place) are activated. There are two stages for the front Air Bag modules: the first intervenes at an intial impact level, the second in the case of a more serious impact. The two stages are produced by means of two separate charges which "fill" the bag 60% (first stage) and 40% (second stage). The driver side air bag module is located in the middle of the steering wheel. It is fitted on a tilting plate that is also used to control the horns. The plate houses a metal container that contains the folded bag and the gas generation device that inflates the bag. A clock spring allows the connecting cables for the Air Bag module to follow the rotation of the steering wheel without danger of breaking. The passenger Air Bag module is located in the dashboard, above the glove compartment and is fastened directly to the vehicle crossmember through a special bracket. The passenger air bag may be deactivated manually by means of a special switch which can be operated using the key: it is located at the edge of the dashboard and is only accessible with the door open. With the key OFF the control unit also controls activation of a special "passenger air bag disabled" warning light. The Side Bags are housed in the outer part of the front seats The Head Bag consists of a bag that inflates positioning itself between the head of the passengers and the side windows. The folded Head Bag is located under the ceiling lining, whilst the rear pillar houses the gas generator. The pretensioners are incorporated in the reels of both the front and rear seat belts. The control unit is equipped with an autodiagnostic function: it detects and stores faults; it recognises the various components and the fault type; it indicates the onset of faults by means of warning lights The activation of the system following a particularly serious impact is memorized by the control unit. when operations are carried out to the Air Bag system, the following safety recommendations must be closely followed. The MBA (Mechanic Brake Assistance) and HBA (Hydraulic Brake Assistance) functions are systems that provide an automatic increase in the braking pressure in emergency braking conditions. In effect, in critical situations, when the driver operates the brake pedal decisively, the system intervenes on the braking circuit, increasing braking pressure to ensure that the vehicle stops as quickly as possbile. The two systems behave in the same way, the only difference being that the pressure increase setting in one case is regulated by the ABS - ESP system control unit and in the other case in a mechanical fashion. The MSR function (Motor Schleppmoment Regelung) completes the system. This function automatically regulates the engine braking torque whilst changing down; if there is a sudden gear change down, it intervenes, supplying torque to the engine to prevent excessive drive at the drive wheels which, especially in poor grip conditions, could lead to a loss in stability of the vehicle.

The ESP function is managed by ABS/ESP control unit M050. Control unit M050 is supplied at connector A from engine compartment control unit B001: - at pin 2, by a line protected by fuse MF2 from pin 2 of connector D; - at pin 28, by a line protected by fuse F07 from pin 3 of connector F; Control unit M050 communicates via the CAN line (pins 25 and 45, 14 and 25 connector A) with the body computer node M001) (pins 2 and 4, 25 and 27 connector E, pins 8 and 10 connector D), with engine control unit M010 (pins A3 and A4 connector A), with steering wheel node control unit M093 (pins 1 and 2), with yaw control unit M091 (pins 2 and 3), with instrument panel E050 (pins 6 and 12), with warning light and odometer control unit M140 (pins 2 and 5) and with engine compartment control unit B001 (pins 11 and 12 connector F). Control unit M050 (pins 26-5, 9-10, 6-27, 8-29 connector A respectively) controls the speed of each wheel via left front wheel sensor K070 (pin 1 and 2), right front wheel sensor K071 (pins 1 and 2), left rear wheel sensor K075 (pins 1 and 2) and right rear wheel sensor K076 (pins 1 and 2). Pin 33 of connector A of control unit M050 is connected to pin 14 of door lock control unit M080. See E3095 SLIDING SIDE DOORS The yaw sensor is built into control unit M050, which activates the stability control system when a vehicle stability situation is detected (understeer or oversteer). Left brake wear sensor K020 and right brake wear sensor K021 (pin 1 connector A) send an earth signal to control unit M050 (pin 31 connector A). Brake fluid level signal sensor K02 (pin 1) is connected to M050 (pin 17 connector A), which sends signals (via the CAN line) to control units E050 and M140. Instrument panel E050 (pin 13) and warning light and odometer control unit M140 (pin 4) are supplied by body computer node M001 (pin 6 connector D) via a line protected by fuse F14. The ESP system may be cut out by pressing switch I115: - the power (pin 4) is supplied by body computer node M001 (pin 7 connector D). - the cut-out signal (pin ) reaches instrument panel E050 (pin 4). There is a second "redundant" switch on the brake pedal used, in particular, by the engine management control unit and the ABS control unit. The "basic" switch (I030) is the "normally open" type (when the pedal is pressed, the switch closes), whilst the "redundant" switch (I035) is the "normally closed" type (when the pedal is pressed, the switch contact opens): the system checks the consistency of the "pedal pressed" information in this way. The brake pedal pressed signal reaches brake pedal switch I030: - pin 1 is connected via a line protected by fuse F31 to pin G31 of connector G of supplementary fuse box B098; - pin 2 is connected to pin 4 of connector B of body computer node M001 and with pin 30 of connector A of control unitM050. Pin 1 of redundant switch I035 is connected to pin 20 of connector F of engine compartment junction unit B001 via a line protected by fuse F06, while pin 2 is connected to pin E4 of connector A of control unitM010. Pin 2 of clutch pedal switch I031 is connected to pin E3 of connector A of control unit M010 and pin 1 is connected to pin 9 of connector B of M001. Body computer M001 is connected via the latter pin also to pin 4 of M091. Lastly, pin 1 of connector G of M001 is connected to pin 4 of connector D of M093. Control unit M050 (pin 11 connector A) is equipped with a self-diagnostic function: The control unit autodiagnostic data can be read by connecting to connector R010 (pin 12).

Operational Description Control unit M060 receives ignition-operated power at pin 47 from body computer node M001 from pin 14 connector F. The control unit M060 communicates, via the CAN, from pins 30, 33, with the body computer node M001, pin 30, 28 connector L; it receives a supply, via the CAN (pin 37), from the line protected by fuse F16, located in the body computer node M001. Pin 34 is connected to the dedicated earth C050. When, according to the control logic, a front impact is detected, the control unit sends signals for the intervention of the front modules and the pretensioners. Driver side air bag module Q009 is connected to steering wheel node M093 that is connected to control unit M060 at pins 1, 2, 20, 21 from pins 1 and 2 of connector B and C. The steering wheel node M093 communicates, via the CAN, with the body computer node, at pins 38, 40 connector L. In addition, node M093 receives a supply (pin 5 connector A) from the line protected by fuse F11, located in the body computer node M001; it also receives a supply via the CAN (pin 6 connector A) from the line protected by fuse F16, located in the body computer node M001. The Air Bag is connected to the dashboard on the driver's side Q011 at pins 3, 4, 18, 19. The air bag module on the passenger side facia Q011 is disabled by switch H075 connected to the control unit at pins 49, 50. The control unit M060 is connected to front and rear driver side pretensioners Q020 and Q022 via pins 13, 14. The control unit is connected to front and rear passenger pretensioners Q021 and Q023 from pins 22, 23. The side impact detection sensors K066 (driver's side) and K067 (passenger side) send signals to pins 1209 and 5-8 of the control unit M060, respectively. When, according to the control logic, a side impact is detected, the control unit sends signals for the intervention of the side modules. Pins 6,7 are connected to the side Air Bag Q031 and to the passenger side Window Bag Q041; pins 11, 10 are connected to the side Air Bag Q030 and to the driver's Window Bag Q040. Switches I046 and I047 inform body computer node M001 that the front seat belts are properly fastened at pins 37, 39 connector L. The lighting up of the three Air Bag warning lights (Air Bag failure, passenger Air Bag disabled and seat belt not fastened) is managed by the milometer warning lights node M140 which communicates with the instrument panel E050 and the body computer node M001, via the CAN. The instrument panel E050 and the milometer warning lights node M140 receive a supply via the CAN (pin 13 of E50 and pin 4 of M140) through the line protected by fuse F24 of the body computer M001.

Description The electronic automatic transmission has four forward speeds plus reverse with self-adapting management (i.e. it is capable of adapting to the driving style of the driver) depending on vehicle load and road conditions. The display can show the following: in automatic driving mode, the gear selected (P, R, N or D); in sequential driving mode, the (manual) engagement of a higher or lower gear by means of an up or down arrow, respectively. In sequential driving mode, each gear change is shown on the display; any possibility of errors is excluded by the continuous check by the management control unit which only allows a lower gear to be engaged if the engine revs permit. In sequential driving mode, the electronic automatic transmission works like a fixed ratio gearbox controlled in sequence. The electronic control intervenes by altering the ratios when the engine speed goes above or below the permitted rpm limit. Moving the lever from P to D, N to D or R to D should only be done with the vehicle stationary, the engine idling and the brake pedal fully depressed (shift-lock). The engine cannot be started with the lever in position R. The engine can only be started with the lever in P or N The lever can only be moved from position P, with the ignition in position M, with the brake pedal fully depressed (shift-lock). A failure with the electronic automatic transmission is signalled by the flashing of the milometer warning lights node; in this case, the gearbox stabilizes itself automatically in third gear. driving where there is snow or ice: when the road holding conditions are poor (snow, ice, etc.) and the special button next to the gear lever is pressed, the display will light up and the vehicle will pull away in second gear. The vehicle is equipped with an electronically controlled safety system which, in the case of a frontal impact of a certain severity, activates the front seat belt pretensioners and the front Air Bags protecting the driver and the passenger. In the case of a fairly serious side impact, the side Air Bags (Side Bags) and the corresponding front Window Bags (only on the side where the impact took place) are activated. An electronic control unit manages the entire system controlling all the components and activating the retention systems (pretensioners and Air Bags), when necessary. The control unit is located under the centre console and is securely fastened to the bodyshell: in this way the deceleration sensors located inside the unit are near the centre of gravity and detect the deceleration for the entire vehicle accurately. An accelerometric sensor on the pillar of both front doors transmits a signal to the control unit in the case of a side impact. When, according to the control logic, the two sensors detect a slight frontal impact, the control unit sends signals for the intervention of the front modules in the first stage and both the front and rear pretensioners. If a more serious frontal impact is detected, the control unit sends signals for the intervention of the front modules in the second stage. In the case of a fairly serious side impact, the front and rear side Air Bags (Side Bags) and the corresponding Head Bag (only on the side where the impact took place) are activated. There are two stages for the front Air Bag modules: the first intervenes at an intial impact level, the second in the case of a more serious impact. The two stages are produced by means of two separate charges which "fill" the bag 60% (first stage) and 40% (second stage). The Air Bag module is fitted in the centre of the steering wheel. it is fitted on a rocker plate that allows the horn to be operated. The plate houses a metal container that contains the folded bag and the gas generation device that inflates the bag. A clock spring allows the connecting cables for the Air Bag module to follow the rotation of the steering wheel without danger of breaking. The passenger Air Bag module is located in the dashboard, above the glove compartment and is fastened directly to the vehicle crossmember through a special bracket. The passenger air bag may be deactivated manually by means of a special switch which can be operated using the key: it is located at the edge of the dashboard and is only accessible with the door open. With the key OFF the control unit also controls activation of a special "passenger air bag disabled" warning light. The Side Bags are housed in the outer part of the front seats. The Head Bag consists of a bag that inflates positioning itself between the head of the passengers and the side windows. The folded Head Bag is located under the ceiling lining, whilst the rear pillar houses the gas generator. The pretensioners are incorporated in the reels of both the front and rear seat belts. The control unit is equipped with an autodiagnostic function: it detects and stores faults; it recognises the various components and the fault type; it indicates the onset of faults by means of the special warning light. The activation of the system following a particularly serious impact is memorized by the control unit. When operations are carried out to the Air Bag system, the following safety recommendations must be closely followed. For more details, Op. 5580C AIR BAG SYSTEM

Air Bag control unit M060 receives power from two lines (pins 47 and 37) from body computer node M001 (pins 5 and 11 connector F respectively), of which only one (the first) is ignition-operated. Body computer node M001 communicates with the various control units via the CAN line, in particular: - from pins 23 and 21 of connector L, with Air Bag control unit M060 (pins 30 and 33 respectively); - from pins 3 and 5 of connector G, with steering wheel node control unit M093 (pins 3 and 1 respectively); - from pins 8 and 10 of connector D, with instrument panel E050 (pins 6 and 12) and warning light and odometer control unit M140 (pins 2 and 5). Control units E050 (pin 13) and M140 (pin 4) receive power from body computer node M001 (pin 6 connector D) with one line protected by fuse F14. Control unit M093 receives power (pin 5 connector A and pin 4 connector D) from body computer node M001 (pin 11 connector B and pin 1 connector G respectively) via two lines, of which only the second is protected by fuse F04. Driver side airbag Q009 is connected to connector F of steering wheel node M093, which is in turn (pins 1-2 connectors B and C) is connected to airbag control unit M060 (pins 2-1, 20-21). Switches I046 and I047 (pin 2) inform body computer node M001 (pins 37 and 39 connector L respectively) that the front seat belts are properly fastened. Passenger side airbag Q011 (pins 1, 2, 3, 4 connector A) is connected to control unit M060 (pin 18, 19, 3, 4 respectively) and may be deactivated by means of switch H075 (pins 3 and 6) also connected to the same control unit (pins 49 and 50 respectively). Control unit M060 is also connected: - from pin 7 to pin 1 of connector A of passenger sidebag Q031; - from pin 6 to pin 2 of passenger head bag Q041; - from pin 11 to pin 2 of driver side head bag Q040; - from pin 10 to pin 2 of driver side bag Q030; - from pin 13 to pin 1 of driver side front belt pretensioner Q020; - from pin 14 to pin 2 of driver side rear belt pretensioner Q022; - from pin 23 to pin 2 of passenger side rear belt pretensioner Q023; - from pin 22 to pin 1 of passenger side front belt pretensioner Q021; - from pins 12 and 9 to pins 1 and 2 (respectively) of the sensor for driver side air bag K066; - from pins 5 and 8 to pins 1 and 2 (respectively) of the sensor for passenger side air bag K067;

Operational Description Automatic transmission control unit M055 controls and regulates the entire electronic gearbox management system (CAE). A direct battery power suppy is supplied by body computer node M001 (pin 11 connector B) from a line protected by fuse F23, located inside the control unit, at pin 56 of control unit M055. An ignition-operated power supply is supplied by engine bay control unit B001 (pin 4 connector C) from a line protected by fuse F04, located inside the control unit, at pin 27 of control unit M055. Pin 28 of M055 is earthed. The information is sent, via the CAN, from control unit M055 (from pins 29, 30) to the engine management control units involved M010 and ABS/ESP M050. Relays J006 (pin 1A) and J007 (1B, 3B) receive an ignition-controlled supply from the line protected by fuse F04, located in junction unit B001. The other end of the coil for J006 is connected to the solenoid valve unit L050 at pin A5. When the ignition switch is turned to osition M, the supply reaches pin 3A of relay J006 from pin 3 connector A of H001. The solenoid valve unit L050 only allows starting in certain conditions (e.g. if the brake pedal is pressed). A negative signal from the solenoid valve unit L050 energizes the coil for relay J006: in this way a supply arrives from the line for pin A5 of J006 energizing the starter motor A020 See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING The starting command is only supplied when the control unit M055 receives the "brake pedal pressed" signal at pin 43 coming from switch I030 and when there is no "brake pedal released" signal at pin 16 coming from switch I035. The brake pedal pressed signal comes from the brake pedal switch I030, connected to the body computer node M001 at pin 2 of connector B and is supplied directly by the ignition switch H001. Switch I035 receives a supply from the ignition-controlled line protected by fuse F18 of the body computer M001. there is a second "redundant" switch on the brake pedal: the "basic" switch (I030) is the "normally open" type (when the pedal is pressed, the switch closes), whilst the "redundant" switch (I035) is the "normally closed" type (when the pedal is pressed, the switch contact opens): the system checks the consistency of the "pedal pressed" information in this way. Relay J007 supplies the automatic transmission lever lock solenoid L058 when electronic control unit M055 excites the relay coil via a negative signal from pin 11. The internal contact of the relay closes and the ignition-operated power supply received at pin 3B is sent on to electromagnet L058 from pin 5B. The KEY LOCK signal (engine immobilizing if the gearbox is not in P or N) is sent by control unit M055, from pin 3 to the body computer node M001, pin 36 of connector M. The solenoid valve unit L050 receives an ignition-controlled supply at pin A1 of the engine compartment junction unit B001 (pin 10 connector C) from the line protected by fuse F04, located in the junction unit; pin A4 is earthed. The reverse gear engaged signal is sent from pin A2 to the body computer node M001 (pin 5 connector B) which controls the switching on of the reversing lights See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS All the other pins are connected to the automatic transmission control unit M055; control unit M055 communicates directly through numerous signals with the solenoid valve unit L050 which contains the control valves, pressure regulators and some sensors. The management of the gearbox can be fully automatic (i.e. managed completely by control unit M055) or semi-automatic, in other words setting the gears through the gear lever, switch unit H037 connector B; the latter receives a supply from the body computer node M001 (pin 6 connector F) from the line protected by fuse F18 located in the junction unit. The control unit is informed, from unit H037 connector B, of the automatic or manual management, at pins 36 and 37 of M055. The engagement of the "snow" function by pressing the special button in unit H037 connector A, is communicated to the body computer M001, at pin 16 connector L and from there to the control unit M055, via the CAN. The LED to show that the function is on is supplied by the line protected by fuse F12 located in the body computer. Control unit M055 sends the required information, via the CAN, to instrument panel E050 and odometer warning light node M140 for the management of the warning lights and the gears engaged display. The control unit autodiagnostic data can be read by connecting to the diagnostic socket. The automatic transmission control unit M055 is connected, via the K line, from pin 18 to the diagnostic socket R010, pin 7; it is also connected through diagnostic line L, from pin 17 of M055 to pin 15 of R010 See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR

Description A loss in tyre inflation pressure can result in serious problems: Burst tyre A considerable deterioration in the vehicle's road holding and braking stability. Irregular, rapid wear of the tyres. Increased fuel consumption. The insufficient pressure notification system is designed to satisfy this need to constantly check the four wheels of the vehicle. The information is displayed both via the NSO (milomter warning lights node) by the STOP warning light coming on and via the multifunction screen node in the form of a message in the display. The system consists of: four pressure sensors inside the wheels transmitting a code via radiofrequency (R.F.) and allowing the pressure to be measured one R.F. signal reception and management control unit located inside the steering column switch unit The reception control unit also analyzes the correct operation of each sensor following no response from the sensor (malfunction or batteries run down) or if new sensors are being programmed. The sensors are designed to prevent possible false alarms caused by differences in pressure due to climatic and environmental conditions during the normal use of the vehicle. the wheel control system does not check the spare wheel, does not deal with over inflation and does not allow which wheel(s) has(have) the problem to be precisely identified.
