The electronic automatic transmission has four forward speeds plus reverse with self-adapting management (i.e. it is capable of adapting to the driving style of the driver) depending on vehicle load and road conditions. The display can show the following: in automatic driving mode, the gear selected (P, R, N or D); in sequential driving mode, the (manual) engagement of a higher or lower gear by means of an up or down arrow, respectively. In sequential driving mode, each gear change is shown on the display; any possibility of errors is excluded by the continuous check by the management control unit which only allows a lower gear to be engaged if the engine revs permit. In sequential driving mode, the electronic automatic transmission works like a fixed ratio gearbox controlled in sequence. The electronic control intervenes by altering the ratios when the engine speed goes above or below the permitted rpm limit. Moving the lever from P to D, N to D or R to D should only be done with the vehicle stationary, the engine idling and the brake pedal fully depressed (shift-lock). The engine cannot be started with the lever in position R. The engine can only be started with the lever in P or N. The lever can only be moved from position P, with the ignition in position M, with the brake pedal fully depressed (shift-lock). A failure with the electronic automatic transmission is signalled by the flashing of the milometer warning lights node; in this case, the gearbox stabilizes itself automatically in third gear. Driving where there is snow or ice: when the road holding conditions are poor (snow, ice, etc.) and the special button next to the gear lever is pressed, the display will light up and the vehicle will pull away in second gear.

Automatic transmission control unit M055 controls and regulates the entire gearbox management system. The power supply for the automatic transmission control unit M055 (pin 56) is provided by the Body computer node M001 (pin 11 connector B) and (pin 27) from the engine compartment junction unit B001 (pin 4 connector F) through a line protected by fuse F06. This latter line, also supplies the gear control unit H037 (pin 1 connector B) and the automatic transmission solenoid valve assembly L050 (pin A1). The information is sent via the CAN line from control unit M055 (pins 29-30 for the basic version and pins 29-30, 38-29 for the version with ESP) to the Body computer node M011 (pins 8, 10 connector D), to the engine compartment junction unit B001 (pins 11, 12 connector F), to the instrument panel E050 (pins 6, 12), to the milometer and warning lights control unit M140 (pins 2, 5) and to the other control units involved: engine management M010 and ABS/ESP M050. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES The Body computer node M001 (pins 1, 2 connector A) receives a power supply from the engine compartment junction unit B001 (pins 4, 5 connector D respectively) through two lines protected by fuses MF4 and MF5 (respectively) and provides a power supply (pin 6 connector D) for the instrument panel E050 (pin 13) and the milometer and warning lights control unit M140 (pin 4) through a line protected by fuse F14. The ignition switch H001 is connected (pins 2, 1, 3 respectively) to the body computer M001 (pin 5 connector D, pins 4 and 6 connector G). The gear lever lock actuator relay feed J007 (pins 1B, 5B) receives a power supply from the Body computer node M001 (pin 10 connector B). This same actuator J007 (pins 2B, 3B respectively) is still connected to the automatic transmission control unit M055 (pin 11) and to the automatic transmission lever lock solenoid L058 (pin 1). The solenoid valve unit L050 only allows starting in certain conditions (e.g. if the brake pedal is pressed). The brake pedal switch I030 is connected: - at pin 1, to the additional fuse box B098 (pin G31 connector B) from which it receives a power signal via a line protected by fuse F31; - at pin 2, to the Body computer node M001 (pin 4 connector B) and to the automatic transmission control unit M055 (pin 43). The KEY LOCK signal (locking of starting if the gearbox is in a position other than P or N), is supplied by the automatic transmission solenoid valve assembly L050 (pin A5) to junction unit B001 (pin 15 connector F). Once the brake pedal pressed and gearbox in position P or N signal is received, the junction unit B001 commands starting (pins 2, 3 connector C). See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING The automatic transmission control unit M055 (pins 15, 31, 32, 33, 42, 53, 54, 14, 13, 8, 7, 1, 9, 10, 20, 19, 26, 25, 55, 24, 46, 45, 12, 2) communicates with the solenoid valve assembly L050 (pins A3, A10, A11, A12, A7, B4, B1, B2, B5, B7, B10, B3, B8, B11, B9, B6, B12, C3, C2, C1, D2, D1, E2, E1) by means of numuerous signals: the latter contains the control valves, the pressure regulators and several sensors. The management of the transmission may be completely automatic (managed by M055) or semi-automatic, in other words setting the gears by means of the gear control unit H037: pins 4 and 5 of connector B are connected to pins 37 and 36 (respectively) of the automatic transmission control unit M055 informing it of the management to be carried out. The engagement of the "snow" function takes place by pressing the special button located in unit H037 (pin 1 connector A) connected to the Body computer node M001 (pin 5 connector I). The Body computer node M001 notifies control unit M055 (via the CAN line) that the function has been switched on and supplies (pin 7 connector D) the LED in the gear control unit H037 (pin 2 connector A). The autodiagnosis of the control unit M055 (pin 18) can be carried out by connecting to the diagnostic socket R010 (pin 7). See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR

Operational Description The tyre monitoring system is managed by sensor K171 that communicates data to steering wheel node M093 via a radiofrequency signal. The tyre control information is sent by the steering wheel node control unit M093 to the body computer node M001. The signal travels via the CAN which connects the two control units. The steering wheel node control unit M093 receives a supply (pin 5 connector A) through the line protected by fuse F11, located in the body computer node M001; it receives a supply via the CAN (pin 6 connector A) from the line protected by fuse F16, located in the body computer node M001. The STOP warning light is switched on by the milometer warning lights node M140 which communicates with the instrument panel E050 and the body computer node M001 via the CAN. The instrument panel E050 and the milometer warning lights node M140 receive a supply via the CAN (pin 13 of E50 and pin 4 of M140) through the line protected by fuse F24 of the body computer M001.

Description The car is fitted with numerous electronic control units that perform a self-diagnostic function. When a diagnostic tester (Examiner or other device) is connected to these control units, self-diagnosis data can be read (parameters, errors) or the available active diagnostic tests can be carried out. All the diagnostic lines flow into the EOBD connector (European On Board Diagnosis) which conforms with Directive 98/69/CE (EURO 3) - ISO standard J1962 in the Body Computer connector G. Nodes connected to the network are diagnosed via the CAN network, while the dynamic car control network is diagnosed by a specific K lines. The following are monitored via individual diagnostic K lines: engine management control unit; automatic transmission control unit; ABS control unit; additional heater control unit (JTD only); headlamps control unit (versions with gas discharge headlamps) All the other control units and CAN nodes are connected to the diagnostic socket through the body computer: For more details See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES Component code Description Reference to the assembly C015 Driver's dashboard earth - C020 Passenger dashboard earth - D020 Dashboard/rear coupling - E050 Instrument panel 5560B K171 Tyre inflation pressure sensor 4450B M001 Body computer 5505A M093 Steering wheel node control unit (NVO) 5550A M140 Warning lights and milometer control unit (NSO) -

A loss in tyre pressure can cause: - a blow out; - a considerable deterioration in the vehicle's road holding and braking stability; - irregular, rapid wear of the tyres. - increased fuel consumption. The tyre pressure monitoring system is designed to avoid these problems. The information is displayed both via the milometer warning lights node, by the STOP warning light coming on and via the multifunction screen node in the form of a message in the display. The system consists of: - four pressure sensors on the wheel rims transmitting a code via radiofrequency (R.F.) and allowing the pressure to be measured; - an R.F. signal reception and management control unit located inside the steering column switch unit. The control unit is capable of analyzing the correct operation of each sensor following a lack of response or if new sensors are being programmed. The sensors are designed to prevent possible false alarms caused by differences in pressure due to climatic and environmental conditions.

The tyre pressure monitoring system is managed by control unit M047. The aerials involved in receiving the signals for the right front wheel (pins 1 and 2), the left front wheel (pins 1 and 2) and the rear wheels (pin 1) are connected to the control unit M047 (pins 12-15, 13-14, 10-11 respectively). Control unit M047 (pin 7) receives a power supply from the Body computer node M001 (pin 2 connector F) through a line protected by fuse F09 and communicates (pins 9 and 18), via the CAN line, with M001 (pins 8 and 10 connector D), with the instrument panel E050 (pins 6 and 12) and with the milometer warning lights control unit M140 (pins 2 and 5). The control units M050 (pin 4) and M140 (pin 13) receive a power supply from the Body computer node M001 (pin 6 connector D) via a line protected by fuse F14.
